(أُولئِكَ لَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ وَلَهُمْ سُوءُ الدَّارِ): (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate) is (لهم اللعنة) — the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded. The clause (أولئك لهم اللعنة) is the khabar of (الذين), and (لهم سوء الدار) is conjoined to (لهم اللعنة).
(اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ): (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يبسط الرزق) the khabar; (لمن) is attached to (يبسط); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila; and (يقدر) is conjoined to (يشاء) [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is that (يقدر) is conjoined to (يبسط)].
(وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause (فرحوا) is resumptive, brought to show the ugliness of their deeds despite the provision and ample blessings He poured on them. (بالحياة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (فرحوا), and (الدنيا) is an adjective of (الحياة).
(وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتاعٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is negative; (الحياة) is the mubtadaʾ and (الدنيا) an adjective; (في الآخرة) is a ḥāl, with a muḍāf omitted, that is, "beside the Hereafter". This «في» is for comparison (al-muqāyasa): it is the one that comes between a preceding inferior thing and a following superior thing. The implied form is "and the life of this world, being beside the Hereafter, is…". It is not permissible for «في» to be locative, because the life of this world is not in the Hereafter. (إلا) is the particle of restriction and (متاع) the khabar.
(وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction, so that the link between their saying and the misguidance they were in runs in sequence.
(يقول الذين) is an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (لولا) is a particle of urging equivalent to (هلا); (أنزل) is a past verb, passive; (عليه) is attached to (أنزل), and the pronoun refers to the Prophet Muhammad, upon him be peace; (آية) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (من ربه) is a naʿt (adjective).
(قُلْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنابَ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يضل) is its predicate; (من) is the direct object and the clause (يشاء) the ṣila; (يهدي) is conjoined to (يضل); (إليه) is attached to (يهدي); (من) is the direct object and the clause (أناب) the ṣila.
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أَلا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ): (الذين) is a badal (substitute), and the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; or (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الذين آمنوا) [in the next verse]; the first is preferable. In (تطمئن) the speech turned from the past to the imperfect to convey renewal; further discussion of it will come in the section on rhetoric. (قلوبهم) is the agent of (تطمئن); (بذكر الله) is attached to (تطمئن); and (القلوب) is the agent. [Translator's note: the source does not parse (ألا), the particle of opening and alerting.]
(الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ طُوبى لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ, or the khabar of the first (الذين). The clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila, and (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the ṣila. (طوبى) is a mubtadaʾ and (لهم) the khabar; beginning with it is permitted because of the sense of supplication in it. It was also said that (طوبى) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the lām in (لهم) being for clarification, as in «سقيا لك» and «رعيا لك»; or it is the object of an omitted verb, that is, "you have attained goodly good". (وحسن مآب) was read in the accusative and the nominative. You may parse it [Translator's note: the antecedent of "it" appears to be (طوبى)] as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), as we stated before, on the reading of those who put (حسن) in the accusative, because the case vowel appears on it; but the first is preferable, because the majority read the nominative. Abū al-Baqāʾ made an error regarding it, since he permitted parsing it as an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), and I do not know what his justification is. (حسن) is conjoined to (طوبى), and (مآب) is the muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «الذين آمنوا وتطمئن قلوبهم» there is a lofty rhetorical art which has been mentioned before; we now repeat what relates to this verse. He turned away from conjoining a past verb to a past verb and did not say «واطمأنت قلوبهم», for one of the secrets that is subtle except to those who know the secrets of this noble language. Namely, among the properties of the imperfect verb is that no specific time, present or future — the two times the imperfect can bear — may be considered in it, so that it indicates nothing but mere continuity. Of this is this verse: that is, the believers' hearts find rest constantly, however much trials follow one another, calamities succeed each other and surprises occur — as if they had prepared for every trial a patience and for every calamity a fresh rest. Reflect on this observation, for it is the pillar of the beauty and its secret.

dervis-irab:30-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَيْأَسِ): al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of «أفلم ييأس» is 'did they not know?'. It was said: it is the dialect of a tribe of al-Nakhaʿ. It was also said: despair (al-yaʾs) was used in the sense of knowledge only because one who despairs of a thing knows that it will not be, just as hope (al-rajāʾ) was used in the sense of fear, and forgetting in the sense of leaving." Suḥaym ibn Wathīl al-Riyāḥī said:
أقول لهم بالشعب إذ ييسرونني ... ألم تيئسوا أني ابن فارس زهدم
(I say to them in the mountain pass, as they are dividing me up [as spoil]: do you not know that I am the son of the rider of Zahdam?)
In al-Mukhtār: "Al-yaʾs is despondency; yaʾisa min al-shayʾ, of the pattern fahima. There is another dialect form: yaʾisa yayʾisu, with kasra in both, which is irregular. Yaʾisa is also in the sense of ʿalima (he knew) in the dialect of al-Nakhaʿ, and from it are His words: «أفلم ييئس الذين آمنوا»."
(قارِعَةٌ): a calamity that strikes them with all sorts of affliction. In al-Mukhtār: "qaraʿa al-bāb (he knocked at the door), of the pattern qaṭaʿa; and al-qāriʿa is a severe one of the hardships of fate, that is, the calamity."

* I'rab:
(كَذلِكَ أَرْسَلْناكَ فِي أُمَّةٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِها أُمَمٌ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, like its counterparts, that is, "like that sending We have sent you, a sending of importance"; its counterparts have preceded many times. (أرسلناك) is a verb, an agent and a direct object; (في أمة) is attached to (أرسلناك); the clause (قد خلت) is an adjective of (أمم) [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is evidently an adjective of (أمة)]; (من قبلها) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was [originally] an adjective of (أمم); and (أمم) is the fāʿil (agent).
(لِتَتْلُوَا عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ): (لتتلو): the lām is for cause, and (تتلو) is an imperfect in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of cause; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تتلو) [Translator's note: so in the source; the interpreted maṣdar with the lām is attached to (أرسلناك)], and the agent is "you". (عليهم) is attached to (تتلو); (الذي) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (أوحينا إليك) is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِالرَّحْمنِ): the wāw is circumstantial, that is, while the state of these people is that they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يكفرون). There is nothing to prevent making it resumptive, as some said.
(قُلْ هُوَ رَبِّي لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): (هو ربي) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (لا إله إلا هو): the discussion of it has preceded in detail in al-Baqara, so refresh your memory of it.
(عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ مَتابِ): (عليه) is attached to (توكلت); (إليه) is a fronted predicate and (متاب) a postponed subject.
(وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتى): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to answer those who asked the Messenger of Allah to move the mountains away from Mecca by his Quran so that it might become spacious for them, and to raise their fathers for them to bear witness to his prophethood. (لو) is conditional; (أن) is a particle resembling the verb; (قرآنا) is its noun; the clause (سيرت) is the predicate of (أن); (به) is attached to (سيرت); and (الجبال) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (أو) is a conjunction, and (قطعت به الأرض) is conjoined, as is (أو كلم به الموتى). The apodosis of (لو) is omitted, as you say to someone you threaten, "If I were to get up and come at you…", leaving out the apodosis. The meaning is: "And if there were a Quran by which the mountains were moved from their places, or the earth were cut by it so that it split, came apart and crumbled, or the dead were spoken to by it so that they heard and answered, they would not believe." Abū Ḥayyān supplied it [Translator's note: the source prints «وقدرة» for «وقدّره»] as: "it would be this Quran, because it is the utmost in reminding and the furthest limit in warning and causing fear". Further discussion of this omission will come in the section on rhetoric.
(بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً): (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb); (لله) is a fronted predicate and (الأمر) a postponed subject; and (جميعا) is a ḥāl. It is a conjunction for digressing from the sense of negation contained in (لو), that is, rather Allah is able to bring what they proposed in obstinacy.
(أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ لَهَدَى النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً): the hamza is for interrogation and affirmation (taqrīr); (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; (ييئس) is an imperfect in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم); (الذين) is the agent and the clause (آمنوا) the ṣila. (أن) is lightened from the heavy [anna], because the sense of knowledge precedes it, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). (لو) is a conditional particle; (يشاء) is an imperfect verb and (الله) its agent; the lām is connective; the clause (هدى الناس) is the apodosis [of (لو)] and has no grammatical position [Translator's note: the source prints «جواب لولا محل لها», evidently for «جواب لو لا محل لها»]; (جميعا) is a ḥāl; and the conditional clause with its apodosis is the predicate of (أن).
(وَلا يَزالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا تُصِيبُهُمْ بِما صَنَعُوا قارِعَةٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا يزال) is a defective imperfect verb; (الذين) is its noun and the clause (كفروا) the ṣila; the clause (تصيبهم) is the predicate of (لا تزال) [Translator's note: so in the source, with tāʾ]; (بما صنعوا) is attached to (تصيبهم), that is, because of their doing, so the bāʾ is causal and (ما) maṣdariyya; and (قارعة) is the agent of (تصيبهم).
(أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيباً مِنْ دارِهِمْ): (أو) is a conjunction; (تحل) is conjoined to (تصيبهم), and the agent is "it", that is, the calamity; (قريبا) is an adverb of place, that is, a place near their home; and (من دارهم) is attached to (قريبا) — so that its sparks fly upon them and its woes toss them about. It was also said that the agent of (تحل) refers to the one addressed, namely the Messenger ﷺ, that is, "or you alight with your army near their home", as he alighted at al-Ḥudaybiya, and then the conquest of Mecca came. The first is more evident and preferable.
(حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعادَ): (حتى) is a particle of limit and genitive; (يأتي) is an imperfect in the accusative by an implied an after (حتى); (وعد الله) is the agent, and what is meant by His promise is the decreed victory. (إن) and its noun; the clause (لا يخلف) is its predicate; and (الميعاد) is the direct object.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال» to the end of the verse there is a wondrous concision (ījāz), for the apodosis has been omitted, as preceded. The parsers and exegetes differed about how to supply it. We supplied it in the i'rab as "they would not believe". Al-Zamakhsharī chose this supply but made it the less preferred, and supplied the preferred one with his words "it would be this Quran", because it is the utmost in reminding and the furthest limit in warning. This is an acceptable supply, though the first is closer to the context of the discourse and more emphatic in establishing the meaning. Omission of the apodosis of «لو» is common in their speech. Among its examples in poetry is the saying of Abū Tammām in his ode rhyming in bāʾ in which he praised al-Muʿtaṣim on his conquest of Amorium:
لو يعلم الكفر كم من أعصر كنت ... له المنية بين السّمر والقضب
(If unbelief knew for how many ages death lay waiting for it between the tawny spears and the swords…) [Translator's note: the source prints «كنت» for «كمنت» ("lay hidden").]
For the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being "it would have made its preparations and readied its equipment for the matter", or "it would not have ventured on the audacity it ventured on", as indicated by the story of the Hāshimite woman whom one of the barbarians took captive and who cried out, "O Muʿtaṣim!".
The wording of Ibn Hishām: "«ولو أن قرآنا سيرت به الجبال», the verse, that is, they would not believe in it, by the evidence of «وهم يكفرون بالرحمن». The grammarians supply: 'it would be this Quran', and what I have supplied is more evident."
That is, because of the evidence mentioned. But against it is that what they supplied is also indicated by His words: «لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن على جبل لرأيته خاشعا متصدعا من خشية الله», so it is not shown that his supply is more evident than theirs. And know that each of the two aspects, and the evidence for each, was mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī; so the author [Ibn Hishām] did not supply anything in which he was alone apart from others, contrary to what is suggested by his words "and what I have supplied is more evident". [Translator's note: this paragraph appears to be quoted from a commentator on the Mughnī, though the source does not name him.]
Furthermore, al-Bāqillānī applied to this verse the term "the art of allusion" (al-ishāra), and defined it as "a small amount of wording containing many meanings". Someone said, in describing eloquence: "an indicative glance", and this is exactly the definition of concision.

dervis-irab:32-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَأَمْلَيْتُ): al-imlāʾ is that one is left for a long period of time in ease and security. In al-Qāmūs and its commentary: "Allah granted someone respite (amlā imlāʾan), lengthened his life: He lengthened it and let him enjoy it; and Allah amlā the wrongdoer, and amlā lahu: He gave him respite." He said: "Al-imlāʾ is a maṣdar, [meaning] respite and deferral, and what is dictated of sayings. Al-malī is a long stretch of time; one says 'I waited for him malīyan', that is, a long time; and a malī of the night passed, which is from its beginning to its third; it was also said that it is an undefined portion of it."
(أَشَقُّ): harder than it; an elative (ism tafḍīl) from shaqqa yashuqqu, of the pattern naṣara, mashaqqatan; and «شقّ الأمر»: the matter was severe and difficult.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): the wāw is a conjunction, so that the speech runs in sequence and as a prelude to consoling the Prophet ﷺ. The lām paves the way for an oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (قد) is a particle of realization; (استهزئ) is a past verb, passive; (برسل) stands in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (من قبلك) is a naʿt (adjective) of (رسل).
(فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كانَ عِقابِ): the fāʾ is for conjunction; (أمليت) is a verb and its agent; (للذين) is attached to (أمليت); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (ثم) is a conjunction; and (أخذتهم) is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (فكيف): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted predicate of (كان); (كان) is a defective past verb and (عقابي) its noun, the yāʾ being dropped out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil).
(أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قائِمٌ عَلى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ): the hamza is for the interrogation of denial, and its answer is omitted, its implied form being "No", as will come. The fāʾ conjoins to something omitted, whose supply has preceded. (من) is a relative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject); (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ; (قائم) is the khabar (predicate) of the second mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (على كل) is attached to (قائم). The bāʾ is a preposition in the sense of (مع), and (ما) is a relative noun in the genitive by the bāʾ, or maṣdariyya, and together with what it enters on is in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). The khabar of (من) is omitted, its implied form being "like one who is not so, of their partners which neither harm nor benefit"; it is indicated by His words afterwards: «وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ». The answer to the interrogation is «لا» (No), as we supplied it.
(وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to indicate the omitted khabar of (من), as preceded; this is the best of the views about it. Abū al-Baqāʾ made it conjunctive and others made it circumstantial. (جعلوا) is a verb and its agent; (لله) is attached to an omitted second object, or to an omitted ḥāl; and (شركاء) is the first object of (جعلوا), if (جعل) is in the sense of (صيّر).
(قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِما لا يَعْلَمُ فِي الْأَرْضِ): (سموهم) is an imperative verb expressing [the addressees'] incapacity (taʿjīz); it is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (أم) is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa). (تنبئونه) is an imperfect verb from which the interrogative hamza has been dropped, the implied form being «أتنبئونه»; it is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (بما) is attached to (تنبئونه); the clause (لا يعلم) is the ṣila, and the object of (يعلم) is omitted, that is, "knows it"; and (في الأرض) is a ḥāl. What is meant is the negation that He has partners — as will come in the section on rhetoric — for otherwise His knowledge would encompass them.
(أَمْ بِظاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ): (أم) is also the disconnected one, in the sense of (بل); (بظاهر) is attached to (تنبئونه), that is, without reality or regard for meaning; and (من القول) is an adjective of (ظاهر).
(بَلْ زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مَكْرُهُمْ): (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; (زين) is a past verb, passive; (للذين) is attached to (زين); (كفروا) is the ṣila; and (مكرهم) is the deputy agent.
(وَصُدُّوا عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ هادٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (صدوا) is a verb and its agent; (عن السبيل) is attached to (صدوا). (ومن): the wāw is resumptive and (من) is conditional, in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of (يضلل); (يضلل) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and (الله) its agent. (فما): the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative; (له) is its fronted predicate; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (هاد) is the noun of (ما) in position, genitive by (من) [Translator's note: the source has «بما», evidently for «بمن»] in form.
(لَهُمْ عَذابٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): (لهم) is a fronted predicate and (عذاب) a postponed subject; (في الحياة) is an adjective of (عذاب), and (الدنيا) an adjective of (الحياة).
(وَلَعَذابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَشَقُّ وَما لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ واقٍ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; the lām is that of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (الآخرة) is the muḍāf ilayhi; and (أشق) is the predicate of (عذاب). (وما لهم من الله من واق): its i'rab has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
The noble verse — His words «أفمن هو قائم على كل نفس بما كسبت …» to the end of the verse — contains numerous rhetorical arts, because it came in the context of arguing against them over their associating partners with Allah. We list them below:
1- The interrogation of denial in His words «أفمن», and the omission of its predicate as an explicit [statement] of rebuke and contempt for them, against the corrupt analogy, given the absence of any common aspect joining the two. This is what the scholars of rhetoric call "suppression on condition of explanation" (al-iḍmār ʿalā sharīṭat al-tafsīr): it is that something is omitted at the beginning of the speech which is brought at its end, so that the latter is evidence for the former. It is of three kinds:
a- That it comes by way of interrogation, the first clause being mentioned without the second, as in the verse we are dealing with, and also as in His words: «أفمن شرح الله صدره للاسلام فهو على نور من ربه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أولئك في ضلال مبين». The implied form of the verse is: "Is the one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like one whose heart He has hardened?", and the omitted part is indicated by His words «فويل للقاسية قلوبهم».
b- That it comes in the form of negation and affirmation, as in His words «لا يستوي منكم من أنفق من قبل الفتح وقاتل أولئك أعظم درجة من الذين أنفقوا من بعد وقاتلوا», its implied form being: "Not equal among you are the one who spent before the conquest and fought and the one who spent after it and fought."
c- That it comes in some other way than these two, being neither interrogation nor negation and affirmation, as in the saying of Abū Tammām:
يتجنب الآثام ثم يخافها ... فكأنما حسناته آثام
(He avoids sins and then fears them, as if his good deeds were sins.)
In the first hemistich there is a suppression explained in the second hemistich. Its implied sense is that he avoids sins, and so he has done a good deed, then he fears that good deed, so it is as if his good deeds were sins. The verse, moreover, is taken subtly from His words: «والذين يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة».
2- Putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, to draw attention to the fact that they set up partners for One who is single and alone, with whom no one shares in His name; that is in His words «وجعلوا لله شركاء».
3- Challenging to incapacity (al-taʿjīz) in His words «قل سموهم», that is, specify their names and say "So-and-so and so-and-so". It is a denial of their existence in a demonstrative way, as you say: "If what you claim exists, then name it", because what is meant by the name here is the proper name.
4- Negating a thing by affirming it, or reversal of the apparent — the discussion of this art has preceded, and it is among the extremities of the science of eloquence — and it is in His words «أم تنبئونه بما لا يعلم». The reality of this negation is that they are not partners, and that Allah does not know them as such because they are not, in fact, such; and even if they have established entities which Allah knows, they are created things under lordship, not worshipped gods. But the negation coming in this recited manner is wondrous, its eloquence and expression hardly to be fathomed. Among its delightful instances is the saying of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib describing the assembly of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «its slips are not spread abroad (lā tuthnā faltātuhu)», that is, its lapses are not broadcast. The outward sense of this wording is that there were slips there but they were not spread; but that is not what is meant; rather what is meant is that there were no slips there to be spread.
5- Drawing on (al-istidrāj) [Translator's note: the source prints «الاستدارج»] in His words «أم بظاهر من القول», to urge them to reflection rather than to speech devoid of thought, as in His words elsewhere: «ذلك قولهم بأفواههم» and «ما تعبدون من دونه إلا أسماء سميتموها». This mode of argument is among the most wondrous and strongest of styles.
6- Gradation in each of the digressions, with the disconnected (أم) and with «بل», in the cleanest [Translator's note: the source prints «أنطف», evidently for «أنظف»] manner.

dervis-irab:35-37.t:
* I'rab:
(مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ أُكُلُها دائِمٌ وَظِلُّها تِلْكَ عُقْبَى الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا) مثل الجنة is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted according to the school of Sībawayh, i.e., "in what we have narrated to you is the likeness of the Garden", meaning its description, which is a likeness in its strangeness. Excerpts from Sībawayh's words on a construction of this kind have already been given. Al-Zajjāj said: its meaning is "the likeness of the Garden is a garden beneath which rivers flow", with the described noun omitted, as an illustration of what is hidden from us by what we can observe. والتي is an adjective of الجنة. وعد is a passive past verb, and المتقون is its deputy agent. The clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an explanation of the omitted element according to the view of Sībawayh; according to him it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise the clause أكلها دائم: أكلها is a mubtadaʾ and دائم its khabar. وظلها is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e., "(is) lasting". وتلك is a mubtadaʾ, and عقبى is the khabar; والذين is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive), and the clause اتقوا is its ṣila (relative clause). (وَعُقْبَى الْكافِرِينَ النَّارُ) عقبى is a mubtadaʾ and النار the khabar, or the reverse, to match the first, and perhaps that is better. (وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ) والذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause آتيناهم is the ṣila; الكتاب is the second direct object of آتيناهم; the clause يفرحون is the khabar of الذين; بما is attached to يفرحون; and the clause أنزل إليك is the ṣila. The secret of the rejoicing is its agreement with what they already have.
(وَمِنَ الْأَحْزابِ مَنْ يُنْكِرُ بَعْضَهُ) The wāw is a conjunction; ومن الأحزاب is a fronted khabar and من a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause ينكر is a ṣila; and بعضه is a direct object. The document of the peace treaty on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya will come in the section of Benefits. (قُلْ إِنَّما أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ) إنما is a particle that restrains and is restrained (kāffa and makfūfa); أمرت is a passive past verb and the tāʾ is the deputy agent; أن and what is within its scope are accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e., "to worship Allah" (بأن أعبد الله), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أمرت. (وَلا أُشْرِكَ بِهِ إِلَيْهِ أَدْعُوا وَإِلَيْهِ مَآبِ) ولا أشرك is conjoined to أن أعبد; به is attached to أشرك; واليه is attached to أدعو; and إليه the second is a fronted khabar and مآب a postponed mubtadaʾ, its nominative sign being the implied ḍamma on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person, omitted in observance of the verse-endings, i.e., "and to Him is my return" (مآبي), meaning my place of return. (وَكَذلِكَ أَنْزَلْناهُ حُكْماً عَرَبِيًّا) The kāf is in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e., "and in the like of that sending down We sent it down"; أنزلناه is a verb, agent and direct object; حكما عربيا are two ḥāls, i.e., "a judge between people", "Arabic", i.e., in the language of the Arabs. Since the Qur'an is the cause of judgement, it was made the judgement itself, and parallels of this have already come. (وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْواءَهُمْ بَعْدَ ما جاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ) The lām is the one that prepares for an oath; إن is conditional; اتبعت is a verb and agent, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); أهواءهم is a direct object; بعد is an adverb attached to اتبعت; ما is a relative noun, a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause جاءك is the ṣila; and من العلم is a ḥāl. (ما لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا واقٍ) ما is a negative particle, in the Hijazi or the Tamimi manner; ولك is a fronted khabar; ومن الله is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective; and من is redundant (zāʾida); ولي is the ism of ما, or a mubtadaʾ; ولا واق is conjoined to it. The clause مالك has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, and for that reason it was not joined with the fāʾ. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath, in accordance with the rule when a condition and an oath come together.

* Benefits:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote the document of the peace treaty on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya, he wrote in it "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful". They said: "We know of no Raḥmān except the Raḥmān of al-Yamāma", meaning Musaylima the Liar. So Allah the Exalted revealed «وهم يكفرون بالرحمن قل: هو ربي». And He said only «ومن الأحزاب من ينكر بعضه» because they did not deny Allah but denied al-Raḥmān. It was also said: because they did not deny the stories and some of the rulings and meanings which are established in their books, but they denied the description of the Messenger of Allah and other matters.

dervis-irab:38-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُمُّ الْكِتابِ): Its origin, to which it returns, for every existing thing is written in it. The umm (mother) is the origin of a thing, and the Arabs call everything that serves as the origin of something its "mother", hence umm al-raʾs (the "mother of the head") for the brain and umm al-qurā (the "mother of the towns") for Mecca.
(مُعَقِّبَ): The muʿaqqib is originally one who follows up a thing in order to nullify it; hence it is said that "the truth is a muʿaqqib", because it pursues its adversary with a claim. The muʿaqqib is the one who returns to a thing and invalidates it.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلًا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): The wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to refute the objections they raised in order to invalidate prophethood; the exegetes have reduced them to six objections, which can be consulted in the longer works. The lām prepares for an oath (lām muwāṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and qad is a particle of confirmation. أرسلنا is a verb and agent, رسلا is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), and من قبلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أرسلنا. (وَجَعَلْنا لَهُمْ أَزْواجاً وَذُرِّيَّةً): وجعلنا is a verb and agent; ولهم is in the position of the second object, and أزواجا is the first object; ذرية is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أزواجا. This is a refutation of the first of their objections, namely their saying: "If he were a messenger from Allah, he would not be occupied with women, nor absorbed in having many wives, but would devote himself to worship and asceticism." So He answered that the messengers before you had many wives, and that did not impugn their prophethood.
(وَما كانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): The wāw is a conjunction, كان is a defective past verb (kāna), and لرسول is the fronted predicate of كان; أن and what is within its scope is its postponed subject (ism). بآية is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتي, إلا is a particle of restriction, and بإذن الله is an exception from the most general of circumstances (istithnāʾ min aʿamm al-aḥwāl), so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتابٌ): لكل is a fronted predicate (khabar), أجل is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive), and كتاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَمْحُوا اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ وَعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتابِ): يمحو الله is an imperfect verb and agent, ما is a direct object, and the clause يشاء is its ṣila (relative clause). ويثبت is conjoined to يمحو; وعنده is an adverbial (ẓarf) serving as a fronted predicate, أم is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and الكتاب is its muḍāf ilayhi. This is a reply to a second objection that they used to raise out of obstruction and rumour-mongering, namely that Muhammad commands his companions one day with something, such as facing Bayt al-Maqdis, and then the next day commands them with the opposite, such as facing the Kaʿba. So He answered them, refuting their objection, that He, glorified be He, legislated all the laws only to set right their affairs, to mend their breaches and to choose what is most beneficial for them; but they are obstructionists who pay no heed to the soundness of their affairs and to the requirements of their circumstances. (وَإِنْ ما نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّما عَلَيْكَ الْبَلاغُ وَعَلَيْنَا الْحِسابُ): The wāw is a conjunction, and إن is the conditional particle assimilated into the redundant (zāʾida) ما. نرينك is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we", and the kāf is a direct object. بعض is a second direct object, الذي is a muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause نعدهم is the ṣila of الذي. أو is a conjunction, and نتوفينك is conjoined to نرينك. The grammarians suppose the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) to be omitted, namely "then that is what will heal you and the proof of your truthfulness", and they parse the fāʾ in فإنما as causal for this omitted apodosis. But there is no need for this strained reading; rather it is easier for his saying فإنما to be itself the apodosis, and the sense of the speech is: "Whatever the matter may be and however circumstances may turn, whether We show you their downfall and send down upon them the punishment We threatened them with, or We take you in death before you see any of that, then what falls to you, and all you are bound to do, is only to convey the message." إنما is kāffa and makfūfa (the particle that restrains and the particle restrained), وعليك is a fronted predicate, والبلاغ is a postponed mubtadaʾ, وعلينا is a fronted predicate, and الحساب is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها): The hamza is for rebuking interrogation, and the wāw is a conjunction on an omitted element, as was said before, its implied form being: "Did they deny the coming down of what We threatened them with, and doubt it and dispute about it? Did they not look into that? Did they not see? Was there not for them in those sights that suffice and proofs that fully suffice a lesson?" لم is a particle of negation, inversion and jussion; أن and its ism take the place of the two objects of يروا, and the clause نأتي is the khabar of أن; the agent of نأتي is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we", and الأرض is a direct object. The clause ننقصها من أطرافها is a ḥāl clause, from the agent of نأتي or from its object, that is: "We open it land after land through what diminishes the borders of the polytheists and increases the borders of the believers." (وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ): The majestic name is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يحكم is the khabar. (لا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ): لا is the lā of generic negation, معقب is its ism, indeclinable on the fatḥa, and لحكمه is the khabar of لا. وهو: the wāw is a conjunction, هو is a mubtadaʾ, and سريع الحساب is the khabar of هو. The clause لا معقب لحكمه is also a ḥāl from the agent of نأتي, by way of iltifāt (shift of person), as if it had been said: "and Allah judges, His judgement being enforced"; the benefit of the iltifāt will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعاً): The wāw is resumptive, qad is a particle of confirmation, and the clause مكر الذين من قبلهم is resumptive, introduced to console him ﷺ. The discussion of the attribution of scheming (makr) to Allah has often been given already, so refer to it. فلله المكر: the fāʾ is a conjunction on an omitted element, by way of giving a reason, that is: "so do not care about their scheming and do not fear any harm from it"; this was omitted as sufficient, given the indication of the restriction understood from the reason. والله is a fronted khabar, المكر is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and جميعا is a ḥāl; and how far apart are their scheming and His scheming! (يَعْلَمُ ما تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ): This clause is an explanation of his saying فلله المكر جميعا. يعلم is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; ما is a direct object, the clause تكسب is its ṣila, and كل نفس is the agent.
(وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ): The sīn is for the future; ويعلم الكفار (and in one reading الكافر) is a verb and agent. لمن: the lām is a preposition, and من is an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and عقبى الدار is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا): This clause is resumptive, introduced to sum up the six objections that they raised, which in their belief lead to this conclusion, namely the invalidation of his message ﷺ. The clause لست مرسلا is the content of their saying (maqūl qawlihim) and is the sum of their objections; ليس with its ism and khabar.
(قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتابِ): كفى is a past verb whose discussion has already been given in full; بالله: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and the majestic name is genitive in form and nominative in position (the agent); شهيدا is a tamyīz (specification); بيني وبينكم are two adverbials attached to شهيدا. من is conjoined to الله, وعنده is an adverbial attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and علم الكتاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the ṣila of من.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «أولم يروا أنا نأتي الأرض ننقصها من أطرافها والله يحكم لا معقب في حكمه» there is an eloquent iltifāt. The iltifāt has been mentioned before with examples and attestations, and we add here further elaboration concerning what relates to the verse. We say: the return from the first-person address to the third person in the verse, and the building of the judgement on the majestic Name, contain the greatest and most dazzling of secrets. For when He brought the speech out to them in the guise of counsel mixed with warning, it was necessary to address them directly, in order to show them the place of strength and greatness with Him; then He returned to depicting magnificence and awe, and to verifying the content of the report by pointing to the cause that lies behind the coming to the land and diminishing its borders, and the passing of power from one people to another, and the transfer of dominion from yesterday's wrongdoers to the wronged, and from yesterday's victors to the vanquished. This magnificence can only be achieved by presenting the speech in the third person. So He said, shifting person: "And Allah judges among His creation as He wills, none can repel His judgement"; then He followed that with His saying «لا معقب لحكمه», none to nullify His will; and He added a third with His saying «وهو سريع الحساب», for everything is reckoned with Him, and before long He will call them to account in the Hereafter after the punishment of this world. Wonderful attestations of this lofty art will come.
2- Istikhdām (employment):
In His saying «لكل أجل كتاب يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب» there is a lofty art of the arts of rhetoric, which the scholars of this discipline call "the art of istikhdām". They defined it with definitions not free of obscurity, and we shall try to set out what they stated in brief. As for its definition as given by Ibn Abī l-Iṣbaʿ, Ibn Munqidh and the author of Nihāyat al-Arab, it is: that the speaker brings a word that has two possible meanings, then brings two words between which that word stands in the middle, each of the two words making use of one of the two meanings of the middle word. In the verse mentioned, the word «كتاب» can mean the fixed term, as in His saying in Sūrat al-Baqara «حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله», that is, until the "book" reaches its term, meaning the term of the waiting period (ʿidda), and ajal is its end; and kitāb can also mean "that which is written". The word kitāb stands between the two words «أجل» and «يمحو»: the word أجل makes use of one of its two meanings, namely the term, and the word يمحو makes use of its other meaning, namely that which is written. The estimation accordingly is: "for every fixed limit there is something written, which is erased and confirmed."
There is another definition, in keeping with the method of the author of al-Īḍāḥ and followed by many people: istikhdām is the uttering of a word shared between two meanings, so that you intend by that word one of the two meanings, then you return a pronoun to it by which you intend the other meaning, or, if you wish, you return two pronouns to it, intending by one of them one of the meanings and by the other the other meaning. An example of this type is the saying of the poet: "When the sky (samāʾ) descends upon the land of a people... we graze it, even if they are angry." The word al-samāʾ is meant to be rain, which is one of the two meanings, and the pronoun in "we graze it" is meant to be the other meaning, namely the vegetation. As for an attestation with two pronouns, an example is the saying of al-Buḥturī: "So may He water the ghaḍā and its inhabitants, even if they kindled it between my ribs and my flanks." The word al-ghaḍā can mean a place or a tree, and watering suits both. When he said "and its inhabitants", he meant one meaning of the word, the place, as the context indicates; and when he said "they kindled it", he used the other meaning, the tree, as the context indicates. Shaykh ʿIzz al-Dīn al-Mawṣilī, in his commentary on his Badīʿiyya, presented a fine criticism of al-Buḥturī's verse, saying: "The scholars of badīʿ stipulated that the sharing of the istikhdām word be an original sharing, and the point here is the sharing of the word al-ghaḍā, which is not original, because one of the two meanings is transferred from the other: al-ghaḍā in reality is the tree, and they called the valley ghaḍā because of the abundance of its growth in it, and they said 'the embers of the ghaḍā' for the strength of its fire; so each is transferred from a single origin."
Among examples of istikhdām is the saying of Abū l-ʿAlāʾ in his famous poem rhyming in dāl: "Time set its aim, of Abū Ḥamza, at the Awwāb, a master of reason and companion of moderation / and a jurist whose thoughts built for al-Nuʿmān what the poetry of Ziyād did not build." Here al-Nuʿmān may mean Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, and may mean al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir. By the word al-Nuʿmān, Abū l-ʿAlāʾ meant Abū Ḥanīfa, by his saying "a jurist"; and by the omitted pronoun he meant al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir, king of al-Ḥīra, by the mention of Ziyād, who is al-Nābigha, known for praising al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir. They criticised this too, because the pronoun in "did not build" (yashidhu) does not return to either of them, since the condition of the pronoun in istikhdām is that it return to the shared word so as to use its other meaning, as al-Buḥturī did with "they kindled it" (shabbūhu), for that pronoun returns to al-ghaḍā; whereas this poet made the pronoun in yashidhu not return to the shared word, which is al-Nuʿmān, so that the good repute built by Ziyād cannot be known to be for whom, since the pronoun does not return to al-Nuʿmān.
[Translator's note: the two lines of Abū l-ʿAlāʾ are run together in the Arabic text, with the second hemistich of the second line merged into the commentary; the English gloss above follows the sense as printed.]

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying before this verse: ﴿وَٱلَّذِيۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾ ("and what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth"). The position of (الذى) is nominative: you begin it anew [as mubtadaʾ (subject)] with الحقّ [as its khabar (predicate)], and you make each of the two nominative by the other. If you wish, you may put (الذى) in the position of the genitive, meaning: "Those are the signs of the Book and the signs of what has been sent down to you from your Lord", so that it is genitive; then you make (الحقّ) nominative, i.e. "that is the truth", as in His saying in al-Baqara: ﴿وَإِنَّ فَرِيقاً مِنْهُمْ لَيَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("a party of them conceal the truth while they know. The truth is from your Lord"), where we make it nominative by implying "that is the truth" or "it is the truth". And if you wish, you may make (الذى) genitive and then make (الْحَقّ) genitive too, making it an attribute of الذى; (الذى) would then be a naʿt (adjective) of "the Book", referred back to it, even though it has the wāw, as the poet said:

إلى الملِك القَرْمِ وابن الهمام * وليث الكَتِيبَة فى المُزْدَحَمِ
(To the king, the noble chief, and the son of the valiant, and the lion of the squadron in the press of battle.)

He conjoined with wāw while meaning one person. Similar to it in speech: "This report came to us from Abū Ḥafṣ and al-Fārūq", when you mean ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him.

farraa:2-2.t:
The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا﴾ ("Who raised the heavens without pillars that you see").
Two views have come about it. One says: He created them raised without pillars — you see them: with the seeing you need no report. And it is said: He created them with pillars you do not see — you do not see those pillars. The Arabs sometimes move the negation (al-ḥujja) [Translator's note: so in the text; the sense is the negating element] from the end of the expression to its beginning; that is permissible. One of them recited to me:

إذا أعجبتك الدهرَ حالٌ من امرى * فدَعهْ وواكِل حالَه واللياليا
يجئن على ما كان من صالحٍ به * وإن كان فيما لا يرى الناس آليا
(If some man's state ever pleases you, leave him, and entrust his state to the nights: they will bring out whatever good there is in him, even if, in what people see, he is not one who falls short.)

Its meaning is: even if, (in what) people see, he does not fall short. And another said:

ولا أراها تزال ظالمةً * تُحدث لى نكبَةً وتنكؤها
(And I do not see it ceasing to be unjust, causing me a misfortune and then reopening it.)

Its meaning is: I see it does not cease.

farraa:3-3.t:
﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَدَّ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾ means: He spread out the earth in breadth and length.
His saying: ﴿زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾ ("two kinds, a pair"): the two kinds (zawjān) are two — male and female — and the two sorts. This is made clear by His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ والأُنْثَى﴾ ("and that He created the two kinds, male and female"); so it is clear that they are two, by their being explained as male and female.

farraa:4-4.t:
﴿وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُّتَجَاوِرَاتٌ﴾ ("and in the earth are neighbouring tracts"). He is saying: there is difference in them while they are neighbouring: this one is good and produces growth, and that one is salty and brings forth nothing.
Then He said: ﴿وَجَنَّاتٌ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَزَرْعٌ﴾ ("and gardens of grapes and crops"). In "crops" and what follows it you may use the nominative; had you used the genitive it would be correct. Whoever makes it nominative refers it back to "the gardens", and whoever makes it genitive refers it back to "grapes", i.e. "of grapes and of such-and-such".
His saying: ﴿صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ﴾ ("in clusters and not in clusters"): the nominative here is easy, because it explains the state of the palms. The reading is with the genitive, and had it been nominative it would be correct, meaning: "some of it in clusters and some not in clusters". Al-ṣinwān are palm trees whose root is one. In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ there came: "A man's paternal uncle is the ṣinw (twin trunk) of his father."
Then He said: ﴿تُسْقَىٰ بِمَآءٍ وَاحِدٍ﴾ ("watered with one water"), and (يُسْقَى). Whoever reads with tāʾ goes by the femininity of the crops, the gardens and the palms; whoever uses the masculine goes by "the plants": all of that is watered with one water, yet all of it differs — sour and sweet. In this there is a sign.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ ٱلْمَثُلاَتُ﴾ ("they ask you to hasten the evil before the good, while exemplary punishments have already passed before them").
He is saying: they ask you to hasten the punishment while they feel safe from it, and they see the punishments — the mathulāt — upon others who have passed away; these are the mathulāt. Tamīm say: al-muthlāt. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ﴾ ("and give women their bridal gifts") is Ḥijāzī, while Tamīm say ṣudqāt, its singular being ṣudqa. Al-Farrāʾ said: the people of the Ḥijāz say: "Give her her ṣaduqa", and Tamīm say: "Give her her ṣudqa", in the dialect of Tamīm.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ ("you are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide"). Some said: a prophet. Others said: for every people there is a guide whom they follow, either with truth or with falsehood.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ﴾ ("and what the wombs fall short of and what they exceed"). (تَغِيضُ): He is saying: what they fall short of the nine months, which are the term of pregnancy; (وَمَا تَزْدَادُ) means: what they exceed beyond the nine. Do you not see that the Arabs say: "The waters ghāḍat", i.e. decreased? And in the ḥadīth: "When winter is [hot as] summer, and the child is [a source of] rage, and the noble ones dwindle away (ghāḍat … ghayḍan) and the base ones overflow." So the meaning of decrease in al-ghayḍ has become clear.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿سَوَآءٌ مِّنْكُمْ مَّنْ أَسَرَّ ٱلْقَوْلَ وَمَنْ جَهَرَ بِهِ﴾ ("alike among you is he who conceals speech and he who declares it").
(مَنْ) and (من) are in the position of the nominative; what makes both of them nominative is سواء. Their meaning is: whoever conceals speech or declares it, He knows it. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِٱلْلَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌ بِٱلنَّهَارِ﴾ ("and he who hides by night and goes forth by day"), i.e. is apparent by day. He is saying: He knows the apparent and the secret, and all are alike to Him.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾ ("he has [angels] in succession before him").
Al-muʿaqqibāt are the angels: the angels of the night succeed the angels of the day, guarding him. Al-muʿaqqibāt are males, except that it is a plural of a plural: "angels" is muʿaqqiba [i.e. a collective], and then muʿaqqiba was pluralised, as he said "abnāwāt Saʿd", and rijālāt, the plural of rijāl.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ ("they guard him by the command of Allah"), returning to the masculine of which I told you, which is the meaning. And (ويحفظونه) — that guarding — may be from the command of Allah, i.e. by His command and by His permission, Mighty and Majestic; as you say to a man: "I come to you from your calling me" and "by your calling me". And Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ ٱلْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً﴾ ("it is He who shows you the lightning, in fear and hope"): fear for the traveller and hope for the one at home.
His saying: ﴿وَيُنْشِىءُ ٱلسَّحَابَ ٱلثِّقَالَ﴾ ("and He produces the heavy clouds"): al-saḥāb, though singular in form, is a plural; its singular is saḥāba. Its naʿt (adjective) was made plural, as in His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وَعَبْقَرِىٍّ حِسَانٍ﴾ ("reclining on green cushions and beautiful carpets"), and He did not say akhḍar or ḥasan, nor al-thaqīl for the clouds. Had any of that come it would be correct, as in His saying: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُم مِنَ الشَّجَرِ الأَخْضَرِ نَاراً فَإذَا أَنتُم مِنْهُ تُوقِدُون﴾ ("who made for you fire from the green tree, and lo, you kindle from it"). But if the attribute of something of this kind refers to smallness or largeness, you only say it in the sense of the plural. Thus you say: "This is good dates (tamr ṭayyib)", but you do not say "small dates" or "large dates" [in the singular], because goodness applies to it as a whole, so it was made singular, whereas smallness, largeness, length and shortness are in each date by itself.

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿لَهُ دَعْوَةُ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾ ("to Him is the call of truth"): "There is no god but Allah". ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ﴾ ("and those they call upon besides Him"), meaning the idols: they do not answer the one who calls on them with anything, except as the thirsty man gets [water] who looks down upon water and has nothing with him to draw it with. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إِلاَّ كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى ٱلْمَآءِ﴾ ("except like one who stretches out his palms towards water"). Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made that clear: ﴿لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ﴾ ("that it may reach his mouth, but it will not reach it").

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿وَللَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً﴾ ("and to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly"). It may be asked: who of the people of the heavens and the earth prostrates willingly and unwillingly? The angels prostrate willingly; and whoever of the people of the earth entered Islam out of desire for it, or was born into it, is also willing; and whoever was compelled into Islam prostrates unwillingly. (وَظِلاَلُهُمْ) ("and their shadows"): He is saying: every person's shadow prostrates with him morning and evening, because the shadow turns back in the evening and becomes a fayʾ (returning shade) that prostrates. It is like His saying: ﴿عَنِ اليمينِ وَالشَّمَائِلِ﴾ ("to the right and to the lefts") in meaning — and Allah knows best. So the meaning of the plural and the singular is the same.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي ٱلظُّلُمَاتُ وَٱلنُّورُ﴾ ("or are darkness and light equal?"). It is read (أَمْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ) [with yāʾ], and it is read (تَسْتَوِى) with tāʾ. It is like His saying: ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ ("and the cry seized those who did wrong"), while in another place it is (وَأَخَذَتْ).

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿أَنَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا﴾ ("He sent down water from the sky, and valleys flowed according to their measure"). He struck it as a parable for the Qurʾān when it was sent down upon them, given His saying: ﴿فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا﴾ — He is saying: the hearts received it according to their measures and their inclinations.
His saying: ﴿فَٱحْتَمَلَ ٱلسَّيْلُ زَبَداً﴾ ("and the torrent carried a swelling foam"): it goes away with no benefit in it; likewise what settled in the heart of one who did not believe and worshipped his gods, and came to have nothing in his hand. ﴿وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ ("but as for what benefits people, it remains in the earth"): this is the parable of the believer.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾ ("and from what they heat in the fire") — of gold, silver and copper — there is a foam like the foam of the torrent, meaning its dross, which the fire gathers and draws out of the gold and silver, like the foam on the torrent.
As for His saying: ﴿ٱبْتِغَآءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَاعٍ﴾ ("seeking ornaments or utensils"), He is saying: they heat it in the fire seeking thereby ornaments and utensils — what is made of copper and iron — and that has a foam like it.
His saying: ﴿فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءً﴾ ("then it goes away as scum"): it is with madd (lengthening), its root having a hamza. One says: "The valley cast off (jafaʾa) its froth, jafʾan." [Translator's note: the text has «جَفْثا»; the maṣdar meant is evidently jafʾan.] And it was said al-jufāʾ just as it was said al-ghuthāʾ (froth). Every maṣdar (verbal noun) [denoting things] gathered together, like al-qumāsh (scraps), al-duqāq (crumbs), al-ghuthāʾ and al-ḥuṭām (debris), is a maṣdar, and it takes the course of a noun in this sense, just as al-ʿaṭāʾ is a noun for al-iʿṭāʾ (giving). So it is with al-jufāʾ and al-qumāsh: if you wanted its maṣdar you would say: "I gathered it, qamshan". And al-jufāʾ means: it goes away quickly, as it came.

farraa:23-24.t: His saying: ﴿وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ﴾ ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم﴾ ("and the angels enter upon them from every gate: 'Peace be upon you'"): they say, "Peace be upon you". The verb "saying" is implied, as in His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ رَبَّنا﴾ ("if you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord: 'Our Lord…'"), i.e. they say, "Our Lord"; then it was left out.

farraa:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَآءُ وَيَقَدِرُ﴾ ("Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts"), i.e. He makes ample and He yaqdiru (i.e. He measures out and straitens). It is also said: He extends provision to whom He wills and yaqdiru for him in that, i.e. He chooses [what is best] for him. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the creation while knowing them, and made wealth the good of some of them and poverty the good of others; that is the [best] choice for both parties.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿طُوبَىٰ لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ﴾ ("blessedness is theirs and a goodly return") — nominative, and the reading is on that basis. Had طوبى and الحسن been made accusative it would be correct, [as] the Arabs say: al-ḥamdu li-llāh and al-ḥamda li-llāh. Ṭūbā, even though it is a noun, can take the accusative, as is said in reviling: "Dust (al-turābu) be his!" and "Dust (al-turāba) be his!". But the nominative in such established nouns is better than the accusative.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ﴾ ("and if there were a Qurʾān by which the mountains were moved…"). No answer (jawāb) to law came after it. If you wish, you may make its answer precede it: "and they disbelieve [ms. 86b] even if We sent down to them what they asked for". And if you wish, its answer is left out because its matter is known: the Arabs omit the answer of a thing when it is known, intending brevity, as the poet said:

وأقسم لو شىء أتانا رَسولُه * سواك ولكن لم نجد لك مَدْفعا
(I swear, had anything other than you sent its messenger to us… but we found no way of repelling you.)

His saying: ﴿بَل للَّهِ ٱلأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾ ("rather, the matter belongs to Allah entirely. Have not those who believe despaired…?"). The exegetes said: yayʾas means "know". In meaning it is as they explain it, because Allah had conveyed to the believers that if Allah willed He would guide all mankind; so He said: "Have they not despaired in knowledge?" He is saying: knowledge makes them despair; so the knowledge in them was implied, as you say in speech: "I have despaired of you, [knowing] that you will not succeed, in knowledge (ʿilman)", as though you said: "I knew it with knowledge".
Al-Kalbī said, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: yayʾas in the sense of "know" is a dialect of al-Nakhaʿ. Al-Farrāʾ said: we have not found it in Arabic except as I have explained. And the saying of the poet:

حتى إذا يئِس الرماة وأرْسلُوا * غُضْفاً دواجِن قافلاَ أعصَامُهَا
(Until, when the hunters despaired and let loose droop-eared tame hounds, their collars dried out…)

means: until, when they despaired of everything possible except what had appeared to them, they let loose. So it means: until, when they knew that there was no way except what they saw, they let loose; what lay beyond it was despair.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ تُصِيبُهُم بِمَا صَنَعُواْ قَارِعَةٌ﴾ ("and those who disbelieve will not cease to be struck, for what they have done, by a calamity"): al-qāriʿa is one of the raiding parties; (أَوْ تَحُلُّ) ("or you alight") — you, O Muḥammad, with your army — ﴿قَرِيباً مِّن دَارِهِمْ﴾ ("near their home").

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَآئِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ ("is He then who stands over every soul for what it has earned…?"). Its answer was left out, and He did not say "like such-and-such", because the meaning is known. What follows has made it clear, since He said: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ﴾ ("yet they have assigned partners to Allah"), as though He said in meaning: "[like] their partners whom they have taken". Similar to it is the saying of the poet:

تَخَيَّرِى خُيِّرت أُمَّ عالِ * بين قصير شَبْرُه تِنبَالِ
أذاكِ أم منخرق السربال * ولا يزال آخر الليالى
* مُتلِفَ مال ومفيدَ مال *
(Choose — may you be given good choice, Umm ʿĀl — between a short one of small span, a dwarf: is it that one, or one with a torn shirt who, to the end of nights, never ceases to squander wealth and to gain wealth?)

[I.e.] choose between such-and-such and the one with the torn shirt. When he had brought it in the mention, that sufficed from repeating the [governing] construction for it.
His saying: ﴿فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَم بِظَاهِرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ﴾ ("in the earth, or with an apparent [part] of speech?"): false in meaning, i.e. it is apparent in speech, false in meaning.
And it is read: ﴿وَصُدُّواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾ ("and they were turned away from the path"), while some read (وصَدُّوا) ("and they turned [others] away"), making them the agents.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾ ("the likeness of the Garden promised to the God-fearing"). He is saying: the attributes of the Garden. Al-Farrāʾ said: some of the elders narrated to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, that ʿAlī read it: (أَمثالُ الجنّة) ("the likenesses of the Garden"). Al-Farrāʾ said: I think there was a man below Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [in the chain]. He said: that came from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, but the majority follow the written text of the muṣḥaf.
His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾ ("beneath which rivers flow"): this is what makes [مثل] nominative [as its khabar (predicate)]. And if you wish, [it is because] for "likeness" the "likenesses" are the meaning, as you say: "So-and-so's description: brown-skinned, and such-and-such". "Brown-skinned" is not made nominative by "description"; it is only a fresh start (ibtidāʾ), i.e. "he is red, brown-skinned, he is such-and-such".
Had anna come in something like this, it would be correct. Similar to it in speech: "Your description is that you are such and that you are such". And His saying: ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرِ الإنْسَانُ إِلَي طَعَامِهِ إنَّا﴾ ("so let man look at his food: We…") [with inna] is on the pattern of ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلأَنْهَارُ﴾; and whoever reads ﴿أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا المَاءَ﴾ ("that We poured down water") with the fatḥa has made the noun overt, because it is referred back to "food" in the genitive, or is resumed, i.e. "his food is that We poured, then We did".

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتَابٌ﴾ ("for every term there is a decree"). The exegesis came: "for every decree there is a term". Similar to it is ﴿وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَة المَوْتِ بالْحَقِّ﴾ ("and the stupor of death came with the truth"), and that [reading] from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah have mercy on him: ﴿وجاءتْ سَكرةُ المَوْتِ بالحقِّ﴾ [Translator's note: the two quotations are identical in the text; the reading attributed to Abū Bakr is elsewhere given as "the stupor of the truth came with death"] — because the truth [ms. 87a] brought it and it brings the truth. So likewise you say: "for every term something deferred" and "for every deferred thing a term", and the meaning is one. And Allah knows best.

farraa:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿يَمْحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثْبِتُ﴾ ("Allah erases what He wills and confirms"). (ويُثَبِّتُ) with doubling is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdullāh [Ibn Masʿūd], and it is read (يُثْبِتُ), light. The meaning of its exegesis is that the deeds of the servant, small and great, are raised to Him, Mighty and Majestic; He confirms whatever carries punishment or reward and erases whatever is besides that.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ﴾ ("whether We show you part of what We promise them") — while you are alive — ﴿أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾ ("or We take you [in death]") — it will be after your death — ﴿فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلاَغُ وَعَلَيْنَا ٱلْحِسَابُ﴾ ("upon you is only the conveying, and upon Us is the reckoning").

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا نَأْتِي ٱلأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ ("have they not seen that We come to the land, diminishing it from its borders?"). It has come [in the exegesis]: Have the people of Mecca not seen that We open for you what is around it? That is His saying (نَنقُصُهَا): i.e. do they not fear that it will reach them? And it was said: ﴿نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ — by the death of the scholars.
His saying: ﴿لاَ مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ﴾ ("there is no reverser of His judgement"). He is saying: there is none to turn back His judgement when He judges something. Al-muʿaqqib is the one who comes back upon a thing. And the saying of Labīd:

حتّى تُهجَّر فى الرَّوَاح وهَاجه * طلبُ المعقِّب حَقَّه المظلومُ
(Until he set out at midday towards evening, roused like the wronged claimant pursuing his due.)

is from that, because (al-muʿaqqib is the creditor who comes back to his debtor and takes it from him, or one from whom something was taken, who comes back to take it).

farraa:42-42.t: His saying: ﴿ وَسَيَعْلَمُ ٱلْكُفَّارُ﴾ ("and the disbelievers will know") is in the plural, and the people of Medina read (الكَافِر) ("the disbeliever").

farraa:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ ("and whoever has knowledge of the Book"): it is said [this is] ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām. And (مِنْ عِنْدِه) is genitive, referred back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: an elder narrated to me from al-Zuhrī, tracing it back to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that when he came to embrace Islam he heard the Prophet ﷺ reciting ﴿وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾. Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: an elder narrated to me from a man, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba: ﴿وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾. And it is read (وَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ عِلْمُ الكِتَابِ) ("and from Him is the knowledge of the Book"), with kasra on the mīm of (من).

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «والذي أنزل»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the relative is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «الحق». The two prepositional phrases «إليك» and «من ربك» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزل». The clause «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون» is conjoined to the clause «الذي أُنزل ... الحقُّ».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «ترونها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عَمَد», and the clause «كل يجري» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الشمس والقمر». The clause «يدبِّر» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «استوى», and likewise the clause «يُفَصِّل». The clause «لعلكم توقنون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «ومن كل الثمرات»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the later «جعل». «اثنين» is a naʿt (adjective) of «زوجين». The second clause «جعل» is conjoined to the first, and the clause «يغشي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «جعل». The lām in «لآيات» is for emphasis, and «آيات» is the noun of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «وفي الأرض قطع» is conjoined to the clause «إن في ذلك لآيات». «وجنات»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «قطع», and the preposition and its genitive noun «من أعناب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «جنات». «صنوان» is a naʿt of «نخيل». «وغير»: a noun conjoined to «صنوان». The clause «يسقى» is a naʿt of the kinds mentioned before, and the clause «ونفضِّل» is conjoined to the clause «يسقى». The preposition and its genitive noun «في الأكل» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بعضها», and the clause «يعقلون» is a naʿt of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «فعجب قولهم»: the fāʾ is connective; «عجب» is a fronted khabar (predicate), and «قولهم» is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «أئذا كنا» is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of an accusative. «إذا»: a pure ẓarf (adverb) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied «نبعث», and the clause «أئنَّا لفي خلق جديد» is explicative of the implied «نبعث». The clause «أولئك الذين كفروا» is resumptive. «وأولئك الأغلال في أعناقهم»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; «الأغلال» is a second mubtadaʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to the clause «أولئك الذين كفروا», and the clause «الأغلال في أعناقهم» is the khabar of «أولئك». The clause «وأولئك أصحاب النار» is conjoined to the clause «أولئك الذين كفروا», and the clause «هم فيها خالدون» is a second khabar of «أولئك».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «قبل الحسنة»: a ẓarf (adverb) of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السيئة». The clause «وقد خلت المثلات» is a ḥāl from the wāw in «يستعجلونك», and the preposition and its genitive noun «على ظلمهم» is attached to a ḥāl from «الناس».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «لولا»: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). The clause «إنما أنت منذر» is resumptive, and the clause «ولكل قوم هاد» is conjoined to the resumptive one. «هادٍ»: a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «وكل شيء عنده بمقدار» is conjoined to the clause «الله يعلم». The adverb «عنده» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء», and the preposition and its genitive noun «بمقدار» is attached to the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «عالم»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is عالم", and «الكبير المتعال» are two khabars of the implied «هو».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «سواء» is a fronted khabar (predicate). The preposition and its genitive noun «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «سواء». «مَنْ» is a relative, the mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar is not put in the dual because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and here it means "equal". «مستخفٍ» is a khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ. The preposition and its genitive noun «بالليل» is attached to «مستخفٍ». The clause «سواء منكم من أسر» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من بين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «معقبات», and the clause «يحفظونه» is a naʿt of «معقبات». The preposition and its genitive noun «بأنفسهم» is attached to the implied ṣila (relative clause). The conditional clause is resumptive. «إذا» is a conditional adverb attached to the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e. "it occurs"; its apodosis «فلا مردَّ له» does not govern «إذا», because what comes after the fāʾ does not govern what comes before it. «فلا مرَدَّ له»: the fāʾ is connective, «لا» is the lā of generic negation, «مردَّ» is its noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun «له» is attached to the khabar (predicate). «وما لهم مِنْ دونه مِنْ وَالٍ»: the wāw is a conjunction, «ما» is negating, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to the khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun «من دونه» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the mubtadaʾ (subject) «والٍ», and «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause is conjoined to the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «خوفا»: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «وينشئ» is conjoined to the clause «يريكم».

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The preposition and its genitive noun «من خيفته» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسبح». The clause «وهم يجادلون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative «مَنْ», in the position of an accusative, and the wāw is circumstantial. The clause «وهو شديد المحال» is a ḥāl from the Name of Majesty.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «والذين يدعون»: the wāw is a conjunction; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). The preposition and its genitive noun «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied hāʾ, i.e. "they call upon them, being other than Him". The clause «لا يستجيبون» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «الذين»; «إلا» is for restriction, and the preposition and its genitive noun «كباسط» is attached to an omitted element standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "except with a response like the response of one who stretches out". «وما هو ببالغه»: the wāw is circumstantial; «ما» is negating, operating like «ليس», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar; the clause is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يبلغ». The clause «وما دعاء الكافرين إلا في ضلال» is resumptive; «إلا» is for restriction, and the preposition and its genitive noun «في ضلال» is attached to the khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «ولله يسجد» is conjoined to the clause «له دعوة الحق». The preposition and its genitive noun «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). «طوعا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «قل الله»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth". The clause «أفاتخذتم» is conjoined to an implied element which is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), i.e. "did you acknowledge, and then take…". The preposition and its genitive noun «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أولياء», and the preposition and its genitive noun «لأنفسهم» is attached to a ḥāl from «نفعا». «أم هل تستوي»: a particle of digression (iḍrāb), and the clause after it is resumptive, and likewise «أم جعلوا». The preposition and its genitive noun «كخلقه»: the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a creating like His creating". The clause «وهو الواحد» is conjoined to the clause «الله خالق»; «القهار» is a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «ومما يوقدون»: the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «زبد». The preposition and its genitive noun «في النار» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليه». «ابتغاء» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); «مثله» is a naʿt (adjective). The clause «ومما يوقدون عليه زبد» is conjoined to the clause «أنزل». «فأمَّا»: the fāʾ is resumptive; «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing; the clause «فيذهب» is the khabar, and the fāʾ is connective; «جفاء» is a ḥāl. «كذلك»: the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "He strikes with a striking like that striking"; the clause «يضرب» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «الحسنى»: a mubtadaʾ (subject). The conditional clause with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «الذين». The maṣdar after «لو» is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied «ثبت». The preposition and its genitive noun «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause); «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the ṣila. «ومثله»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ما»; «معه» is a ẓarf (adverb) of place attached to a ḥāl from «مثله». The clause «والذين لم يستجيبوا» together with its khabar is conjoined to the clause «للذين استجابوا الحسنى». The clause «أولئك لهم سوء» is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ «والذين لم يستجيبوا», and the clause «لهم سوء» is the khabar of «أولئك». The clause «ومأواهم جهنم» is conjoined to the clause «لهم سوء». The clause «وبئس المهاد» is resumptive, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. «جهنم».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: «أفمن يعلم»: the hamza is for interrogation, and the fāʾ is resumptive; «مَنْ» is a relative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject). «أنَّ» is abrogating; «ما» is a relative noun, its noun, and «الحق» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the maṣdar takes the place of the two objects of «علم». «كمن»: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «منْ».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «الذين يوفون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أولي الألباب». «الميثاق»: its origin is «المِوْثاق»; the wāw became quiescent after a kasra, so it was changed into yāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «والذين»: a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the relative before it. The interpreted maṣdar «أن يوصل» is a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in «به».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «والذين صبروا»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. «سرا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «أولئك لهم عقبى الدار» is resumptive, and the clause «لهم عقبى» is the khabar (predicate) of «أولئك».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «جنات» is a badal (substitute) from {عُقْبَى}. «ومَنْ صلح» is a relative noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the wāw; conjoining the overt noun to the nominative pronoun wāw is permitted because of the separating element. The preposition and its genitive noun «من آبائهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the referring pronoun. The clause «والملائكة يدخلون» is a ḥāl from the wāw in «يدخلونها».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition and its genitive noun after it is its khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it denotes a supplication. «بما»: «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what the notion of "being settled" (al-istiqrār), to which the khabar is attached, is attached to. «فنعم عقبى الدار»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. «الجنة». The clause «سلام عليكم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of a concealed verb of saying, and the concealed saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being «يقولون». The clause «فنعم عقبى الدار» is conjoined to the clause «سلام عليكم».

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «والذين ينقضون»: the wāw is resumptive, and the relative is a mubtadaʾ (subject). The maṣdar «أن يوصل» is a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ. The clause «أولئك لهم اللعنة» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «الذين», and the clause «لهم اللعنة» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «أولئك». The clause «ولهم سوء» is conjoined to the clause «لهم اللعنة».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The clause «وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «فرحوا»; «ما» is negating and inoperative, «إلا» is for restriction, and «متاع» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and the preposition and its genitive noun «من ربه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «آية».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «الذين آمنوا»: this relative is a badal (substitute) from the preceding {مَنْ أَنَابَ}. «ألا» is a particle of opening (istiftāḥ), and the clause after it is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «الذين آمنوا»: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «طوبى لهم» is its khabar (predicate). «طوبى»: a mubtadaʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar. «وحُسْنُ»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «طوبى».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (كذلك) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "We sent you to the people with a sending like that sending". The clause «قد خلت» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أمة», and the clause «وهم يكفرون بالرحمن» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «عليهم». The clause of tanzīh (declaring Allah's oneness) is a second khabar (predicate) of «هو»; «إلا» is for restriction, and «هو» is a badal (substitute) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar.
