According to Sībawayh this is not permissible, because one does not begin with an indefinite noun. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is that these are equal before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His knowledge of them is one. Ḥassān said: [al-Wāfir] 243-
فمن يهجو رسول الله منكم ... ويمدحه وينصره سواء
(Whoever of you satirises the Messenger of Allah, or praises him and supports him, it is all the same.)
That is, in his standing before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ: the plural of معقّبة, the hāʾ being for intensiveness; that is why يَحْفَظُونَهُ is permissible in the masculine. مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ: that is, their guarding him is by Allah's command — Mighty and Majestic — He commanded them to guard him against what has not been decreed. It is said: the meaning is that the مُعَقِّبات are from Allah's command, Mighty and Majestic. These two answers are according to those who say the مُعَقِّبات are the angels. As for those who say the مُعَقِّبات are the guards (shuraṭ), the meaning for them is: they guard him from Allah's command, according to their claim. إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ: there are two views on it. One is that the meaning is: Allah does not change the favour and honour He began with a person by punishing or tormenting him, unless he changes what is in himself. The other view: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not change the condition of a righteous believing people, calling them disbelievers and transgressors, unless they do what necessitates that, and He does not command their humiliation unless they change what is in themselves. وَإِذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوْءاً فَلا مَرَدَّ لَهُ: so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, warned them after informing them that He knows their secrets and what they conceal. وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ والٍ: that is, no protector to help them and defend them.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً: as maṣdars (verbal nouns). The exegetes say: fear for the traveller and hope for the resident, for the most part; in reality it applies generally to everyone who fears or hopes. وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحابَ الثِّقالَ: [السحاب is] the plural of سحابة, and that is why it is described with الثقال.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ: the exegetes say: الرعد is the name of an angel, so this is literal. It is also said that it is figurative and that it is the sound; then the meaning of يسبح is that it indicates Allah's transcendence, Mighty and Majestic, above all likenesses, and so glorification is attributed to it figuratively.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: وَما دُعاءُ الْكافِرِينَ: that is, the disbelievers' calling upon idols. إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ: away from what is right and from benefiting by an answer.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: the scholars have discussed the meaning of this, and among the best things said is that prostration here is submission to Allah's ordering, Mighty and Majestic, and His disposal [of them], in health, sickness and other things.
طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً: that is, they are led along whether they like it or dislike it; they have no stratagem in that. Their shadows too are subject to Allah's ordering, Mighty and Majestic, and His making the sun run, with the shadow's increase and decrease and its disappearing through the passing of time and the course of the sun, as He, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ: that is, the believer and the disbeliever. أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُماتُ وَالنُّورُ: that is, disbelief and faith.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
فَسالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِها: the exegetes said: i.e. according to the measure of what fills them; and it is said: what was decreed for them.
فَاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَداً رابِياً: the sentence ends here. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتاعٍ زَبَدٌ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the Basrans. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is nominative because its meaning is "from what you kindle in the fire there is froth". He said: and it is الغثاء (scum); غثى يغثي غثيا وغثيانا; it is what is of no benefit. مثله: that is, like the froth of the sea. كَذلِكَ: in the position of the accusative. فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ: that is, from these things. فَيَذْهَبُ جُفاءً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial); from their saying انجفأت القدر, when the pot throws off its froth; it too is الغثاء.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنى: [الحسنى is] in the position of the nominative; the implied form may be "the reward of the best", and it is said: it is a name for Paradise. أولئك لهم سوء الحساب: the scrutiny, the rebuke, and the cancelling of good deeds by bad deeds.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ: in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from His words, Mighty and Majestic: إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: كَذلِكَ أَرْسَلْناكَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative. الأمة is the community.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَالَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ: that is, they maintain their ties of kinship, and [ties with] those of the people of obedience whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded to be honoured and revered.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ: that is, they repel; when they are inclined to an evil deed, they reflect, restrain themselves, and repel it by seeking forgiveness and desisting. This is a good deed. They also forbid wrongdoing, by admonition or by harshness, and all of this is good. أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ.

nahhas-irab:23-24.t:
جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ: a badal (substitute) from عقبى. يَدْخُلُونَها وَمَنْ صَلَحَ: this is one of the difficult points of grammar, because most grammarians say: ضربته وزيد ("I struck him, and Zayd") is ugly until the latent/attached pronoun is reinforced. The grammarians discussed this, until a group of them said: قمت وزيد is good with an alif [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense of "with an alif" is unclear], because this is not like the genitive, since the genitive pronoun is never separated. Abū Isḥāq held that the better form is قمت وزيدا, meaning "together", unless the speech is lengthened, so that you say: قمت في الدار وزيد, and ضربتك أمس وزيد — and if you wish, you use the accusative. In this, regard is paid only to what is separated, which is treated like reinforcement (tawkīd). Abū Jaʿfar said: in my view — and Allah knows best — «من» may be in the position of the nominative, the implied form being: "Those, and whoever is righteous among their fathers, spouses and offspring, theirs is the final abode."
وَالْمَلائِكَةُ: mubtadaʾ (subject). يَدْخُلُونَ: in the position of the khabar (predicate), and the implied form is: [they enter] saying: سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: this too was out of obstinacy, after they had seen the signs.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from (من). وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: that is, by His promise. أَلا: [a particle of] alerting. بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ: that is, their hearts.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is طُوبى لَهُمْ. الَّذِينَ may also be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «من», or meaning "I mean". And طُوبى may be in the position of the accusative, meaning "Allah has granted them ṭūbā".

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "if this occurred". The scholars have several views on this verse. One is that the apodosis is omitted, the implied form being "it would have been this Quran"; and it is said the implied form is "they would not have believed". Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "We wished that there were a Quran by which the mountains were moved", and so this is without omission. Al-Farrāʾ has a good view on it. He said: the apodosis is in what precedes it, i.e. "and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful, even if there were a Quran by which the mountains were moved". بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً: [جَمِيعاً] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: there are several dialect forms in it: one says يائس, and one says ييئس on the pattern فعل يفعل, and one says يئس يئس, the imperfect having the same form as the past [Translator's note: the forms are distinguished only by vowelling, which the source does not show]. أَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ: in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قائِمٌ عَلى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, indicated by وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: the implied form is "like their partners". قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ: that is, name them by a creation they created or a deed they did by their own power. أَمْ بِظاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ: it is said its meaning is: it has no reality; and it is said: or by an apparent statement mentioned in the scriptures. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read وَصُدُّوا with kasra on the ṣād, because the original is صددوا, and the vowel of the dāl was shifted onto the ṣād.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
لَهُمْ عَذابٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا:
Allah's cursing them, Mighty and Majestic, and the believers' hostility towards them.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh; the implied form for him is: "In what is related to you is the likeness of the Garden", or "The likeness of the Garden is in what We relate to you". Al-Farrāʾ said: what makes it nominative is تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ, the meaning being "the Garden that the God-fearing were promised, rivers flow beneath it", as one says: حلية فلان أسمر ("so-and-so's description: dark"). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: whoever says مثل means صفة (description) has erred, because one says only:
صفة فلان أنه ظريف وأنه كريم ("so-and-so's description is that he is witty and generous"), and one says: مثل زيد مثل عمرو ("Zayd's likeness is ʿAmr's likeness"). «مثل» is taken from المثال (pattern) and الحذو (model), while صفة is taken from التحلية (portraying) and النعت (describing). The implied form is only: "In what is related to you is the likeness of the Garden." أُكُلُها دائِمٌ: and in it is such-and-such, and in it is such-and-such. تِلْكَ عُقْبَى الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا: mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَعُقْبَى الْكافِرِينَ النَّارُ.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ: it is said He means by it the believers, and the Book is the Quran. وَمِنَ الْأَحْزابِ: that is, those who banded together in enmity to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and the believers reject what did not agree with them. It is also said: those given the Book are the Jews and the Christians, who rejoice at the Quran because it confirms their prophets and their scriptures, even if they did not believe in Muḥammad ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:38-39.t: وَما كانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: that is, except by His permitting him to ask for the sign, so that he knows there is benefit in that. لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتابٌ: that is, for every nation there is a written decree and a determined, decided matter which the angels come to know, so that Allah's power, Mighty and Majestic, is known thereby; and likewise وَعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتابِ. We have already explained the meaning of يَمْحُوا اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: وَإِنْ ما نُرِيَنَّكَ: in the position of the jussive by the condition, and the nūn entered for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها: the plural of طرف. We have mentioned the view of the exegetes on it. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: الطرف is the noble part of everything, and its plural is أطراف, as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Ṭawīl] 244-
هم الطّرف النّاكي العدوّ وأنتم ... بقصوى ثلاث تأكلون الوقائصا ]
(They are the noble ones who wound the enemy, while you, at the farthest of three [stages], eat the broken-necked beasts.)
He said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: «Knowledge is valleys; in whichever valley you take of it, you will be exhausted, so take from everything a ṭaraf» — i.e. the choicest. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها, i.e. by [taking] its scholars, and the scholars are the choicest, the noble. From this is «He does not know which of his two ṭarafs is longer», i.e. he does not know, because of his simple-mindedness, whether nobility comes to him from his father's side or his mother's side. الطّرف is also the noble horse, and الطّارف is newly acquired property.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعاً: that is, to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, belongs the abiding plotting that encompasses its people. The meaning of plotting on the part of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is that He sends down punishment upon whoever deserves it from where he does not know. وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ: and الكافر [in the other reading] has the same meaning, a singular standing for a plural.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ: [الله is] in the position of the nominative. شَهِيداً: as a specification (bayān). وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ: in the position of the genitive, conjoined according to the wording; it may also be in the position of the nominative according to the meaning. عِلْمُ الْكِتابِ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَوَآءٌ مِّنْكُمْ مَّنْ أَسَرَّ ٱلْقَوْلَ وَمَنْ جَهَرَ بِهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِٱلْلَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌ بِٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: al-sārib (السَّارب) is the one who is out in the open.
Qatāda said: al-sārib is the one out in the open, the one going about.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ means concealed in acts of disobedience, and «sāribun bi-l-nahār» means out in the open.
Some of the people of language said: ﴿وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾ means out in the open, from خَفَيْتُه meaning "I brought it out into the open," and ﴿وَسَارِبٌ بِٱلنَّهَارِ﴾ means concealed, from their saying: انسرب الوحش, "the wild animal slipped away," when it enters its lair.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The first view is more fitting because of the eminence of those who held it, and it is closer to the meaning, because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: equal among you are the one who keeps his speech secret and the one who declares it, the one who hides himself by night and the one who appears by day; all of that is equal in Allah's knowledge.
And it is better known and more common in the language.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says سَرَب يَسْرُب سَرْباً وسُرُوباً when he goes off.
And al-Aṣmaʿī related: خَلِّ له سَرْبَه, i.e. "leave his way clear for him."

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
There are three views on the verse:
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Angels who guard him; then when the decree comes, they leave him to it.
And Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — he said: by Allah's permission; they are of Allah's command, and they are angels.
Al-Ḥasan said: "by (ʿan) Allah's command."
Mujāhid and Qatāda said — and this is Qatāda's wording —: They are angels who take turns by night and by day by (ʿan) Allah's command, i.e. by Allah's command.
So this is one view.
The second view: it was narrated from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ — he said: They are the rulers who have people in front of them and behind them, guarding them from Allah's command; but when Allah's command comes, they are of no use at all.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: It is the ruler who seeks to guard himself against Allah, and those are the people of shirk (associating partners with Allah).
And Shuʿba narrated from Sharqī, from ʿIkrima, who said: They are the emirs.
So these are two views.
The third view: Ibn Jurayj said: It is like His saying ﴿عَنِ اليَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾: the one on the right writes the good deeds, and the one on the left writes the bad deeds.
And ﴿يَحْفَظُونَهُ﴾ means they record against him his speech and his deeds.
The most fitting of these views is the first, because of the high standing and soundness of its chain of transmission.
It is strengthened by the fact that Mālik ibn Anas narrated from Abū l-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah has angels who take turns among you by night and by day…" and he mentioned the ḥadīth.
And Shuʿba narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abū ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, regarding His saying ﴿إنَّ قُرْآنَ الفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُوداً﴾, that he said: They go round like guards — the angels of the night and the angels of the day.
And Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he recited: ﴿معقِّباتٌ﴾ «من بين يديه ورقباء من خلفه، من أمر الله يحفظونه» ("followers in turn before him and watchers behind him; by Allah's command they guard him").
So this has made the meaning clear.
And al-Ḥasan said concerning the meaning: they guard him by (ʿan) Allah's command. [This is close to the first, i.e. their guarding him is from Allah,] not from themselves.
And ʿAmr ibn Mālik narrated from Abū l-Jawzāʾ regarding His saying ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ — he said: the Prophet ﷺ.
And by this too he means the angels.
And it is reported from some of them that he recited «معاقيبُ من بين يديه ومن خلفه», and «معاقيب» is the plural of مُعَقِّب; its interpretation is like the interpretation of the first.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ مِّن دُونِهِ مِن وَالٍ﴾.
That is, there is no one to take charge of them apart from Allah.
And «وَالٍ» and وليّ are one and the same, just as one says قدير and قادر, and حفيظ and حافظ.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ ٱلْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, fear for the traveller and hope for the one at home.
The meaning is that the traveller fears the rain and is harmed by it.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿أذًى مِنْ مَطَرٍ﴾.
And the one at home is the one who benefits from the rain; he hopes for it when he sees the lightning.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيُنْشِىءُ ٱلسَّحَابَ ٱلثِّقَالَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Those in which there is rain.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيُسَبِّحُ ٱلرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Sālim, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: The thunder (al-raʿd) is an angel who glorifies.
And ʿUthmān ibn al-Aswad narrated from Mujāhid, who said: The thunder is an angel named "al-Raʿd." Do you not hear His saying: ﴿وَيُسَبِّحُ ٱلرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾?
And Sufyān narrated from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba, from Mujāhid, who said: The thunder is an angel who drives the clouds with his voice.
ʿIkrima said: The thunder is an angel who calls out to the clouds as the camel-driver calls out to the camels.
And it is narrated that Ibn ʿAbbās, when he heard the sound of thunder, used to say: "Glory be to the One for whom you have glorified."
And Mālik narrated from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, that when he heard the sound of thunder he would leave off his talk and say: "Glory be to the One whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him," then he would say: This is a severe warning to the people of the earth.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلصَّوَاعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِهَا مَن يَشَآءُ وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It is possible that the wāw is a wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He strikes with them whom He wills while he is in the state of disputing.
For it is narrated that Arbad asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: Tell us about our Lord — is He of copper or of iron? So Allah sent a thunderbolt which killed him.
And it is possible that His saying ﴿وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾ is cut off from (i.e. independent of) what precedes.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ ٱلْمِحَالِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, al-ḥawl (might).
Qatāda said: That is, al-ḥīla (stratagem).
Al-Ḥasan said: al-makr (devising/plotting).
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: That is, destruction.
These are views close to one another, and the one most resembling the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that it is destruction (al-ihlāk), because al-maḥl is severity, so it is as if the meaning were: severe in punishment and destruction.
A group of the people of language, among them "Abū ʿUbayda" and "Abū ʿUbayd," said: It is plotting (al-makr), from their saying مَحَلَ به ("he plotted against him"), and he recited the verse of al-Aʿshā:
فَرْعُ نَبْعٍ يَهْتَزُّ فِي غُصُنِ المَجْدِ * غَزِيرُ النَّدَى شَدِيدُ المِحَالِ.
(A branch of the nabʿ tree swaying on the bough of glory, abundant in generosity, severe in cunning/might.)
Abū ʿUbayd said: What best fits the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās is that he read «شديد المَحَال» with fatḥa on the mīm.
As for al-Aʿraj, what is known of his reading is «المَحَال» with fatḥa on the mīm.
And its meaning is like the meaning of al-ḥawl in their saying: لا حَوْلَ وَلاَ قوَّةَ إلاَّ باللهِ ("there is no might and no power except through Allah").
As for the meaning of plotting (makr) on the part of Allah: it is bringing what is hateful upon the one who deserves it from where he does not perceive.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُ دَعْوَةُ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "There is no god but Allah."
Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said likewise.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لاَ يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُم بِشَيْءٍ إِلاَّ كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى ٱلْمَآءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, he points to the water with his hand and calls it with his tongue.
Others said: That is, the one who calls upon idols is like one who grasps at water: nothing is gained by him.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَللَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً﴾.
It was said: whoever embraced Islam willingly, and whoever did not embrace Islam until his head was searched out by the sword, so that his entry was at first unwilling.
And it was said: this applies universally, because everyone who worships other than Allah only directs himself to what is great in his heart, and Allah is the Great, the Most Great.
Prostration (al-sujūd) in the language is submission and yielding, and there is nothing but that it submits to Allah and yields to Him.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَظِلالُهُم بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلآصَالِ﴾.
It is narrated that the unbeliever prostrates to other than Allah while his shadow prostrates to Allah, and this is of yielding and submission.
And it was said: the shadows (al-ẓilāl) here are the persons (bodies).

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ جَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ خَلَقُواْ كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ ٱلْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
That is, have they seen anyone other than Allah create the like of His creation, so that the creation became confusingly alike to them?!

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَنَزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Kathīr informed me, saying: I heard Mujāhid say: according to the measure of their filling.
Ibn Jurayj said: according to their smallness and their largeness.
Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read ﴿فَسَالَتْ أوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدْرِهَا﴾ (with sukūn on the dāl), and the meaning is the same.
And it was said: its meaning is "according to what was measured out for them."
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَٱحْتَمَلَ ٱلسَّيْلُ زَبَداً رَّابِياً﴾.
That is, rising up, high.
Mujāhid said: The statement is complete (here).
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي ٱلنَّارِ ٱبْتِغَآءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَاعٍ زَبَدٌ مِّثْلُهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The goods (al-matāʿ) are iron, copper and lead.
Others said: That which is heated in pursuit of ornament is gold and silver.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, as solidified (residue).
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ — may Allah have mercy on him — said: One says أجفأَتِ القِدْرُ ("the pot cast off its froth") when it boils until its froth runs out, and when it solidifies at its bottom.
Abū Zayd said: Ruʾba used to read ﴿فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَالاً﴾; one says جَفَلتِ الرِّيحُ السَّحَابَ when the wind breaks up the clouds and carries them off.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is the water, and this is a parable of truth and falsehood; i.e. the truth remains and is benefited from, and falsehood goes away and vanishes, just as this froth goes away, and like the going away of the dross of these things.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلأَمْثَالَ﴾.
The statement is complete (here).

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾.
Qatāda said: It is Paradise.
* And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ سُوۤءُ ٱلْحِسَابِ﴾.
Abū l-Jawzāʾ said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: meaning the close scrutiny of deeds.
This is indicated by the ḥadīth: "Whoever has his reckoning scrutinised is ruined."
Farqad said: Ibrāhīm said to me: O Farqad, do you know what the evil reckoning is? I said: No. He said: That the servant is taken to account for all of his sins, and nothing of them is forgiven him.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ﴾.
That is, whoever was righteous.
They do not enter it by lineage.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَالمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ﴾.
That is, as an honour from Allah to them.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُم بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ﴾.
That is, they say: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَىٰ ٱلدَّارِ﴾.
Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī said: ﴿فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّار﴾ — Paradise in place of the Fire.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا ٱلْحَيَاةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ إِلاَّ مَتَاعٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, it passes away.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِيۤ إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنَابَ﴾.
أناب (anāba): when he returns to obedience.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is, by affirming His oneness and by praising Him.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَلاَ بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ﴾.
That is, those which are the hearts of the believers.
Mujāhid said: Meaning the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ طُوبَىٰ لَهُمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Umāma said: «طُوبَى» is a tree in Paradise.
ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said likewise.
Mujāhid said: It is Paradise.
ʿIkrima said: That is, how excellent is what they have!
Ibrāhīm said: «طُوبَى» means good and honour.
These views are close to one another, because «طُوبَى» is of the pattern fuʿlā from al-ṭīb (goodness), i.e. of the good life for them, and these things all go back to the good thing.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, a place of return.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The unbelievers said to the Prophet ﷺ: Make the mountains move for us, cut the earth apart for us, bring the dead to life for us.
Mujāhid said: They said to the Prophet ﷺ: Move these mountains away from us, and pray for us that we may have crops, and bring Syria close to us, for we trade there, and bring the dead to life for us.
Qatāda said: Quraysh said to the Prophet: Bring the dead to life for us, so that we may ask them about what you have brought — is it true? So Allah sent down ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾.
He said: If this had been done for the People of the Book, it would have been done for you.
All these views require that the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, because the hearer knows it; for they asked, and their asking was an indication of the apodosis of (لو).
Its parallel is: ﴿لَوْ أنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أوْ آوِي إلَى رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾.
And the poet said:
فَلَوْ أنَّها نَفْسٌ تَمُوتُ سَوِيَّةً * وَلَكِنَّهَا نَفْسٌ تَسَاقَطُ أنْفُسَا
(If it were a soul that died all at once… but it is a soul that falls away soul by soul.)
So the apodosis of (لو) is omitted, i.e. "it would have found consolation."
Concerning what is omitted from the verse there are two views:
Most of the people of language hold that the meaning is: and if there were a Qurʾān by which the mountains were moved, or the earth cut apart, or the dead spoken to, it would be this Qurʾān.
Some of them said: the meaning is: if this were done for them, they still would not believe, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَا إلَيْهِمْ المَلاَئِكَةَ، وَكَلَّمَهُمُ المَوْتَى، وَحَشَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلاً، مَا كَانُوا لِيُؤْمِنُوا إلاَّ أنْ يَشَاءَ اللهُ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: [And it was said: in the statement there is] fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr), and the meaning is: and they disbelieve in the All-Merciful even if there were a Qurʾān by which the mountains were moved; i.e. they would disbelieve even if this happened.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ لَهَدَى ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is much disagreement concerning this verse.
Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim narrated from Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm, and ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read ﴿أفَلَمْ يَتَبَيَّن الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ — abridged. [Translator's note: the word «مختصر» ("abridged") stands as written in the source; the chain is also given as written, though it is usually "Yaʿlā ibn Ḥakīm from ʿIkrima".]
And in the book of Khārija, Ibn ʿAbbās read ﴿أفَلَمْ يَتَبَيَّنْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾.
And al-Minhāl ibn ʿUmayr narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾, i.e. "have they not known?"
Most of the people of language hold this view.
Among those who held it were Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and Abū ʿUbayda. Suḥaym ibn Wuthayl said:
أقُولُ لَهُمْ بِالشِّعْبِ إذْ يَيْسِرُونَنِي * ألَمْ تَيْأَسُوا أنِّي ابنُ فَارِسِ زَهْدَمِ
(I say to them in the mountain pass while they are dividing me up by lot: Do you not know that I am the son of the rider of Zahdam?)
And it is also narrated: إذْ يأسِرونني ("while they are taking me captive").
So the meaning of ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾ is: have they not known?
And Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾ — he said: have they not known? [Translator's note: the Arabic reads «معاوية بن صالح بن علي بن أبي طلحة», evidently for "Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa".]
There is another view on the verse:
Al-Kisāʾī said: I do not know this usage, nor have I heard anyone say يئستُ meaning "I knew"; rather, in my view it is from despair (al-yaʾs) itself. The meaning is: when the unbelievers asked for the mountains to be moved by the Qurʾān, the earth to be cut apart and the dead to be spoken to, the believers became eager for that and hoped that the unbelievers would be given it and so would believe. So Allah said: ﴿أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ﴾, i.e. have those who believe not despaired of the faith of these people, because they know that if Allah wished to guide them He would have guided them — as you say: "I have despaired of so-and-so ever succeeding," meaning: because of what I know of him.
* And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ تُصِيبُهُم بِمَا صَنَعُواْ قَارِعَةٌ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: Meaning the raiding parties (al-sarāyā).
ʿIkrima and ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said likewise, except that Abū ʿĀṣim narrated from Shabīb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the calamity.
Mujāhid said: qāriʿa means a raiding party and a misfortune that befalls them.
Al-qāriʿa in the language is the great misfortune.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيباً مِّن دَارِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid, ʿIkrima and Qatāda said: Or you, O Muḥammad, alight near their home.
Saʿīd ibn Mūsā narrated to us in Qarqīsiyā, saying: Makhlad ibn Mālik narrated to us from Muḥammad ibn Salama, from Khuṣayf, who said: al-qāriʿa is the raiding parties that the Messenger of Allah used to send out, or you, O Muḥammad, alight near their home.
Al-Ḥasan said: Or the qāriʿa alights near their home.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: That is, the conquest of Mecca.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَآئِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He is Allah, majestic is His majesty.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means Himself, Mighty and Majestic is He; He is the One who stands over His servants, whoever of them is righteous and whoever of them is wicked, providing for them and feeding them, while they have assigned partners to Allah.
Allah said: ﴿قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ﴾ — and if they named them they would be lying, and would be informing Him of what He does not know; and that is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مَّثَلُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱلَّتِي وُعِدَ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾.
Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl narrated from al-Khalīl, who said: «مَثَلُ» means "description" (ṣifa). On this basis the meaning is: the description of the Garden that the God-fearing were promised is that rivers flow beneath it — as you say: "the description of so-and-so is: dark-skinned," because its meaning is "so-and-so is dark-skinned."
Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: Allah has made a likeness for us of what is unseen by what we see, and such is the speech of the Arabs. So the meaning is: the likeness of the Garden that the God-fearing were promised is a garden beneath which rivers flow.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ مَآبِ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, to Him is the destination of every servant.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يَمْحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ وَيُثْبِتُ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read: ﴿وَيُثَبِّتُ﴾ (with shadda).
It is narrated from him: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, settles the affair of the year in the month of Ramaḍān, and He erases what He wills and confirms, except life and death, and wretchedness and happiness.
And in the narration of Abū Ṣāliḥ: ﴿يَمْحُواْ ٱللَّهُ﴾ — of what the recording angels have written — whatever is neither for the person nor against him, ﴿وَيُثْبِتُ﴾ what is for him and against him.
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿يَمْحُواْ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾ — he says: Allah replaces of the Qurʾān what He wills and abrogates it, and confirms what He wills and does not replace it.
﴿وَعِندَهُ أُمُّ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ — he says: the whole of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book, the abrogating and the abrogated. Qatāda said likewise.
Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿يَمْحُو اللهُ ما يَشَاءُ﴾ means He abrogates; and it is as though the meaning of ﴿ويُثْبِتُ﴾ in his view is: He does not abrogate it, so it is firmly established (muḥkam).
And «يُثَبِّت» with shadda is for intensity/multiplicity.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «وَيُثْبِت» without shadda is more comprehensive of these views than «يُثَبِّتُ».
Abū ʿUbayd had chosen ﴿وَيُثَبِّتُ﴾, though Abū Ḥātim indicated that their meaning is one.
And ʿAwf narrated from al-Ḥasan, who said: He erases whoever's term has come, and confirms whoever's term has not yet come, until his term.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن مَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلاَغُ وَعَلَيْنَا ٱلْحِسَابُ﴾.
That is, whether We show you some of what We promised you — the making of the religion of Islam prevail over all religion — ﴿أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾ before that, your duty is only to convey to them, and it is for Us to take them to account and requite them for their deeds.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made clear that what He promised came to be.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
So He said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا نَأْتِي ٱلأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾.
Islam prevails by taking away what is in the hands of the polytheists and by making the Muslims prevail over them.
There are several views on this verse, and this is the one most resembling the meaning.
Among the evidence for its correctness is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَلاَ يَرَوْنَ أنَّا نَأْتِي الأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أطْرَافِهَا أفَهُمُ الغَالِبُونَ﴾. This view is the position of al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
Salama ibn Nubayṭ narrated from him that he said, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا نَأْتِي ٱلأَرْضَ نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾: It is what was conquered of their lands.
And ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: It is the ruin of the earth until it is in one region of it, i.e. until habitation is in one region of it.
And Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid: ﴿نَنقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ — he said: death: the death of the jurists and the scholars.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لاَ مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ﴾.
Al-Khalīl said: There is none to repel His decree.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And the meaning is: there is no one who follows up His judgement with annulment or alteration.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿قُلْ كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujāhid: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām.
And Shuʿba said, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid: ﴿وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾ — He is Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He.
Sulaymān al-Taymī said: He is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām."
Qatāda said: Among them is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām," for he said: Qurʾān was revealed concerning me; then he recited: ﴿وَمَنْ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī and ʿIkrima rejected this view.
Al-Shaʿbī said: This verse was revealed before ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām embraced Islam.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima said: This verse was revealed in Mecca, so how could it have been revealed concerning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām?
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, Allah suffices as witness, and Allah — twice; he holds that (مَنْ) refers back to the name of Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the best of what has been said about this verse, for several reasons:
One of them: it is unlikely that Allah would call one of His creatures to witness.
Among them: what al-Shaʿbī and ʿIkrima objected.
Among them: it has been read ﴿وَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ عِلْمُ الكِتَابِ﴾ with kasra on the mīm, the dāl and the ʿayn. This is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, though there is weakness in the narration: Sulaymān ibn al-Arqam narrated it from al-Zuhrī ibn Sālim, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ read (ومِنْ عِنْدِهِ عِلْمُ). [Translator's note: «عن الزهري بن سالم» is as written; the chain is presumably "from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father".] And likewise it is narrated of Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr that they both read it so.
And there is no disagreement among the exegetes that the meaning is "and from Allah"; so that the meaning of the two readings be one is better.
And Maḥbūb narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī that he read: {وَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ عُلِمَ الكِتَابُ) with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the nominative on «الكتاب».
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of those who said it is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām" and others is also possible, because when the proofs are sound and those who have read the scriptures revealed before the Qurʾān recognise them, it is a confirmed matter.
And Allah knows best the truth of that.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤمۤر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾.
This is the end of the statement (tamām al-kalām).
And whoever holds that each of these letters conveys a meaning says: the meaning is "I am Allah; I see (anā Allāhu arā)."

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا﴾.
The meaning: you see them without pillars.
And the pronoun may refer back to the pillars [i.e. without pillars that you can see].
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ﴾.
That is, they are both subdued and governed; this is the meaning of taskhīr in the language.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي مَدَّ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
That is, He spread it out.
﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ﴾, i.e. mountains.
﴿وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَاتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾, i.e. two kinds; and every kind is a zawj (pair-member).

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُّتَجَاوِرَاتٌ﴾.
There are two views on this:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: He means the good [soil] and the bad, the salty marshes and the sweet.
And Mujāhid said the same.
The other view: that there is an omission (ḥadhf) in the speech, and the meaning is: and in the earth are neighbouring tracts and non-neighbouring ones; just as He said ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تقيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾, where the meaning is "and protect you from the cold", and that was omitted because the listener knows it.
﴿المُتَجَاوِرَاتُ﴾ are the cities and what is inhabited, and ﴿وغَيْرَ مُتَجَاوِرَاتٍ﴾ are the deserts and what is uninhabited.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَجَنَّاتٌ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾.
That is, and in it are gardens of grapevines.
﴿وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ﴾.
Abū Rajāʾ, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read ﴿صُنْوَانٌ﴾ with ḍamma on the ṣād.
Abū Isḥāq narrated from al-Barāʾ, who said: Al-ṣinwān is [palms] growing together, and "not ṣinwān" is those growing separately.
Zuhayr ibn Sharīk narrated to us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūnus narrated to us: Zuhayr ibn Muʿāwiya narrated to us: Abū Isḥāq said, from al-Barāʾ, concerning His saying ﴿صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ﴾: he said: Al-ṣinwān is what has a single root while being separate [above], and "not ṣinwān" is what grows alone. [Translator's note: the source prints «أصلحه», evidently for «أصله» (its root); translated accordingly.]
And so it is in the language: a palm tree that has another palm or more [growing from it] is called "ṣinwān", and when they are separate it is said: "not ṣinwān".
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُسْقَىٰ بِمَآءٍ وَاحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي ٱلأُكُلِ﴾.
That is, in fruit; i.e. they come out different, even though the air is one. So it is known that this is not because of the air, nor of nature, and that they have a Governor.
Sufyān narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي ٱلأُكُلِ﴾. He said: The sweet, the sour, the Persian [dates] and the poor-quality dates (al-daqal).

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإِن تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾.
That is, if you wonder at their denial of the resurrection after these proofs, then that is indeed something that ought to be wondered at.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: [They ask you to hasten] punishment before well-being.
Someone else said: He means their saying: ﴿اللهُمَّ إنْ كَانَ هَذَا هُوَ الحَقُّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ ٱلْمَثُلاَتُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the examples (al-amthāl).
Qatāda said: He means the exemplary punishments.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is more fitting, because it is well known in the language that a severe punishment is called mathula and muthla.
It is narrated from al-Aʿmash that he read ﴿المُثُلاَتُ﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm and the thāʾ. This too is the plural of (مُثْلة).
And it is narrated from him that he read ﴿المُثْلاَتُ﴾ with ḍamma on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ.
This too is the plural of (مُثْلة).
And (المُثْلاَتُ) [i.e. al-muthalāt] is permissible, a fatḥa being substituted for the ḍamma because of its heaviness.
It is also said: The fatḥa comes as a compensation for the hāʾ [of the feminine].
And it is also narrated from al-Aʿmash that he read ﴿المثْلاَتُ﴾ with fatḥa on the mīm and sukūn on the thāʾ; this is the plural of (مَثْلَة) — then the ḍamma was dropped because of its heaviness.
[Translator's note: the vowel signs in this passage are printed as given; the forms described in words (muthulāt, muthlāt, muthalāt, mathlāt) do not always match the vocalisation printed in the parentheses.]
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلْمِهِمْ﴾.
Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ ٱلْعِقَابِ﴾ was revealed, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Were it not for Allah's pardon, His mercy and His overlooking, no one's life would be pleasant; and were it not for His punishment, His threat and His chastisement, everyone would rely [on His forgiveness and neglect to act]."

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said — and this is the sense of their words: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ﴾ means the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾, i.e. a prophet who calls them.
Sufyān narrated from Abū al-Ḍuḥā: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ﴾ — he said: the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ — he said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ [— he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Ṣāliḥ said: The meaning is: for every people there is] a caller to guidance or a caller to misguidance.
What a group of the lexicographers hold is that the meaning is: when they demanded signs, Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that every people has a prophet who guides them and makes things clear to them, and that it is not incumbent on him to bring them whatever signs they demand.
Sufyān narrated from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ﴾ — he said: the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ﴾ — he said: Allah, exalted be His mention.
Sufyān narrated from al-Suddī, from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿اللهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِل كُلُّ أُنْثَى﴾. Sufyān said: He means whether male or female.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا تَغِيضُ ٱلأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: It is the child's falling short of nine months, and its exceeding them.
Qatāda said: [The wombs] fall short with the miscarried foetus, and exceed beyond the nine months.
Mujāhid said: Al-ghayḍ is decrease. When a woman sheds blood while pregnant, the child is diminished; and when she does not shed blood, the child grows large and complete.
[Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: When a woman becomes pregnant and then menstruates,] her child is diminished; then the pregnancy is lengthened for it by the amount [of time] the blood came to her.
ʿIkrima said: Al-ghayḍ is that the child is diminished by the coming of the blood, and the increase is that [the pregnancy] increases by the amount [of days] during which the blood came to her, until she completes nine months, apart from the days during which the blood came to her.

safi-cedvel:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(الكاف) a preposition of comparison [Note: The exegetes and grammarians differed over what the kāf is attached to. It was said that it is attached to the meaning contained in His words: "He leads astray whom He wills and guides…", i.e. just as Allah guided whoever turned in repentance, likewise We sent you. Al-ʿUkbarī attached the kāf to the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: "Thus is the matter: We sent you."], (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing word is أرسلناك; the reference is to the sending of the messengers; (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address. (أرسلنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn… and (نا) is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (في أمّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أرسلناك), i.e. "to a nation". (قد) a particle of realisation. (خلت) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters… and (التاء) is for the feminine. (من قبلها) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خلت)… and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (أمم) fāʿil of خلت, nominative (marfūʿ). (اللام) for causation. (تتلو) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تتلو). (الّذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (أوحينا) like أرسلنا. (إليك) like عليهم, attached to the verb أوحينا.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن تتلو..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أرسلناك).
(الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (circumstance). (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (يكفرون) an imperfect verb, nominative… and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (بالرّحمن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يكفرون). (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (هو) like هم. (ربّي) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ… and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi. (لا) the lā of generic negation. (إله) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative… and the khabar of lā is omitted, its implied form being "existent" (موجود). (إلّا) a particle of exception. (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, badal (substitute) for the pronoun concealed in the khabar. (عليه) like عليهم, attached to (توكّلت), a past verb with its fāʿil. (الواو) a conjunction. (إليه) like عليهم, attached to a fronted khabar. (متاب) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ that was dropped for lightness…
and the dropped (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. متابي.
The clause «أرسلناك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قد خلت.. أمم» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of أمّة.
The clause «تتلو ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «أوحينا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «هم يكفرون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «يكفرون ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو ربّي ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لا إله إلّا هو ...» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو) «1».
The clause «توكّلت ...» is in the position of nominative as a third khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو) «2».
The clause «إليه متاب ...» is in the position of [Translator's note: the source reads «في محلّ معطوفة», with the case word missing] conjoined to the clause توكّلت.

* Morphology:
(متاب): a mīmī maṣdar from تاب يتوب; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn. It contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution: its original form is متوب — with sukūn on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the wāw — then the wāw was made quiescent and its vowel transferred to the tāʾ before it, then the wāw was changed into an alif because the letter before it carries a fatḥa.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (أنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative — an abrogator (nāsikh) —. (قرآنا) the noun of أنّ, accusative (manṣūb). (سيّرت) a past verb, passive, and (التاء) is for the feminine. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (سيّرت); the bāʾ is causal. (الجبال) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (أو) a conjunction in both places. (قطّعت به الأرض، كلّم به الموتى) like سيّرت به الجبال…
and the sign of the nominative in الموتى is an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّ قرآنا ...) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, its implied form being ثبت ("it were established").
(بل) a particle of iḍrāb (digression). (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). (الأمر) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (جميعا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from الأمر; what governs it is the meaning of stability (istiqrār). (الهمزة) for interrogation. (الفاء) a conjunction. (لم) a particle of negation and jussive. (ييئس) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm). (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (آمنوا) a past verb with its fāʿil. (أن) lightened from the heavy form [Note: This is the view of the majority… Abū Ḥayyān chose that (أن) is redundant at the head of the clause answering an implied oath, the implied form being: "I swear that, if Allah willed, He would have guided…"], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted. (لو) like the first. (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (اللام) occurring in the answer of لو. (هدى) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif, and the fāʿil is "he". (الناس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (جميعا) a ḥāl from الناس, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنه) لو يشاء.. is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the verb ييئس, by its being made to carry the meaning of يعلم ("know") [Note: They said it is the dialect of Hawāzin, or of a clan of al-Nakhaʿ, in the sense of يعلم.].
(الواو) resumptive. (لا) negative. (يزال) an incomplete imperfect verb — an abrogator —. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the noun of لا يزال. (كفروا) a past verb with its fāʿil. (تصيبهم) an imperfect verb, nominative… and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الباء) a preposition. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, the clause after it being its ṣila (relative clause), with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e.: بما صنعوه.], (صنعوا) like كفروا. (قارعة) fāʿil of تصيبهم, nominative. (أو) a conjunction. (تحلّ) like تصيب, and the fāʿil is either القارعة or the pronoun of address directed to the Messenger, upon him be peace. (قريبا) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (تحلّ) — it is an adjective of an omitted noun qualified, i.e. "a near place" —. (من دارهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قريبا)… and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما صنعوا) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (تصيب).
(حتّى) a particle of extent and genitive. (يأتي) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى. (وعد) fāʿil, nominative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (تحلّ).
(إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative. (لا) negative. (يخلف) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "He". (الميعاد) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «(ثبت) تسير الجبال ...» [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic wording is سيّرت به الجبال] has no grammatical position: resumptive; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have believed" or "it would have been this Quran".
The clause «سيّرت به الجبال ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «قطّعت به الأرض ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause سيّرت.
The clause «كلّم به الموتى ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause قطّعت.
The clause «لله الأمر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ييئس الذين آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: "Were they heedless of the matter being Allah's, so that they did not know…"
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يشاء الله ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the lightened أن.
The clause «هدى ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the second non-jussive condition (لو).
The clause «لا يزال الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «تصيبهم.. قارعة» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of لا يزال.
The clause «صنعوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «تحلّ ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause تصيبهم.
The clause «يأتي وعد الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن), implied.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يخلف ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يخلف ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(قارعة): the feminine of قارع, the active participle of the triliteral قرع; its pattern is فاعل, and the feminine فاعلة.

* Rhetoric:
Concision (al-ījāz): in the words of the Exalted وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ to the end of the verse, since the answer of «لو» is omitted because the speech leads on to it. The exegetes and grammarians differed over its implied form: al-Zamakhsharī supplied it as «لما آمنوا به» ("they would not have believed in it"), but he regarded this as the weaker option and supplied the preferable one with his words «لكان هذا القرآن» ("it would have been this Quran").
- The grammarians differed over the implied form of the answer of «لو» in this verse and took various positions on it; what springs most quickly to mind from the context of the speech is that the answer is «لما آمنوا» ("they would not have believed"). So reflect, for supplying implied forms is a faculty of taste and good perception.

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of realisation. (استهزئ) a past verb, passive. (برسل) a preposition and its genitive noun, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (من قبلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استهزئ)… and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) a conjunction. (أمليت) a past verb with its fāʿil (agent). (اللام) a preposition. (الّذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (أمليت). (كفروا) a past verb with its fāʿil. (ثمّ) a conjunction. (أخذتهم) like أمليت… and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الفاء) a conjunction. (كيف) an interrogative noun carrying the meaning of threat and affirmation, the khabar (predicate) of the incomplete (كان). (عقاب) the noun of كان, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ that was dropped for lightness and for the verse-ending rhyme… and the dropped (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «استهزئ برسل ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied oath.
The clause «أمليت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the oath.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أخذتهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أمليت.
The clause «كان عقاب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أمليت [Note: It may be resumptive, after the resumptive fāʾ.].

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of disavowal (istifhām inkārī). (الفاء) resumptive. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "like one who is not so"…
(هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (قائم) khabar, nominative (marfūʿ). (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قائم). (نفس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (بما كسبت) like بما صنعوا [Note: In verse (31) of this sura.], and the fāʿil (agent) is "it" (هي), referring to النفس. (الواو) resumptive [Note: Or circumstantial, the clause after it being in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).], (جعلوا) like كفروا [Note: In the previous verse (32).], (الله) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is لله] a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of (شركاء), which is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). قل an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (سمّوهم) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn…
and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (أم) it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning "rather" (bal) plus the hamza. (تنبّئونه) an imperfect verb, nominative… and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الباء) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (تنبّئون). (لا) a negating particle. (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "He", and it is the returning pronoun. (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يعلم [Note: The first object is omitted, i.e. "He does not know it to be existent in the earth".], (أم) like the first. (بظاهر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being تسمّونهم ("you name them"). (من القول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (ظاهر). (بل) for iḍrāb (digression). (زيّن) a past verb, passive. (للذين كفروا) its i'rab has been given [Note: In the previous verse (32).], and the preposition is attached to (زيّن). (مكرهم) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative… and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (صدّوا) a past verb, passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma… and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (عن السبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (صدّوا). (الواو) resumptive. (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi. (يضلل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (الله) fāʿil, nominative. (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (ما) negative. (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a fronted khabar. (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. (هاد) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ; or it is the postponed noun of the ما that operates like ليس; the sign of the genitive is an implied kasra on its end because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ), and the yāʾ was dropped to accord with the tanwīn.
The clause «من هو قائم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هو قائم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «كسبت ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما), whether nominal or particle.
The clause «جعلوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.].
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سمّوهم ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «تنبّئونه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «(تسمّونهم) بظاهر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: (أم) may be connected (muttaṣila), so that it conjoins what follows it to the clause تنبّئونه ... or conjoins the prepositional phrase بظاهر to the prepositional phrase بما لا يعلم.].
The clause «زيّن.. مكرهم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «صدّوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause زيّن ...
The clause «يضلل الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما له من هاد ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(سمّوهم): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion to accord with the indeclinability on the sukūn; its original form is سميوهم; the yāʾ was dropped after its vowel was transferred to the mīm; its pattern is فعّوهم.

* Rhetoric:
(1) The interrogative of disavowal: in the words of the Exalted أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قائِمٌ عَلى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ the khabar is omitted, i.e. "like one who is not so", as a disavowal of that. The fāʾ is brought in to direct the disavowal at the delusion of likeness, and the khabar is omitted as an explicit rebuke and disparagement of them.
(2) Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun: in the words of the Exalted وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun, to state expressly His oneness in essence and in name, and to draw attention to His being exclusively deserving of worship, together with the clarification after vagueness that it contains.
3- Challenging to incapacity (al-taʿjīz): in the words of the Exalted قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ there is rebuke upon rebuke, i.e. name them: who are they and what are their names? In al-Baḥr: the meaning is that they are not among those who are mentioned and named; only one who benefits and harms is mentioned and named. This is like someone mentioning to you that a person is revered and honoured, while in your view he does not deserve that, so you say to the one who mentioned him: "Name him, so that I may show you his falseness and that he is far from deserving that."
4- Metonymy (al-kināya): in the words of the Exalted أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِما لا يَعْلَمُ فِي الْأَرْضِ, i.e. of partners deserving worship whom He, glorified and exalted, does not know; what is meant is to negate them by negating their necessary concomitant, by way of metonymy, because if He, glorified be He, does not know them — He from whose knowledge not an atom's weight in the earth or in the heaven escapes — then they have no reality at all.
5- Leading on step by step (al-istidrāj): by His words أَمْ بِظاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ, to urge them to reflection rather than speech devoid of thought, like His words in another place ذلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ and ما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَسْماءً سَمَّيْتُمُوها. This form of argument is among the most wondrous and powerful of styles.

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(لهم عذاب) like إليه متاب [Note: In verse (30) of this sura.], (في الحياة الدّنيا) its i'rab has been given [Note: In verse (26) of this sura.], and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب. (الواو) a conjunction. (اللام) the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), conveying emphasis. (عذاب) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (الآخرة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (أشقّ) khabar (predicate), nominative.
(الواو) a conjunction. (ما لهم من واق) like ماله من هاد [Note: In the previous verse (33).], (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (واق) [Note: Or attached to the fronted khabar.].
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لعذاب الآخرة أشقّ ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: The clause may possibly be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the third-person pronoun in (لهم), the link being implied, i.e. "harder for them"… or the wāw suffices, and what governs the ḥāl is the istiqrār (stability).].
The clause «ما لهم.. من واق» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(أشقّ): an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral شقّ; its pattern is أفعل; its ʿayn and lām have been assimilated, so they are a single letter.
(واق): the active participle of the triliteral وقى; its pattern is فاع, so it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ), and to accord with the tanwīn.

* Benefits:
(1) The reader finds in these verses repeated dropping of the yāʾ, in observance of the verse-endings (fawāṣil) and the cadence of the speech.
But the dropping mentioned is not of one kind. In the word «عقاب» the yāʾ of the speaker was dropped, and the reader supplies it from the context of the speech; in the two words «هاد» and «واق» the yāʾ that belongs to the root of the word was dropped, and the reason for its dropping is the meeting of two quiescent letters: «the tanwīn and the quiescent yāʾ at the end of the defective noun. When pausing at the ends of the verses, the desired cadence is obtained, which we notice always and ever in the arrangement of the Noble Quran. It is one of the factors of its inimitability and eloquence.

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(مثل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (الجنّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr)… and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "is in what We relate" or "what We recite". (الّتي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الجنّة. (وعد) a past verb, passive. (المتّقون) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "was promised it". (تجري) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ. (من تحتها) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تجري) [Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأنهار.]… and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الأنهار) fāʿil (agent), nominative. (أكلها) mubtadaʾ, nominative… and (ها) like the last. (دائم) khabar, nominative. (الواو) a conjunction. (ظلّها) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أكلها [Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the conjunction being one of clauses.], (تلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the sukūn, overt on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters… and (اللام) is for distance, and (الكاف) for address; the reference is to the Garden. (عقبى) khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma on the alif. (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (اتّقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters… and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (الواو) a conjunction. (عقبى) mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being as in the first. (الكافرين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ. (النار) khabar, nominative.
The clause «مثل الجنّة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «وعد المتّقون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (التي).
The clause «تجري.. الأنهار ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the implied returning pronoun, i.e. "the God-fearing were promised it, with rivers flowing beneath it".].
The clause «أكلها دائم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl of the implied returning pronoun, i.e. "its food being perpetual".].
The clause «تلك عقبى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «عقبى الكافرين النار ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تلك عقبى..

* Morphology:
(دائم): the active participle of the triliteral دام; its pattern is فاعل. It contains the change of the weak letter into a hamza because its verb is weak, hollow (ajwaf); its original form is دوام — the alif's origin is wāw; its imperfect is يدوم —.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (الّذين) a relative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (آتيناهم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn… and (نا) is the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الكتاب) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (يفرحون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ)…
and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (الباء) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفرحون). (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it", and it is the returning pronoun. (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل). (الواو) a conjunction. (من الأحزاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (ينكر) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he", and it is the returning pronoun. (بعضه) mafʿūl bihi, accusative… and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (أمرت) like أنزل… and (التاء) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle. (أعبد) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is "I". (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو) a conjunction. (لا) negative. (أشرك) like أعبد and conjoined to it. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أشرك).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن أعبد..) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, governed by أمرت.
(إليه) like به, attached to (أدعو), which is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw. (الواو) a conjunction. (إليه) like به, attached to a fronted khabar. (مآب) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ that was dropped for lightness… and the dropped (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «الذين آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يفرحون ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «أنزل إليك ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «من الأحزاب من ينكر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ينكر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أمرت ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «أعبد ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «لا أشرك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أعبد.
The clause «أدعو ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the speech [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of أشرك.].
The clause «إليه مآب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إليه أدعو.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(المر) disconnected letters (ḥurūf muqaṭṭaʿa) with no grammatical position «[Note: see the first verse of Sūrat al-Baqara.]»; (تلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn that is overt on the yāʾ, which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the reference is to all the verses of the Quran or to the verses of the surah ... and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (آيات) a khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (الكتاب) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is "it" (هو); (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (من ربّك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزل) «[Note: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الحقّ) — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies —]», and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الحقّ) the khabar of the relative mubtadaʾ «[Note: it may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it" (هو) ... and in that case (الذي أنزل ...) is parsed as conjoined to (آيات الكتاب), which is a badal (substitute) from (تلك) — or a naʿt (adjective) of it — and the clause «هو الحقّ» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (تلك).]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) making the noun accusative — abrogating (nāsikh) —; (أكثر) the noun of lākinna, accusative (manṣūb); (النّاس) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا) negative; (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and (الواو) the fāʿil (agent).
The clause «تلك آيات ...» has no grammatical position, being initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «الّذي أنزل ... الحقّ» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the initial clause.
The clause «أنزل إليك ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «لكنّ أكثر ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «الذي أنزل ... الحقّ».
The clause «لا يؤمنون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

* Benefits:
- We have stated our view earlier about the opening of some surahs with letters such as these, so refer back to it in its places.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (كذلك أنزلناه) like كذلك أرسلناك [Note: In verse (30) of this sura.], (حكما) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), from the third-person pronoun, i.e. "as a judge". (عربيّا) a naʿt (adjective) of (حكما), accusative [Note: Or a second ḥāl, accusative — al-Jamal in his gloss —.], (الواو) resumptive. (اللام) paving the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam). (إن) a jussive conditional particle. (اتّبعت) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ)… and (التاء) is the fāʿil (agent). (أهواءهم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative… and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (بعد) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اتّبعت).
