(ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (جاءك) a past verb… and (الكاف) is the mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "it", and it is the returning pronoun. (من العلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl of the returning pronoun. (مالك ... ولا واق) the i'rab of its like has been given [Note: In verse (33) of this sura.], and (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation. (واق) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to وليّ, taking its i'rab.
The clause «أنزلناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إن اتّبعت ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاءك من العلم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «ما لك.. من وليّ» has no grammatical position: the answer of the oath… and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.

* Benefits:
- The parser asks: why is the clause ما لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا واقٍ not joined with the fāʾ? The answer to that: an oath and a condition have come together in the verse, and the oath precedes the condition, so the answer belongs to the one that comes first. As for the apodosis of the condition, the answer of the oath indicates it, and the answer of the oath does not require that it be linked with the fāʾ. So return to this discussion in its proper places, for we have given it its due there.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of realisation. (أرسلنا) a past verb with its fāʿil (agent). (رسلا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من قبلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (جعلنا) like أرسلنا. (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (جعلنا) [Note: Or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of (جعلنا).], (أزواجا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (ذرّيّة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (أزواجا) by the wāw, accusative. (الواو) a conjunction. (ما) negative. (كان) an incomplete past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) —. (لرسول) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of كان. (أن يأتي) like أن أعبد [Note: In verse (36) of this sura.], (بآية) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي). (إلّا) exception. (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted word excepted from the most general of states. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يأتي..) is in the position of nominative as the noun of كان.
(لكلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar. (أجل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (كتاب) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
The clause «أرسلنا رسلا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied oath.
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the oath.
The clause «ما كان لرسول ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause answering the oath [Note: Or conjoined to the implied resumptive oath clause.].
The clause «لكلّ أجل كتاب ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya), or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(يمحو) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "He". (الواو) a conjunction. (يثبت) like يشاء. (الواو) a conjunction. (عنده) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate)…
and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (أمّ) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يمحو الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يثبت ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «عنده أمّ الكتاب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of يمحو and يثبت.].

* Rhetoric:
- The figure of istikhdām (double-sense employment): in the words of the Exalted لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتابٌ يَمْحُوا اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ وَعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتابِ. This figure is a lofty one among the figures of rhetoric; the scholars of this art called it «the figure of istikhdām» and defined it with definitions not free of obscurity. As for its definition as given by Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ, Ibn Munqidh and the author of Nihāyat al-Arab, it is: that the speaker brings a word that has two senses, then brings two words between which that word stands in the middle, and each of the two words employs one of the two senses of the middle word. In the verse mentioned, the word «كتاب» can mean the fixed term, as evidenced by the words of the Exalted حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتابُ أَجَلَهُ, i.e. its term — the term of the waiting period — and its أجل is its end; and [it can mean] the written thing. The word كتاب stands in the middle between the two words «أجل» and «يمحو»: the word أجل employs one of its two senses, namely the term, and the word يمحو employs its other sense, namely the written thing. So the implied meaning on that basis is: for every fixed limit there is something written that is erased and confirmed.

* Benefits:
- This verse was revealed in reply to those among the polytheists who rejected abrogation (naskh) and took it as a means of attacking the Quran and defaming the Messenger ﷺ. He refuted their claims, making clear that change, as the jurists say, occurs in the branches (furūʿ), whose rulings are not denied to change with the change of time and place.
They revolve in the orbit of the general benefit and the interests of the people.
As for the fixed aims and the general principles, they are what remains everlasting, untouched by alteration or change, and they are what is referred to by «أم الكتاب». So contemplate the understanding of this religion — may Allah protect us and you from slips and delusions.

safi-cedvel:40-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (إن) a jussive conditional particle, assimilated with ما, and (ما) is redundant (zāʾida). (نرينّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (النون) is for emphasis, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is "We", for majesty. (بعض) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (نعدهم) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ)… and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "We", for majesty. (أو) a conjunction. (نتوفّينّك) like نرينّك and conjoined to it. (الفاء) causal. (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (على) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate). (البلاغ) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (الواو) a conjunction. (علينا الحساب) like عليك البلاغ.
The clause «نرينّك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive… and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then that will heal you".
The clause «نعدهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «نتوفّينّك ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause… and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then there is no blame on you".
The clause «عليك البلاغ ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «علينا الحساب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the causal clause.
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of disavowal (istifhām inkārī). (الواو) a conjunction. (لم) a particle of negation and jussive. (يروا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn… and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (أنّا) a particle of emphasis and accusative… and (نا) is the noun of أن. (نأتي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "We", for majesty. (الأرض) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (ننقصها) like نأتي… and (ها) is mafʿūl bihi. (من أطرافها) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ننقصها), and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) resumptive. (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (يحكم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "He". (لا) the lā of generic negation. (معقّب) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative. (لحكمه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of lā…
and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (سريع) khabar, nominative. (الحساب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «لم يروا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نرينّك.
The clause «نأتي ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أنّا نأتي..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يروا.
The clause «ننقصها ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of نأتي, or of its object.
The clause «الله يحكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, carrying the force of causation.
The clause «يحكم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «لا معقّب لحكمه ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "His judgement being effective".
The clause «هو سريع ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الله يحكم.

* Morphology:
(معقّب): the active participle of the quadriliteral عقّب; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
- Shift of person (al-iltifāt): in the words of the Exalted أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ there is a shift from the first person to the third person. Building the judgement upon the Majestic Name indicates grandeur, cultivates awe, and confirms the content of the statement, by pointing to the cause which is the reason for coming to the land and diminishing its extremities, and for transferring dominance from yesterday's oppressors to the oppressed, and from yesterday's victors to the vanquished. This grandeur is attainable only by presenting the speech in the mode of the third person.

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (قد) a particle of realisation. (مكر) a past verb. (الذين) a relative in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). (من قبلهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative… and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition. (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate). (المكر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (جميعا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb). (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "He". (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the clause after it being its ṣila, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. تكسبه.] (تكسب) like يعلم. (كلّ) fāʿil, nominative. (نفس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) a conjunction. (السين) a particle of the future. (يعلم) like the first. (الكفّار) fāʿil, nominative. (اللام) a preposition. (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (عقبى) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif. (الدار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «مكر الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لله المكر ...» is in the position of [Translator's note: the source reads «في محلّ جواب شرط», with the case word missing] the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if they plot, then to Allah belongs the plotting" [Note: It may be causal (taʿlīliyya) for implied speech, i.e.: "Their plotting is of no account, for to Allah belongs the plotting."].
The clause «يعلم ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «تكسب كلّ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (ما تكسب ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «سيعلم الكفّار ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قد مكر الذين ...
The clause «لمن عقبى الدار ...» is in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of the verb of knowing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative (من).

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (الذين) a relative in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). (كفروا) a past verb with its fāʿil. (لست) an incomplete, inflexible (jāmid) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn… and (التاء) is the noun of ليس. (مرسلا) khabar (predicate), accusative (manṣūb). (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (كفى) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif. (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. (الله) the Name of Majesty, genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil of كفى. (شهيدا) a tamyīz (specification), accusative [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative.], (بيني) an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (شهيدا), the sign of the accusative being an implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ… and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو) a conjunction. (بينكم) like the first and conjoined to it. (الواو) a conjunction. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, conjoined to the position of the Name of Majesty. (عنده) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar… and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (علم) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «يقول الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لست مرسلا ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كفى بالله ...» is in the position of accusative as the maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «عنده علم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).

safi-cedvel:2-4.t:
* I'rab:
(الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (الّذي) a relative, the khabar (predicate) «[Note: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty.. and the clause «يدبّر الأمر» the khabar of the Name of Majesty.]»; (رفع) a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being "He" (هو); (السّموات) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), its sign of the accusative being the kasra; (بغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (السموات), i.e. "free of pillars" «[Note: or "not resting upon anything".]»; (عمد) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (ترونها) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) the fāʿil, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi «[Note: it refers either to the heavens or to the pillars.. and the i'rab of the clause «ترونها» differs according to what the pronoun refers to.]»; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (استوى) is like (رفع), the fatḥa being implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (على العرش) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استوى); (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (سخّر الشّمس) is like (رفع السموات); (القمر) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (الشمس) by the wāw, accusative; (كلّ) a mubtadaʾ, nominative «[Note: the indefinite here indicates generality, and the muḍāf ilayhi is implied, i.e. "each heavenly body".]»; (يجري) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, the fāʿil being "it" (هو); (لأجل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يجري); (مسمّى) a naʿt of (أجل), genitive, its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif; (يدبّر) an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil being "He" (هو), i.e. Allah; (الأمر) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (يفصّل الآيات) is like (يدبّر الأمر), and the sign of the accusative of the object is the kasra; (لعلّكم) a particle of hope (tarajjī) making the noun accusative — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of laʿalla; (بلقاء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (توقنون); (ربّكم) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (توقنون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and (الواو) the fāʿil.
The clause «الله الذي رفع ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «رفع ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الّذي).
The clause «ترونها ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from (السموات) «[Note: the ḥāl is anticipated (muqaddara), because we were not created at the time of the raising. It may also be resumed, and then it has no grammatical position ...
If the pronoun in (ترونها) refers to the pillars, the clause is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of (عمد).]».
The clause «استوى ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «رفع»..
The clause «سخّر ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «رفع»..
The clause «كلّ يجري ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the object of (سخّر).
The clause «يجري ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ).
The clause «يدبّر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: it may be a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «استوى على العرش» ... and likewise the clause «يفصّل»..]».
The clause «يفصّل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لعلّكم ... توقنون» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «توقنون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of laʿalla.
(الواو) a conjunction; (هو الّذي مدّ الأرض) is like (الله الذي رفع السموات)..
(الواو) a conjunction; (جعل) is like (رفع); (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (جعل); (رواسي) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (أنهارا) conjoined to (رواسي) by the wāw; (الواو) a conjunction; (من كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جعل) «[Note: it may be attached to a ḥāl from (اثنين) — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies.]»; (الثمرات) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (جعل) is like (رفع); (فيها) is like the first one, attached to (جعل); (زوجين) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (اثنين) a naʿt of (زوجين), accusative like it, and it is treated like the dual; (يغشي) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma, the fāʿil being "He" (هو), i.e. Allah; (الليل) a mafʿūl bihi «[Note: or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the implied form being "He covers the day with the night" (يغشي النهار بالليل).]», accusative; (النهار) a second mafʿūl bihi; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (في) a preposition; (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted element which is the khabar of inna.. and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (اللام) for emphasis; (آيات) the noun of inna, accusative, its sign of the accusative being the kasra; (لقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (آيات); (يتفكّرون) is like (توقنون).
The clause «هو الّذي ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «الله الذي رفع».
The clause «مدّ ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الّذي).
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «جعل (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first clause «جعل».
The clause «يغشي ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of (مدّ) «[Note: it may be cut off as a resumption.. and then it has no grammatical position.]».
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يتفكّرون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of (قوم).
(الواو) a conjunction; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; (قطع) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (متجاورات) a naʿt of (قطع), nominative; (الواو) a conjunction in the four following places; (جنّات، زروع، نخيل) words conjoined to (قطع) by the conjunctions, nominative; (من أعناب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (جنّات); (صنوان) a naʿt of (نخيل), nominative; (غير) conjoined to (صنوان) by the wāw, nominative; (صنوان) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (يسقى) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), i.e. what has been mentioned of the gardens, crops and palms; (بماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسقى); (واحد) a naʿt of (ماء), genitive; (الواو) a conjunction; (نفضّل) an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil being "We" (نحن), for majesty; (بعضها) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi; (على بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نفضّل); (في الأكل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from (بعضها); (إنّ في ذلك ... يعقلون) is like (إن في ذلك ... يتفكّرون).
The clause «في الأرض قطع ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «يسقى ...» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of the kinds that were mentioned.
The clause «نفضّل ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «في الأرض قطع».
The clause «إنّ في ذلك ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يعقلون ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of (قوم).

* Morphology:
(عمد): plural of عماد — irregularly — because its regular plural would be عمد with two ḍammas; a primitive (jāmid) noun for a stone of whatever shape. عمد — with two fatḥas — may also be a collective noun (ism jamʿ).
(رواسي): plural of رأس «[Translator's note: so written in the source; the singular meant is راس / الراسي, as what follows shows.]», a name for a mountain; it is originally an active participle from the defective (nāqiṣ) رسا, its pattern being فاعل. The weak letter has been dropped because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ), on account of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and without the dropping, (الراسي) contains a vowel-change (iʿlāl) by substitution, because the last radical of the word is wāw, from the verb رسا يرسو; its origin is (الراسو) with kasra on the sīn.. then (الواو) was changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it.
(قطع): see verse (27) of Sūrat Yūnus.
(متجاورات): plural of متجاورة, the feminine of متجاور, an active participle from the five-letter تجاور; its pattern is متفاعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(زرع): a name for what is sown, coming in the form of the maṣdar (verbal noun); its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(صنوان): plural of صنو, a noun originally meaning a full brother, and here a shoot of the palm-tree; its pattern is فعل with kasra or fatḥa on the fāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the pattern described fits صنوان (فعلان) rather than فعل.]». It has another plural, أصناء.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Metaphor (al-istiʿāra): in the saying of the Exalted «اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ», i.e. supports. What is meant here is the power of Allah the Exalted, and it is He who holds the sky from falling upon the earth; on this view the pillars are a metaphor.
(2) Negating a thing by affirming it (nafy al-shayʾ bi-ījābih): in the saying of the Exalted «بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها», i.e. He raised the heavens free of pillars; the sense is the negation of both the pillars and the seeing together: there is no seeing and no pillars.

* Benefits:
- His saying in the third verse «جَعَلَ فِيها زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ»: mention of pairing recurs in the Noble Quran, whether in the human world or the plant world. In this there are decisive proofs of the existence of the Powerful, All-Knowing God who orders the affairs of this universe. One contemporary philosopher said: the existence of pairing in living things is a proof of the existence of God, and even greater as a proof is its existence in plants, which neither reason nor think, but rather submit to laws dictated to them by the Originating Creator; and it cannot possibly come about by chance under any circumstance.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إن) a particle of condition making the verb jussive; (تعجب) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil (agent) being "you" (أنت); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (عجب) a fronted khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (قولهم) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative.. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الهمزة) for interrogation; (إذا) an adverb of future time not containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element whose implied form is "shall we be raised" (أنبعث) — or — "shall we be gathered" (أنحشر); (كنّا) a deficient past verb.. and (نا) a pronoun, the noun of kāna; (ترابا) a khabar, accusative (manṣūb); (الهمزة) is like the first one; (إنّنا) a particle of emphasis making the noun accusative — abrogating (nāsikh) — and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (اللام) for emphasis; (في خلق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna; (جديد) a naʿt (adjective) of (خلق), genitive (majrūr); (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as khabar; (كفروا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (بربّهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كفروا).. and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (أولئك) is like the first one; (الأغلال) a second mubtadaʾ, nominative; (في أعناقهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ.. and (هم) is like the last one; (الواو) a conjunction; (أولئك) is like the first one; (أصحاب) the khabar of (أولئك), nominative; (النار) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (خالدون), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم), nominative, its sign of the nominative being (الواو).
The clause «إن تعجب ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «عجب قولهم..» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كنّا ترابا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi ... and the adverb and the clause after it are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of (قولهم).
The clause «إنّا لفي خلق ...» has no grammatical position, being explicative (tafsīriyya) of the content of what the adverb (إذا) is attached to.
The clause «أولئك الّذين ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الّذين).
The clause «أولئك ... (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أولئك الذين»..
The clause «الأغلال في أعناقهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «أولئك أصحاب ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause «أولئك»..
The clause «هم فيها خالدون ...» is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of (أولئك) «[Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (أصحاب), its governing word being the demonstrative.]».

* Morphology:
(جديد): an adjective resembling the participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the verb جدّ يجدّ, of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:6-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (يستعجلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الواو) the fāʿil (agent); (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بالسيّئة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يستعجلون); (قبل) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (السيّئة); (الحسنة) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (خلت) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because the sukūn of the tāʾ met the sukūn of the alif.. and (التاء) is for the feminine; (من قبلهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خلت)..
and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (المثلات) a fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) a conjunction; (إنّ) a particle of emphasis making the noun accusative — abrogating (nāsikh) —; (ربّك) the noun of inna, accusative.. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (ذو) a khabar (predicate), nominative, its sign of the nominative being the wāw; (مغفرة) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مغفرة); (على ظلمهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl from (الناس) whose governing word is (مغفرة).. and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (إنّ ... لشديد) is like (إنّ ... لذو); (العقاب) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «يستعجلونك ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أولئك الذين» «[Note: in the previous verse (5).]».
The clause «خلت.. المثلات» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl «[Note: it may be resumptive after a resumptive wāw, with no grammatical position.]».
The clause «إنّ ربّك لذو ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «يستعجلونك».
The clause «إنّ ربّك لشديد ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the previous clause.
(الواو) a conjunction; (يقول) an imperfect verb, nominative; (الّذين) a relative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; (كفروا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) in the sense of "why not" (هلّا); (أنزل) a past verb, passive; (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (أنزل); (آية) the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (من ربّه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (آية).. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّما) the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (منذر) a khabar, nominative; (الواو) a conjunction; (لكلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a fronted khabar; (قوم) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (هاد) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the omitted alif «[Translator's note: so in the source; the omitted letter of هاد is a yāʾ, as the Morphology section below states.]», for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ) «[Note: and it is the adjective of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "a guiding prophet" (نبيّ هاد).]».
The clause «يقول ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «إنّ ربّك لذو».
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أنزل.. آية» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّما أنت منذر» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لكلّ قوم هاد» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أنت منذر».

* Morphology:
(المثلات): plural of المثلة, a name for an exemplary, disgracing punishment; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and ḍamma on the ʿayn, and the pattern of مثلات is فعلات, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and ḍamma on the ʿayn.
(هاد): an active participle from the triliteral هدى; its pattern is فاع. It contains a vowel-change (iʿlāl) by deletion, for it is defective (manqūṣ): its yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

* Benefits:
1- ذو: it is one of the five nouns — some count them as six — which are: أب، أخ، حم، فم، ذو, and the sixth is «الهن».
a- There are three views on their declension:
1- The preferred view: they are nominative with the wāw, accusative with the alif and genitive with the yāʾ.
2- The second, «less preferred» view: they are declined like the abbreviated noun (ism maqṣūr), the alif always remaining at their end.
3- Some of the Arabs held that they are declined with the vowels like other nouns.
b- The conditions for their declension with letters:
that the noun be singular, that it be in construct (muḍāf), and that it be annexed to something other than the yāʾ of the first person.
c- If the five nouns are put in the dual they are declined like the dual: with the alif in the nominative and with the yāʾ in the accusative and genitive.
If they are put in the plural they are declined like the broken plural, with the vowels — except ذو, which is declined like the sound masculine plural, because it is treated like it. If they are annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, they are declined with vowels implied on the letter before the yāʾ, because the place is occupied by the vowel of harmony. «ذو» alone among the five nouns may come as a relative; it also comes for pointing, and comes in the sense of "possessor" (صاحب), and each is discussed in its place. So do not be hasty.
2- Among the characteristics of our Arabic language is «inversion» (al-qalb), and it is of two kinds:
a- Inversion in predication, and from it is «يجعلون الأغلال في أعناقهم والقيود في أيديهم» ("they put the fetters on their necks and the shackles on their hands").
This is contrary to reality, because it is the necks that are in the fetters and the hands that are in the shackles, and not the reverse that is correct.
b- Inversion in the letters, like خيرزان and خيزران, and سجادة and سداجة.
It has many parallels in verbs and nouns.
Remark: there is a kind of conversion (iqlāb) that occurs in the recitation of the Noble Quran, in which the quiescent nūn or the nunation is changed into a mīm in particular places; its place is the science of tajwīd, so whoever wishes should consult it there.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil (agent) being "He" (هو); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Note: it may be a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar the mafʿūl bihi.. They also allowed it to be an interrogative noun governed by the verb (تحمل) — as its mafʿūl bihi — and the clause «تحمل» governed by the verb of knowing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.]», and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted; (تحمل) is like (يعمل) «[Translator's note: so in the source; (يعلم) is evidently meant.]»; (كلّ) a fāʿil, nominative; (أنثى) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) a conjunction; (ما تغيض الأرحام وما تزداد) is like (ما تحمل كلّ أنثى), and the fāʿil of (تزداد) is a pronoun whose implied form is "it" (هي); (الواو) a conjunction; (كلّ) a mubtadaʾ, nominative; (شيء) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (عنده) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (كلّ) or of (شيء) «[Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (مقدار), or attached to the "being settled" (istiqrār) which is the khabar.]», and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بمقدار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (كلّ).
The clause «الله يعلم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «تحمل كلّ ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «تغيض الأرحام ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «تزداد ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative (ما).
The clause «كلّ شيء ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(مقدار): it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of power (القدرة) or in the sense of measure (القدر) — with sukūn on the dāl — and it may be a name for that by which the measure of a thing is known, whether counted, measured by volume or weighed. Its pattern is مفعال, with kasra on the mīm, and its plural is مقادير, of the pattern مفاعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): in the saying of the Exalted «اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثى وَما تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحامُ وَما تَزْدادُ», i.e. what they decrease and increase.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(عالم) the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "He" (هو) «[Note: or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الكبير).]»; (الغيب) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction; (الشهادة) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (الغيب), genitive; (الكبير) a second khabar, nominative (marfūʿ); (المتعال) a third khabar, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, which was dropped for lightness or to match the verse-endings (fawāṣil).
The clause «هو عالم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(المتعال): an active participle from the five-letter verb تعالى; its pattern is متفاعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. The dropped (الياء) is converted from a wāw; its origin is المتعالو — with kasra on the lām — because its bare form is علا يعلو.. then the wāw was changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. The word has been written in the Muṣḥaf with the yāʾ dropped, for lightness, and the yāʾ may be pronounced when pausing.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(سواء) a fronted khabar (predicate) «[Note: or a mubtadaʾ qualified by his saying (منكم), and the khabar is (من أسرّ)..]», nominative (marfūʿ); (من) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (سواء), which is in the sense of "equal" (مستو); (من) a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), in the position of the nominative; (أسرّ) a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being "he" (هو), and it is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid); (القول) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) a conjunction; (من جهر) is like (من أسرّ) and is conjoined to it; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (جهر); (الواو) a conjunction; (من) is like the first one and is conjoined to it; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (مستخف) a khabar, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a nunated defective noun (ism manqūṣ); (بالليل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مستخف); (الواو) a conjunction; (سارب بالنهار) is like (مستخف بالليل).
The clause «سواء ... من أسرّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أسرّ ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (من).
The clause «جهر به ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «هو مستخف ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the third relative (من).

* Morphology:
(مستخف): an active participle from the six-letter (استخفى); its pattern is مستفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. The yāʾ was dropped — its origin is المستخفي — because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, on account of the nunation.
(سارب): an active participle from the triliteral (سرب); its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Hyperbole (al-mubālagha): in the saying of the Exalted «وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ», one who goes to extremes in hiding, as though he hides (in the night) and seeks yet more. Secrecy and hiding are put first to show the perfection of His knowledge, the Exalted, as though in relating to hidden things it is prior to its relating to manifest ones; otherwise its relation to all is equal.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); (معقّبات) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (من بين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (معقّبات); (يديه) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (من خلفه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what the previous prepositional phrase is attached to, so it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it.. and (الهاء) is like the last one; (يحفظون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) the fāʿil (agent), and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من أمر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحفظون); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّ) a particle of emphasis making the noun accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (لا) negative; (يغيّر) an imperfect verb, nominative, the fāʿil being "He" (هو); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (بقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (يغيّروا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after (حتّى), its sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) the fāʿil; (ما بأنفسهم) is like (ما بقوم).. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يغيّروا..) is in the position of the genitive by (حتّى), attached to (يغيّر).
(الواو) a conjunction; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, attached to the content of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) «[Note: the implied form of the speech is: "When Allah wills evil for a people, it befalls" or "it is not turned back" — with the verb in the passive —]»; (أراد) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (بقوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (سوءا), which is a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (مردّ) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative; (له) is like the first one, attached to the khabar of lā; (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) a negating particle; (لهم) is like (له), attached to a fronted khabar; (من دونه) is like (من خلفه), attached to a ḥāl from (وال); (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (وال) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ, its sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).
The clause «له معقّبات ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحفظونه ...» is in the position of the nominative as another naʿt of (معقّبات) «[Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from (معقّبات), because it is qualified.]».
The clause «إنّ الله لا يغيّر ...» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا يغيّر ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «يغيّروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «أراد ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا مردّ له ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ما لهم ... من وال» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.

* Morphology:
(معقّبات): plural of معقّبة, the feminine of معقّب, an active participle from the four-letter عقّب; its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(مردّ): a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun) from the triliteral (ردّ); its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn, because its ʿayn in the imperfect has ḍamma.
(وال): an active participle from the triliteral ولي; its pattern is فاع, and it contains a vowel-change (iʿlāl) by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, on account of the nunation.

* Benefits:
1- The saying of the Exalted: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ».
This verse has become proverbial, but people have understood its purport in different ways.
Most likely the preferable of its many interpretations are two:
a- One of them, which is the one that first strikes the mind, is that people are in one of the forms of harm and evil, so they cry out with supplications to Allah that He lift from them the calamity of evil. The verse reminds them that they must first reform themselves, and consequently Allah will set their affairs right for them.
b- The interpretation opposite to this is that people are in blessing and good, and when their souls change and become ungrateful for His blessings, the Exalted, Allah announces that He will take away His blessings from them, and exchange for them prosperity with adversity, and abundant good with grievous evil.
So seek leave in your understanding and choose in your opinion; every one who exerts effort (mujtahid) has a share of reward.

safi-cedvel:12-13.t:
* I'rab:
(هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate); (يريكم) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ.. and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being "He" (هو); (البرق) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (خوفا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object in (يريكم) «[Note: i.e. He shows you the lightning while you are fearful.. al-ʿUkbarī made it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and al-Zamakhsharī disallowed that because of the difference of agent between the verb and the maṣdar: the agent of the verb is Allah, and the agent of the maṣdar is the people ...]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (طمعا) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (خوفا), accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (ينشئ) is like (يري); (السحاب) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الثقال) a naʿt (adjective) of (السحاب), accusative.
The clause «هو الذي ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يريكم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «ينشئ ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(الواو) a conjunction; (يسبّح) an imperfect verb, nominative; (الرعد) a fāʿil, nominative; (بحمده) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسبّح) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl from (الرعد).]», and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (الملائكة) conjoined to (الرعد), nominative; (من خيفته) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسبّح), and (من) is causal, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (يرسل الصواعق) is like (ينشئ السحاب); (الفاء) a conjunction; (يصيب) is like (يسبّح); (الباء) a conjunction «[Translator's note: so in the source («حرف عطف»); a preposition (حرف جرّ) is evidently meant.]» and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يصيب); (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governing word being (يصيب); (يشاء) is like (يسبّح), and the object of (يشاء) is omitted, its implied form being "its striking" (إصابته), and the fāʿil of (يشاء) is Allah; (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl; (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يجادلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) the fāʿil; (في الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يجادلون); (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl; (هو) is like (هم); (شديد) a khabar, nominative; (المحال) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «يسبّح الرعد ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «يريكم» «[Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.]».
The clause «يرسل الصواعق ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «يسبّح الرعد».
The clause «يصيب ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «يرسل».
The clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «هم يجادلون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the relative (من) «[Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.]».
The clause «هو شديد ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the Name of Majesty.

* Morphology:
(الرعد): in exegesis, al-raʿd is the name of an angel among the angels, or it is his voice.. or it is a maṣdar applied to the sound of the electric spark produced by the friction of clouds ... Abū Ḥayyān said: the exegetes did not agree that al-raʿd is the name of an angel, and supposing it is the name of an angel, it does not follow that this angel manages either the clouds or anything else ... etc. See verse (19) of Sūrat al-Baqara.
(المحال): it is said that the mīm in it is radical, from محل بفلان, said when one plots against someone and exposes him to destruction; on this view it is an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb that comes in the pattern-classes فتح, فرح and كرم.. It is also said: al-miḥāl is plotting and strength.. In al-Qāmūs it says: المحال, like كتاب, is plotting, seeking an aim by stratagems and contrivance, power, disputation, torment, punishment, enmity, strength and severity.. ومحل به, with any of the three vowels on the ḥāʾ, محلا ومحالا: he plotted against him by slandering him to the ruler; وماحله مماحلة ومحالا: he contended in strength with him until it became clear which of them was stronger. In all the above the mīm is radical, and its pattern is فعال.. It is also said: the mīm is extra, from الحول and الحيلة, and it underwent a vowel-change (iʿlāl) irregularly, because the rule would be no vowel-change, as one says محور, مقود and مرود.. its pattern being مفعل, with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- «هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً»: what is meant by lightning is its immediately understood sense; and from Ibn ʿAbbās it is reported that what is meant by it is water, and so it is figurative (majāz), of the type of applying a thing to what usually accompanies it.
2- In the verse there is a marvellous art among the arts of rhetoric, namely «the soundness of the divisions» (ṣiḥḥat al-aqsām). It can be defined as fully covering the meaning in all its divisions and aspects, so that the speaker leaves nothing of them out. In the verse mentioned, He fully covered the two divisions of seeing lightning, for in it there is nothing but fear of thunderbolts and hope of rain, and there is no third to these two divisions. But merely covering the divisions is not counted as eloquence; rather there is something beyond that, subtler and harder to attain, and that is putting first what is more worthy of mention and more deserving of precedence: He put fear before hope, since thunderbolts may strike from the first flash, while rain comes only after the lightning flashes repeatedly, for its repetition hardly ever fails. For this reason the Arabs would count seventy flashes and then set out in search of pasture, and they would not miss the rain and the herbage.

* Benefits:
1- «يُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ»: though the scholars differ about this bāʾ, they have complicated the simple and made difficult the easy, and they have not agreed. We know that the original meaning of the bāʾ is attachment (ilṣāq), and it does not leave it in any of its meanings; that is why Sībawayh confined himself to it. Whether we say that the bāʾ here is for attachment, for seeking aid (istiʿāna) or for causation, all of them come from one niche, namely adjacency and accompaniment, and we have no need for affectation and strained interpretation. We point out here that the scholars have mentioned thirteen meanings for the bāʾ.

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(له دعوة) is like (له معقّبات) «[Note: in verse (11) of this surah.]»; (الحقّ) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يدعون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الواو) the fāʿil (agent); (من دونه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied object of (يدعون), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negative; (يستجيبون) is like (يدعون); (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يستجيبون); (بشيء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يستجيبون) in the sense of "they answer" (يجيبون); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (كباسط) a preposition and its genitive noun «[Note: the kāf may be a noun in the sense of "like" (مثل), and then it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its adjective..]», attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e.: "except with an answering like the answering of one who stretches out his two palms" «[Note: this is the analysis of al-Zamakhsharī, and Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī followed him in it.. There are many other interpretations in explaining the verse, for which the books of exegesis should be consulted.]», so it is on the omission of a muḍāf; (كفّيه) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (إلى الماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (باسط); (اللام) for giving the reason (taʿlīl); (يبلغ) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) «أن» after the lām, the fāʿil being "it" (هو), i.e. the water; (فاه) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, its sign of the accusative being the alif.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلغ..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (باسط).
(الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl; (ما) negative, working as laysa works; (هو) a detached pronoun, the noun of mā, in the position of the nominative; (الباء) redundant (zāʾida); (بالغة) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of mā «[Translator's note: so written in the source; the word in the verse is (ببالغه): بالغ with the pronoun هـ, as the next phrase shows.]»..
and (الهاء) is like the last one; (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative, inoperative; (دعاء) a mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الكافرين) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (في ضلال) a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
The clause «له دعوة ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «الّذين يدعون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يدعون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يستجيبون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يبلغ ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied relative (أن).
The clause «ما هو ببالغه ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «ما دعاء الكافرين ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(دعوة): a maṣdar (verbal noun) of a single instance (maṣdar marra) from دعا يدعو; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ. It may also be a pure maṣdar stripped of the sense of a single instance.
(كفّيه): dual of كف, a primitive (jāmid) noun for the well-known body part; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الواو) a conjunction; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسجد), which is an imperfect verb, nominative; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative; (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (السموات) by the wāw, genitive; (طوعا) a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "obeying"; (كرها) conjoined to (طوعا) by the wāw, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (ظلالهم) conjoined to the relative (من), nominative.. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بالغدوّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يسجد); (الآصال) conjoined to (الغدوّ) by the wāw, genitive like it.
The clause «يسجد ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the previous resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
1- The composite representational simile (al-tashbīh al-murakkab al-tamthīlī): in the saying of the Exalted «وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ إِلَّا كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى الْماءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فاهُ وَما هُوَ بِبالِغِهِ», i.e. because it is an inanimate thing that does not perceive his thirst or his stretching out his hands to it. Their gods — when they ask them, with the tongue of necessity, to suffice them in what concerns them, in their lack of perception, let alone the ability to answer, and their remaining therefore in loss — are likened to the state of water within sight of a thirsty man who stretches out his palms to it, calling it by word and by gesture, and he is therefore in ever-increasing distress and ruin.
From Abū ʿUbayda it is reported that this is a likening to one who grasps at water, in that he obtains nothing. Then he said: the Arabs give as a proverb, for one who strives after what he cannot attain, the one who grasps at water; and he recited the saying of the poet:
فأصبحت فيما كان بيني وبينها ... في الود مثل القابض الماء باليد
(So I became, in the love that was between her and me, like one who grasps water in his hand.)
2- Sarcasm (al-tahakkum): in the noble verse, where the speech is given the form of sarcasm against them; it is said that they do not answer them with any answering except an answering found in this form, in which there is absolutely no trace of answering. So it is in reality of the type of attaching [the impossible] to a condition «[Translator's note: «من باب التعلق بالحال» — rendered literally; the phrase is elliptical in the source.]».
3- Metaphor (al-istiʿāra): in the saying of the Exalted «وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ», where prostration is borrowed for submission and humility.

safi-cedvel:16-16.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, the fāʿil (agent) being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (ربّ) a khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (السموات) a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (السموات) by the wāw, genitive; (قل) is like the first one; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "the Lord of the heavens" (ربّ السموات); (قل) is like the first one; (الهمزة) for interrogation; (الفاء) a conjunction; (اتّخذتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) a pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; (من دونه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (أولياء) — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies — and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (أولياء) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (لا يملكون لأنفسهم) is like (لا يستجيبون لهم) «[Note: in verse (14) of this surah.]»; (نفعا) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), for emphasising the negation; (ضرا) conjoined to (نفعا), accusative like it; (قل) is like the first one; (هل) an interrogative particle; (يستوي) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (الأعمى) a fāʿil, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif; (البصير) conjoined to (الأعمى) by the wāw, nominative; (أم) in the sense of (بل), for digression (iḍrāb); (هل تستوي.. النور) is like (هل يستوي ... البصير); (أم) is like the first one, and after it there is an implied hamza; (جعلوا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from (شركاء), which is the object of (جعلوا), accusative; (خلقوا) is like (جعلوا); (كخلقه) a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of an omitted element which is the mafʿūl bihi «[Note: on the view that الخلق is a collective noun or in the sense of "the created".. or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) on the view that الخلق is a maṣdar.]» — and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) a conjunction; (تشابه) a past verb; (الخلق) a fāʿil, nominative; (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تشابه); (قل الله) is like the previous one; (خالق) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative; (كلّ) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (شيء) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) a conjunction; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (الواحد) a khabar, nominative; (القهّار) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «من ربّ ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption confirming the report of their saying.
The clause «الله (ربّ السموات) ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «قل (the third) ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اتّخذتم ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to an implied clause which is the object of the saying, i.e.: "Have you acknowledged the answer, and then taken ...?" or "Have you known that Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and then taken ...?" «[Note: the fāʾ may connect the apodosis of an implied condition, the clause being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e.: "If you acknowledge the lordship of Allah, then why have you taken ...?"]».
The clause «لا يملكون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (أولياء).
The clause «قل (the fourth) ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هل يستوي الأعمى ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «هل تستوي الظلمات ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «جعلوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «خلقوا ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (شركاء).
The clause «تشابه الخلق ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause «خلقوا».
The clause «قل (the fifth) ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «الله خالق ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «هو الواحد ...» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying «[Note: the clause may be resumed, not falling within the scope of the saying.]».

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of the Exalted «قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ». The blind one is the polytheist who is ignorant of worship and of the One who deserves it, and the seeing one is the monotheist who knows that. It is also said that the speech is a simile, and the meaning is that the believer and the unbeliever are not equal just as the blind and the seeing are not equal, so there is no figurative usage.
2- Sarcasm (al-tahakkum): in the saying of the Exalted «أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ», in the context of disavowal; it was brought for sarcasm, for none other than Allah the Exalted creates anything, neither equal nor inferior.

* Benefits:
The borrowing of prostration for submission and humility in the saying of the Exalted «وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً» — these two being among the characteristics of rational beings — for beings both rational and non-rational. Willingness (al-ṭawʿ) is what arises from choice, and it is what proceeds from the human being; unwillingness (al-karh) is what arises without choice, and it is what proceeds from the inanimate. The meaning of the submission of the shadows is their compliance with what is intended for them, such as their lengthening and shortening, their extending and contracting.
Abū Ḥayyān has a fine statement which we record below, to dispel misconceptions. He said: "That the shadows are meant to be the persons themselves, as some said, is weak; and weaker than it is the saying of Ibn al-Anbārī: that the Exalted gave the shadows intellects by which they prostrate to Him and humble themselves, just as He gave the mountains understanding so that they addressed and were addressed. For a mountain cannot have an intellect except on the condition of supposing life in it; as for the shadow, it is an accident in which life cannot be conceived to subsist."

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(أنزل) a past verb, the fāʿil (agent) being "He" (هو); (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل) «[Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (ماء) — an adjective placed before the noun it qualifies.]»; (ماء) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الفاء) a conjunction; (سالت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine; (أودية) a fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (بقدرها) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سالت) «[Note: or attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (أودية).]», and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) a conjunction; (احتمل) is like (أنزل); (السيل) a fāʿil, nominative; (زبدا) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (رابيا) a naʿt of the object, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (من) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (يوقدون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) the fāʿil; (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يوقدون); (في النّار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the pronoun in (عليه) «[Note: or attached to (يوقدون).]»; (ابتغاء) a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) «[Note: or a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "seeking ornament"..]»; (حلية) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (أو) a conjunction; (متاع) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (حلية), genitive; (زبد) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (مثله) a naʿt of (زبد), nominative.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الكاف) a preposition and particle of likening; (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governing word is (يضرب); the reference is to what has been mentioned before, and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address; (يضرب) an imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الحقّ) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the likeness of the truth"; (الباطل) conjoined to (الحقّ) by the wāw, accusative; (الفاء) a conjunction of derivation (tafrīʿiyya); (أمّا) a particle of condition and detailing; (الزبد) a mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (يذهب) is like (يضرب), the fāʿil being "it" (هو); (جفاء) a ḥāl, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (أمّا) is like the first one; (ما) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (ينفع الناس) is like (يضرب.. الحقّ), the fāʿil being "it" (هو), and it is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid); (فيمكث) is like (فيذهب); (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يمكث); (كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال) is like (كذلك ... الحق).
The clause «أنزل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «سالت أودية ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أنزل».
The clause «احتمل السيل ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «سالت».
The clause «يوقدون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «ممّا يوقدون ... زبد» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أنزل»; so it is another likeness.
The clause «يضرب الله» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أمّا الزبد فيذهب ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «يضرب الله»..
The clause «يذهب جفاء ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الزبد) «[Note: the original form of the speech is: "Whatever be the case, the foam goes away as scum"; when أمّا was substituted for the condition, the fāʾ shifted to the khabar.]».
The clause «ما ينفع الناس فيمكث ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «الزبد فيذهب».
The clause «ينفع ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يمكث ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
The clause «يضرب الله (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive, for emphasis.

* Morphology:
(سالت): it contains a vowel-change (iʿlāl) by substitution; its origin is سيلت, and the yāʾ was changed into alif because it is vowelled and the letter before it has fatḥa; its pattern is فعلت.
(السيل): a primitive (jāmid) noun; abundant flowing water was named with it, with the name of the maṣdar (verbal noun); its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(زبدا): a name for dirt and grime and what rises on the surface of water, like bubbles; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.
(رابيا): an active participle from ربا يربو in the sense of "increased", and here in the sense of "high"; its pattern is فاعل, and (الياء) is converted from wāw by vowel-change, because it is vowelled after a kasra; the origin is رابوا, with kasra on the bāʾ.
(حلية): a name for that with which one is adorned, of precious metal or precious stones; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn «[Translator's note: so in the source; حلية is فِعْلة, with sukūn on the ʿayn.]». Its plural is حلي, with kasra or ḍamma on the ḥāʾ — the latter irregularly. As for حليّ, with ḍamma or kasra and with a doubled yāʾ, it is the plural of الحلي, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the lām.. See verse (148) of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
(جفاء): a name for what the flood throws onto the two banks of what is of no use, from جفأ النهر, i.e. the river threw out foam and debris; on this view the hamza is radical.. One says: جفأت القدر بزبدها (the pot threw out its froth), and أجفأت.. and one says جفأ الوادي and أجفأ when the valley dries up. Al-ʿUkbarī makes the hamza converted from a [weak] letter, and that is not so.

* Rhetoric:
- The parable (al-mathal): in the noble verse there is a parable that Allah struck for the truth and its people and falsehood and its party, just as He struck the blind and the seeing, and darkness and light, as a parable for them. He likened the truth and its people to the water that He sends down from the sky, so that people's valleys flow with it, they are given life by it and it benefits them in many kinds of benefit; and to the metal which they make use of in fashioning ornaments from it and making vessels and various implements. He likened falsehood, in the speed of its vanishing, the imminence of its passing and its being stripped of benefit, to the foam of the flood which it casts off, and to the dross of metal that floats on top of it when it is melted. Under this splendid parable are folded various kinds of eloquence, which we present briefly:
a- The indefiniteness of «الأودية» (valleys), because rain comes only by way of alternation between regions.
b- Guarding against misunderstanding (al-iḥtirās) by His saying «بقدرها», i.e. in its measure, which Allah knew to be beneficial for those it floods and not harmful; otherwise, had it overflowed and turned into a torrent, it would have swept away the green and the dry and destroyed tillage and offspring.
c- Observing correspondence (murāʿāt al-naẓīr) in the words water, flood, foam and swelling, and in the words fire, substance, metals, kindling, ornament and goods.
d- Embroidered involution and evolution (al-laff wa-l-nashr) in the saying of the Exalted «فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفاءً» to the end of the verse.

safi-cedvel:18-18.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) a preposition; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) «[Note: or attached to (يضرب) in the previous verse — on the view of al-Zamakhsharī — and (الحسنى) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar because it is its adjective, i.e.: "they responded with the best response".]»; (استجابوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma..
and (الواو) the fāʿil (agent); (لربّهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استجابوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الحسنى) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) a conjunction; (الذين) a relative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ «[Note: or it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first relative (للذين).]»; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (يستجيبوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) the fāʿil; (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يستجيبوا); (لو) a non-jussive particle of condition; (أنّ) a particle of emphasis making the noun accusative — abrogating (nāsikh) —; (لهم) is like (له), attached to the khabar of anna; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); (جميعا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), from the pronoun of "being settled" (istiqrār), which is the khabar.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم ما في الأرض) is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "it were established" (ثبت).. and that is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
(الواو) a conjunction; (مثله) conjoined to the position of (ما), accusative.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (معه) an adverb, accusative, attached to a ḥāl from (مثله).. and (الهاء) is like the last one; (اللام) occurring in the answer of (لو); (افتدوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and (الواو) the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (افتدوا); (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) a particle of address; (لهم) is like (له), attached to a fronted khabar; (سوء) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الحساب) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) a conjunction; (مأواهم) a mubtadaʾ, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif.. and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (جهنّم) a khabar, nominative, prevented from nunation because of being a proper name and feminine; (الواو) the wāw of the ḥāl; (بئس) an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; (المهاد) a fāʿil, nominative..
and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "it" (هي) or "Jahannam".
The clause «استجابوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the first relative (الذين).
The clause «للذين استجابوا ... الحسنى» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «الذين لم يستجيبوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لم يستجيبوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «(ثبت) ملك الأرض ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) «[Note: the clause may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.. or have no grammatical position as a resumption, in the case where the second relative is conjoined to the first.]».
The clause «افتدوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أولئك لهم سوء ...» is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) «[Note: or it has no grammatical position, being resumptive.]».
The clause «لهم سوء الحساب ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «مأواهم جهنّم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause «لهم سوء الحساب».
The clause «بئس المهاد ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:19-25.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for disavowing interrogation (istifhām inkārī); (الفاء) resumptive; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the fāʿil (agent) being "he" (هو), and it is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid); (أنّ) a particle of emphasis making the noun accusative; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as the noun of anna; (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو), and it is the returning pronoun; (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (من ربّك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزل), and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الحقّ) the khabar (predicate) of anna, nominative; (الكاف) a preposition; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of the relative (من); (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أعمى) a khabar, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (إنّما) the restraining [mā] and the restrained [inna] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (يتذكّر) is like (يعلم); (أولو) a fāʿil, nominative, its sign of the nominative being (الواو), for it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (الألباب) a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «من يعلم ... كمن هو أعمى» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (من).
