And His saying: {لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الحق}: this is of the type of annexing the qualified to the qualifier, the origin being «له الدعوةُ الحقُّ» ("His is the true call"), as in His saying {وَلَدَارُ الآخرة} [Yūsuf: 109] on one of the two views. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "There are two views on it. The first: «الدعوة» is annexed to «الحق» which is the opposite of falsehood, as «الكلمة» is annexed to it in his saying 'the word of truth'. The second: it is annexed to «الحق» which is Allah, in the sense of the calling of the One called upon, the Real, who hears and answers." The Shaykh said: "This second view is not evident, because it amounts to the implied sense 'to Allah belongs the calling of Allah', as you would say 'to Zayd belongs the calling of Zayd', and this construction is not valid." I say: and where is this in relation to what al-Zamakhsharī said, that he should rebut him with it?
His saying: {والذين يَدْعُونَ}: by «الذين» may be meant the polytheists; so the wāw in «يَدْعُون» refers to them, and its object is omitted, namely the idols; and the wāw in {لاَ يَسْتَجِيبُونَ} refers to the omitted object of «يَدْعون», the pronoun referring to it as to rational beings because they treated it as such. The implied sense is: and the polytheists who call upon the idols — the idols do not answer them except with an answering like the answering of one who stretches out his two palms, i.e. like the water's answering of one who stretches out his two palms to it, asking it to reach his mouth; and water is inanimate, perceiving neither the stretching of his palms nor his thirst, and it is unable to answer him and reach his mouth. Al-Zamakhsharī said its meaning. When Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned something close to that and supplied the mentioned implied sense, he said: "The maṣdar (verbal noun) in this reconstruction is annexed to its object, as in His saying {لاَّ يَسْأَمُ الإنسان مِن دُعَآءِ الخير} [Fuṣṣilat: 49], and the agent of this maṣdar is implied, namely the pronoun of the water; i.e. they do not answer them except as the water answers the one who stretches out his palm to it; and 'answering' here is a metonymy for compliance."
By «الذين» may also be meant the idols, i.e. and the gods whom they call upon besides Allah do not answer them with anything except an answering; the implied sense being as in the previous view. They were pluralised with the plural of rational beings either because of mixing — since the gods are rational beings and inanimate things — or because they treated them as rational beings in their claim. So the wāw in «يَدْعُون» is for the polytheists, the omitted returning pronoun is for the idols, and likewise the wāw of «يستجيبون».
Al-Yazīdī read from Abū ʿAmr «تَدْعُونَ», in the second person, and it strengthens the second view; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else.
His saying: «ليَبْلُغَ»: the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «باسِط», and the fāʿil (agent) of «ليبلُغَ» is the pronoun of the water.
His saying: {وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ}: there are three views on «هو». The first: it is the pronoun of the water, and the hāʾ in «ببالغِه» is for the mouth, i.e. and the water does not reach his mouth. The second: it is the pronoun of the mouth, and the hāʾ in «ببالِغه» is for the water, i.e. and the mouth does not reach the water; since in this situation neither of them reaches the other, attributing the act to either of them, or denying it, are both valid. The third: it is the pronoun of the one stretching out, and the hāʾ in «ببالغه» is for the water, i.e. and the one who stretches out his palms to the water does not reach the water.
It is not permissible that «هو» be the pronoun of the one stretching out, with the agent of «ببالغِه» implied and the hāʾ in «ببالِغه» for the water [Translator's note: the context — "the qualifier applied to other than its own" and the required overt agent «الماءُ» — indicates the hāʾ here is meant to be for the mouth; the text as written has "for the water"], because it would then be a case of a qualifier being applied to other than the one it belongs to, and whenever that is so the agent must be made overt, so that the construction would be thus: «وما هو ببالغِه الماءُ». But if you make the hāʾ in «ببالغِه» for the water, it is permissible for «هو» to be the pronoun of the one stretching out, as has been set out.
The kāf in «كباسطِ» is either a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from that maṣdar, as has been set out more than once.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The kāf in «كباسط», if you make it a particle, contains a pronoun referring to the omitted qualified noun; and if you make it a noun, it contains no pronoun." I say: the kāf being a noun in [ordinary] speech is not held by the majority, but rather by al-Akhfash. By "the qualified noun" he means the maṣdar which he supplied in what preceded.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً}: either a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. willing and unwilling, or accusative (manṣūb) as an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb. Abū Mijlaz read «والإِيصال» with the yāʾ before the ṣād. Ibn Jinnī accounted for it as the maṣdar of «آصَلَ», like «ضارَبَ», i.e. he entered the late afternoon (al-aṣīl), as «أصْبَح» means he entered the morning.
And «ظلالُهم» is conjoined to «مَنْ». «بالغُدُوِّ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسْجُد», and the bāʾ means «في», i.e. at these two times.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
The two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «يَسْتوي» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, and the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ. Both are clear, in view of the fact that the fāʿil (agent) is figuratively feminine, so both masculine and feminine are allowed in its verb, like parallels of it that have passed.
And His saying: «أَمْ هَلْ»: this is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) «أم», so it is to be rendered as «بل» plus the hamza according to the majority, and as «بل» alone according to some of them; this has preceded in detail. Whoever holds that it is to be rendered as «بل» alone may draw strength from this verse, through «هَل» occurring after it: if we rendered it as «بل» plus the hamza, two particles of [the same] meaning would combine, so one renders it as «بل» alone. But it gives him no strength, for the hamza has combined with «هل» in actual wording, as in the poet's saying:
285 - 0-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أهلْ رَأَوْنا بوادِي القُفِّ ذي الأَكَمِ
(… did they see us in the valley of al-Quff, with its hillocks?)
So it is all the more fitting that it combine with it in implication. And one could say: we do not grant that this «هل» is interrogative; rather it means «قد», and a group held this, even when no hamza combines with it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {هَلْ أتى عَلَى الإنسان حِينٌ} [al-Insān: 1], i.e. "there has come"; so here it is all the more fitting. Usage has attested both the occurrence of «هل» after «أم» and its absence: of the first is this verse, and of the second is what follows it in His saying «اَمْ جَعَلوا». The poet also combined the two usages in his saying:
285 - 1- هل ما عَلِمْتَ وما استُودِعْتَ مكتومُ ... أم حَبْلُها إذ نَأَتْكَ اليومَ مَصْرومُ
أَمْ هَلْ كبيرٌ بكَى لم يَقْضِ عَبْرَتَه ... إثرَ الأحبَّةِ يومَ البَيْنَ مَشْكُومُ
(Is what you knew and what was entrusted to you kept secret, or is her bond, now that she has gone far from you today, severed? Or is an old man who wept, not having finished his tears after the loved ones on the day of parting, to be rewarded?)
And the clause in His saying «خَلَقوا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شركاء».

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {أَوْدِيَةٌ}: it is the plural of «وادٍ». As for pluralising «فاعِل» on «أَفْعِلَة», Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is anomalous, and we have not heard it in any word other than this one. Its justification is that «فاعِل» has come with the meaning of «فَعِيل», and just as «فَعِيل» has come with «أفْعِلَة», as in «جَرِيْب» and «أَجْرِبَة», so has «فاعِل»." I say: «فاعِل» with «أفْعِلة» has been heard in two other words: one of them is their saying «جائز» and «أجْوِزَة», and the second «ناحِية» and «أَنْحِية».
His saying: «بقَدَرها»: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «سالَتْ». The second: it is attached to something omitted, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أَوْدية». The generality read it with fatḥa on the dāl, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī and Abū ʿAmr, in one transmission, with sukūn; this has preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara.
And «احتمل» means «حَمَل» ("carried"), so «افْتَعَلَ» has the meaning of the bare form. He made «الأودية» indefinite and «السيل» definite only because rain falls on places by turns, so some valleys of the earth flow and not others; and «السيل» is definite because it has been understood from the verb before it, namely «فسالَتْ»; had it been mentioned it would have been indefinite, so when it was repeated it was repeated with the definite form, as in «رأيت رجلاً فأكرمت الرجلَ» ("I saw a man and honoured the man"). [And «الزَّبَد» is the scum and dross of boiling.] Al-Nābigha said:
285 - 2- فما الفُراتُ إذا هَبَّ الرياحُ له ... تَرْمي غوارِبُه العِبْرَيْنِ بالزَّبَدِ
(Nor is the Euphrates, when the winds blow upon it and its crests hurl foam on both its banks, [more generous than he].)
It is also said: it is what the torrent carries of rubbish and the like, and the bubbles it throws [onto] its bank. It is also said: it is what the valley casts out when its water surges and its waves rise. These are closely related expressions. And «الزُّبَد» is what is extracted from milk (butter); it is said to be derived from this because it resembles it in colour. One says «زَبَدْتُه زَبْداً», i.e. I gave him wealth. It is used proverbially for abundance; in the ḥadīth: "His sins are forgiven him, even if they are like the foam of the sea."
His saying: {وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ}: this prepositional phrase is [a fronted khabar (predicate), and its mubtadaʾ (subject) is «زَبَدٌ»]. «مثلُه» is a naʿt of the mubtadaʾ, and the implied sense is: and from the substances such as copper, gold and silver there is a scum, i.e. a dross like it, i.e. like the scum of the water. The point of likeness is that each of them arises from impurities.
The two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «يُوقِدُوْن» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. people; and the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ, in the second person.
«عليه» is attached to «يُوْقِدون». As for «في النار», there are two views on it. The first: it is attached to «يوقِدون»; this is the view of al-Fārisī, al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ. The second: it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "being" or "fixed", said by Makkī and others. They disallowed its being attached to «يُوقِدُون» because they claimed that nothing has a fire kindled over it except while it is in the fire, and attaching the preposition to «يُوْقِدون» entails distinguishing one state from another. This does not necessarily follow. Abū ʿAlī said: "A fire may be kindled over something even if it is not in the fire, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {فَأَوْقِدْ لِي ياهامان عَلَى الطين} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 38], and the clay was not in it; only its flame reaches it. Moreover, that may be by way of emphasis, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ} [al-Anʿām: 38]."
His saying: «ابتغاءَ»: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The second: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. seeking ornament; and «حِلْيةٍ» is an object in meaning. «أو متاعٍ» is coordinated to «حِلْيةٍ». «الحلْيَة» is that with which one adorns oneself, and «المَتَاع» is that with which they meet their needs, such as iron spades and the like. And «مِنْ» in His saying {وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ} admits two views. The first: it is for the beginning of the extent, i.e. and from it arises a scum like the scum of the water. The second: it is partitive, meaning: and some of it is scum.
His saying: «جُفاءً» is a ḥāl. As for «الجُفَاء», Ibn al-Anbārī said: "what is scattered"; one says «جَفَأَتِ الريحُ السحابَ», i.e. the wind cut up the clouds and scattered them. It is also said: «الجُفاء» is what the torrent casts out; one says «جَفَأَتِ القِدْرُ بزَبَدِها تَجْفَأُ» ("the pot threw off its scum"), and «جَفَأَ السَّيْلُ بزَبَدِه» and «أَجْفَأَ» and «أَجْفَلَ»; and Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj read it with the lām. Abū Ḥātim said: "The reading of Ruʾba is not to be read, because he used to eat rats", meaning that he was an uncouth Bedouin. I say: al-Zamakhsharī's praise of him at the beginning of al-Baqara, and mention of his eloquence, have preceded. They have justified his reading as being from «أَجْفَلَتِ الريحُ الغنمَ», i.e. the wind scattered the sheep into groups; so in meaning it is like the reading of the generality with the hamza.
There are two views on the hamza of «جُفاء». The more apparent of them: it is radical, because it remains in the derived forms of this root, as you have seen. The second: it is a substitute for a wāw, and it seems to be the choice of Abū al-Baqāʾ; and this is open to question, because the meaning of the root «جفا يَجْفو» does not suit here, and the default is the absence of homonymy.
His saying: «كذلك يَضْرِب»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), i.e. like that striking [of examples] He strikes.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لِلَّذِينَ استجابوا}: there are two views on it. The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَضْرِب», and al-Zamakhsharī began with it. He said: "I.e. thus He strikes examples for the believers who responded, and for the unbelievers who did not respond.
«الحُسْنى» is a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «استجابوا», i.e. they responded with the best response. And His saying {لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض} is a new statement mentioning what He has prepared for those who did not respond." The Shaykh said: "The first interpretation is preferable", by which he means that «للذين» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «الحُسْنى» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), as its clarification will come.
He said: "Because in it the striking of examples is not restricted to the like of these two, and Allah the Exalted has struck many examples concerning these two and others; and because in it there is mention of the reward of those who respond, unlike the view of al-Zamakhsharī — so just as He mentioned the punishment for those who do not respond, He mentioned the reward for those who respond; and because his reconstruction with 'the best response' suggests a restriction of the response, and its counterpart is then not the negation of response absolutely, but only the negation of the best response, whereas Allah the Exalted has negated response absolutely; and because, on his view, His saying {لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض} would be loose, or like something loose, since the meaning would become: thus Allah strikes examples for the believers and for the unbelievers, if they had all that is in the earth; had the construction had a particle binding «لو» to what precedes it, the looseness would have gone. Also, it gives the false impression of sharing in the pronoun, even if the restriction of that to the unbelievers is known."
I say: his saying "because in it the striking of examples is not restricted": there is nothing in al-Zamakhsharī's words that entails restriction. His saying "and because in it there is mention of the reward of those who respond" to the end: from the purport of what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned too, their reward is understood. His saying "and Allah the Exalted has negated response absolutely" is not granted; rather, He negated that first response. It is not to be said: then a response that is not "best" is affirmed; because this qualifier has no implied contrary sense (mafhūm), since in reality response to Allah is never other than best. His saying "it becomes loose": how could it be loose, with al-Zamakhsharī's saying: "a new [statement] mentioning what He has prepared for them"? And his saying "also, it gives the false impression of sharing": how could this be imagined in any way at all? And how can he say that along with his saying "even if the restriction of that to the unbelievers is known"? If it is known, how can it be falsely imagined?
The second view: «للذين» is a fronted khabar, and the mubtadaʾ is «الحُسْنَى»; and {والذين لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ} is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is the counterfactual («لو») clause after it. On the first view too {والذين لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُواْ} may be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the counterfactual clause after it; and He specified those who responded with the striking of examples only because they benefit [from them], and not others.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {أَفَمَن يَعْلَمُ}: like His saying «أَفَلَمْ»; the setting out of the two views on it has preceded, and al-Zamakhsharī's position on it is far-fetched here.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين يُوفُونَ}: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «أولي», or a badal (substitute) from it, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it; or nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb, both by way of praise; or it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, what follows it being conjoined to it, and {أولئك لَهُمْ عقبى الدار} being its khabar (predicate).

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {ابتغاء وَجْهِ}: it may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and this is the apparent view, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. seeking; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object.
His saying: {عقبى الدار}: it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the prepositional phrase before it, the clause being the khabar of «أولئك»; or «لهم» may be the khabar of «أولئك» and «عُقْبى» a fāʿil (agent) of the [notion of] being-settled.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ}: it may be a badal (substitute) from «عقبى», or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «يَدْخُلونها». Al-Nakhaʿī read «جنةُ» in the singular. The disagreement over «يَدْخُلونها» has preceded.
The clause «يَدْخُلونها» admits being resumptive or an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara).
His saying: {وَمَنْ صَلَحَ}: it may be nominative (marfūʿ), conjoined to the wāw, the separation by the object making emphasis with a detached pronoun unnecessary; or it may be accusative (manṣūb) as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), and this is the weaker view.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «صَلُحَ» with ḍamma on the lām, and it is a weaker dialectal form.
His saying: {مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ} is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from {وَمَنْ صَلَحَ}, and «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus. ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read «وذُريَّتِهم» in the singular.
His saying: «سلامٌ»: the clause is quoted by an implied verb of saying, and the implied saying is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «يَدْخُلون», i.e. they enter saying.
His saying: «بما صَبَرتم» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to what «عليكم» is attached to, and «ما» is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun-forming), i.e. because of your patience. It is not attached to «سلامٌ», because a maṣdar (verbal noun) is not separated from what it governs by the khabar; said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be attached to «سلام», i.e. we greet you with peace and honour you because of your patience"; and when the Shaykh quoted this from him he made no objection to it. The apparent view is that the preceding objection does not apply to him, because that applies to the maṣdar interpreted as a maṣdar-forming particle plus a verb, and this maṣdar is not of that kind. The bāʾ is either causal, as preceded, or means "in exchange for", i.e. in exchange for your patience, i.e. for having borne the hardships of patience. It is also said: «بما صَبَرْتُم» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. this abundant reward is for your having been patient.
The majority read «فنِعْمَ» with kasra on the nūn and sukūn on the ʿayn; Ibn Yaʿmar with fatḥa and kasra, and it has preceded that this is the original form, as in the poet's saying:
253 - 8-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... نَعِمَ السَّاعُون في القومِ الشُّطُرْ
(… excellent are those who strive [to help] among the people, the far-reaching.)
And Ibn Waththāb with fatḥa and sukūn, which is a lightening of the original; and the dialect of Tamīm makes the ʿayn of «فَعِل» vowelless in all cases. The one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. the Garden.

semin-durr:25-25.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {والذين يَنقُضُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause of His saying {أولئك لَهُمُ اللعنة} is its khabar (predicate). The discussion of «اللعنة» is like the discussion of {لَهُمْ عقبى الدار} [al-Raʿd: 22].

semin-durr:26-26.t:
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ويَقْدُر» with ḍamma on the ʿayn [of the verb].
His saying: «وفَرِحوا»: this is a resumptive statement. It is also said: rather [it is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»] before it. And this is open to question, in that it separates the parts of the ṣila by the khabar (predicate); and also, this is past while what precedes it is future, and there must be agreement in tense — unless it is said that what is intended is their continuing in that, and that the past, when it occurs as a ṣila, is suited to both past and future.
His saying: {وَمَا الحياة الدنيا فِي الآخرة}, i.e. beside the Hereafter. This prepositional phrase is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied sense being: and the near life, being beside the Hereafter, is nothing but a brief enjoyment. It may not be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «الحياة» nor to «الدنيا», because they do not occur in the Hereafter.

semin-durr:27-27.t: The pronoun in «عليه» refers to Allah the Exalted, i.e. to His religion and His law. It is also said: to the Messenger. It is also said: to the Quran.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين آمَنُواْ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ}: five views are allowed in it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the second relative noun, what is between them being parenthetical. [The second: it is a badal (substitute)] from «مَنْ أناب». The third: it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it. The fourth: it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. [Translator's note: "The fifth" is not written in the text:] it is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb.
His saying: {بِذِكْرِ الله}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تطمئنُّ», the bāʾ then being causal, i.e. because of the remembrance of Allah. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may also be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. tranquillity comes about by the remembrance of Allah. The second: it is attached to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «قلوبُهم», i.e. they are at rest while the remembrance of Allah is in them."

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ}: there are several views on it: it may be a badal (substitute) from «القلوبُ», on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the hearts of those who believed; or a badal from «مَنْ أناب» — this on the view of whoever did not make the first relative noun a badal from «مَنْ أناب», otherwise two badals would follow one another; or a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «طُوْبَى لهم» a predicative clause; or the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ; or accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb. On these two [last] views the clause «طُوبَى لهم» is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), governed by «آمَنُوا وعَمِلوا».
The wāw of «طُوبَى» is changed from a yāʾ, because it is from «الطِّيب» (goodness); it was changed only because of the ḍamma before it, as in «مُوسِر» and «مُوْقِن», from «اليُسْر» and «اليقين». They differed about it. It is said: it is a singular noun, a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «بُشْرى» and «رُجْعى», from «طاب يطيب». It is also said: rather it is the plural of «طَيِّبة», as they said «كُوْسَى» in the plural of «كَيِّسَة» and «ضُوْقَى» in the plural of «ضَيِّقة»; and one may say «طِيْبى» with kasra on the first radical, and likewise «الكِيْسَى» and «الضِيقَى». Whether it is the name of a particular tree, or the name of the Garden in the language of India or Abyssinia, is a well-known disagreement.
Beginning a sentence with «طُوبَى» is permissible either because it is a proper name for a particular thing, or because it is an indefinite noun with the meaning of a supplication, like «سَلام عليك» and «وَيْل له»; so said Sībawayh. Ibn Mālik said: "It must be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the abrogating particles [of the mubtadaʾ] do not enter upon it." Against him is the fact that some of them made it, in the verse, accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and He has assigned them «طُوْبَى»"; and that may be supported by the reading of ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī «وحُسْنَ مآب» with fatḥa on the nūn. He said: "It is conjoined to «طُوْبَى», and it is in the position of the accusative." Thaʿlab said: "On this view «طُوْبَى» is a maṣdar, as they said «سُقْياً» ('may [Allah] give you rain')." The author of al-Lawāmiḥ accounted for this reading as a vocative, like {ياأسفى} [Yūsuf: 84], over what has been missed, meaning that «طُوْبَى» is annexed to the pronoun and the lām is intrusive, as in the poet's saying:
284 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يا بُؤْسَ للجهلِ ضَرَّاراً لأقوامِ
(… O the misery of ignorance, so harmful to peoples!)
and [his saying]:
285 - 5- يا بُوسَ للحَرْبِ التي ... وَضَعَتْ أراهِطَ فاستراحوا
(O the misery of war, which brought low whole clans, so they found rest!)
and for that reason the tanwīn was dropped from «بؤس»; as though it were said: "O their goodness!", i.e. how good they are, and how fine their return! Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning of «طُوْبَى لك» is: you have attained good and goodness. Its position is the accusative or the nominative, as when you say «طِيباً لك» and «طِيبٌ لك», «سلاماً لك» and «سلامٌ لك»; and the reading of His saying «وحُسن مآب» in the accusative and the nominative points you to its two positions. The lām in «لهم» is for clarification, like it in «سَقْياً لك»." So this indicates that it is declinable and is not restricted to the nominative as a mubtadaʾ.
Makwaza al-Aʿrābī read «طِيْبَى» with kasra on the ṭāʾ, so that the yāʾ remains sound, as in «بِيْض» and «مَعِيْشة».
It was also read «وحُسْنَ مآبٌ», with fatḥa on the nūn and «مآب» in the nominative, as a past verb, its origin being «حَسُن»; the ḍamma of the second radical was transferred to the first radical with the intention of praise, as in their saying:
285 - 6-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . حُسْنَ ذا أَدَبا
(… how fine this one is in good breeding!)
and «مَآبٌ» is its fāʿil (agent).

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {كَذَلِكَ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), like its parallels. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Like that sending We have sent you, meaning: We have sent you with a sending of consequence." It is also said: the kāf is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the meaning in His saying {إِنَّ الله يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ ويهدي} [al-Raʿd: 27], i.e. "just as Allah has carried this out, so We have sent you". Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What appears to me is that the meaning is: just as We have established the custom that Allah leads astray and guides, not the signs demanded [by them], so likewise We have done with this nation: We have sent you to it with revelation, not with demanded signs."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «كذلك» — [the implied sense is:] the matter is thus; so he made it in the position of the nominative (rafʿ). Al-Ḥawfī said: "The kāf is for comparison, in the position of the accusative, i.e. like Our doing of guidance and leading astray." The reference by «ذلك» is to what He described Himself with, namely that Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.
His saying: {قَدْ خَلَتْ} is a clause [in the position of the genitive (jarr) as a naʿt (adjective)]. And «لتتلُوَ» [Translator's note: printed «للتلُوَ» in the text] is attached to «أَرْسَلْناك».
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ}: this clause may be resumptive or circumstantial. The pronoun in «وهم» refers to «أمة» in terms of meaning; had it referred to its wording, the construction would have been «وهي تكفر». It is also said: the pronoun refers to «أمَّة» and to «أُمَم». It is also said: to those who said {لَوْلاَ أُنزِلَ} [al-Raʿd: 27].

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً}: its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, i.e. "it would have been this Quran", because it is at the utmost limit of soundness. It is also said: its implied form is "they would not have believed". It is reported from al-Farrāʾ that the apodosis of «لو» is the clause of His saying {وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ}, so there is fronting and postponing in the speech, and what is between them is parenthetical; and this in reality is what indicates the apodosis. The tāʾ was omitted in His saying «وكُلِّم به المَوْتى» while it remained in the two verbs before it only because it is of the type of taghlīb (giving precedence to one gender), since «المَوْتى» includes masculine and feminine.
His saying: {أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الذين}: the basic meaning of «اليَأْس» is cutting off desire for a thing and despairing of it. People differed about it here. Some of them said: it is here in its proper meaning, and the sense is: have not those who believe despaired of the faith of the unbelievers of Quraysh? That is because, when they [the unbelievers] asked for these signs, they [the believers] hoped for their faith and sought the sending down of these signs so that the unbelievers would believe; and Allah knew that they would not believe, so He said: have they not despaired of their faith? Said by al-Kisāʾī. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Allah made it occur to the believers that if Allah willed He would guide all people; so He said: have they not despaired in knowledge? He is saying: knowledge made them despair, it being implied; as you say in speech: 'I have despaired of you, that you will not succeed', as though he said: he knew it with certainty." He said: "So «يَئِسَتْ» means «عَلِمَت» ('knew'); even if it has not been heard, it is to be directed to that by interpretation."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that «اليأس» in this verse is in its proper meaning, namely that, when He made their faith remote in His saying {وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً}, on the two interpretations of the omitted implied [apodosis], He said in this one: have not the believers despaired of the faith of these people, knowing that if Allah willed He would guide all people?"
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "{أَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ} may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «آمَنوا», in the sense: have not those who believe that if Allah willed He would guide all people, and would guide them, lost hope of the faith of these unbelievers?" And Abū al-ʿAbbās preceded him in this.
The Shaykh said: "In my view another possibility exists besides what they mentioned: that the statement is complete at His saying {أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الذين آمنوا}, and it is an affirmation, i.e. the believers have despaired of the faith of the obstinate; and {أَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ الله} is the response to an omitted oath, i.e. and I swear, if Allah willed He would guide all people. What indicates this oath is the presence of «أنْ» with «لو», as in the poet's saying:
285 - 7- أَمَا واللهِ انْ لو كنتَ حُرَّاً ... وما بالحُرِّ أنت ولا القَمينِ
(By Allah, if you were a free man — but you are neither free nor worthy [of it] …)
and the other's saying:
285 - 8- فأُقسمُ أنْ لَوِ التقينا وأنتُمُ ... لكان لكم يومٌ من الشرِّ مظلِمُ
(I swear that had we and you met, you would have had a day of evil, dark.)
Sībawayh mentioned that «أنْ» comes after an oath, and Ibn ʿUṣfūr made it a link binding the oath to the clause sworn upon."
Some of them said: rather it here means «عَلِمَ» and «تَبَيَّن» ("knew", "became clear"). Al-Qāsim ibn Maʿn, who is among the trustworthy Kufans, said: "It is the dialect of Hawāzin."
Ibn al-Kalbī said: "It is the dialect of a clan of al-Nakhaʿ"; and of it is the saying of Rabāḥ ibn ʿAdī:
285 - 9- ألم يَيْئَسِ الأقوامُ أني أنا ابنُهُ ... وإن كنتُ عن أرضِ العشيرةِ نائيا
(Do the tribes not know that I am his son, even if I am far from the land of the clan?)
and the saying of Suḥaym:
286 - 0- أقولُ لهم بالشَّعْبِ إذ يَأْسِرُونني ... ألم تَيْئَسُوا أني ابنُ فارسِ زَهْدَمِ
(I say to them in the ravine as they take me captive: do you not know that I am the son of the horseman of Zahdam?)
and the other's saying:
286 - 1- حتى إذا يَئِسَ الرُّماةُ وأَرْسَلوا ... غُضْفاً دواجنَ قافِلاً أعْصامُها
(Until, when the archers knew [or: despaired], and they loosed droop-eared, trained hounds with dried-up collars …)
Al-Farrāʾ rejected this and said: "I have not heard «يَئِسْتُ» meaning «عَلِمْتُ»." He was answered that whoever has preserved [a usage] is a proof against whoever has not. What indicates that is the reading of ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, Ibn Abī Mulayka, al-Jaḥdarī, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and his son Zayd, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Ibn Yazīd al-Madīnī, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd and ʿAlī ibn Badhīma: «أو لم يتبيَّنْ», from «تبيَّنْتُ كذا» when you come to know it. And whoever said: "The scribe only wrote it while drowsy, its original being «أفلم يتبيَّن», and he levelled these letters so that they were taken to be a sīn", has fabricated a lie.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This and the like of it is something not to be believed about a book — [the Book of Allah, which falsehood cannot approach] from [before] it or from behind it. How could this be hidden so that it remained between the two covers of the Imām [codex], when it was passing through the hands of those eminent men, careful in the religion of Allah and watchful over it, who did not neglect its major points or its minute ones — especially the canon to which reference is made and the rule on which everything is built? By Allah, this is a fabrication in which there is no doubt." Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It is said: «اليأس» was used in the meaning of knowledge only because the one who despairs of a thing knows that it will not happen, just as «الرجاء» (hope) was used in the meaning of fear, of forgetting and of leaving, because it implies that."
Two views are possible regarding «أَنْ». The first: it is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the counterfactual clause after it being its khabar (predicate), the separation having occurred through «لو». And «أنْ» with what falls within its scope, if we attach it to «آمنوا», is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, according to the disagreement between al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, since its origin is the genitive by the preposition, i.e. "they believed that if Allah willed"; and if we attach it to «يَيْئَس» in the sense of «عَلِمَ», it is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects.
The second: it is a link between the oath and what is sworn upon, as preceded.
His saying: {أَوْ تَحُلُّ}: its fāʿil (agent) may be the pronoun of the second person, [i.e.] "or you, O Muḥammad, alight"; or it may be the pronoun of «القارعة», and this is clearer, i.e. a striking calamity befalls them, or the calamity alights.
Ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid read «يَحُلُّ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, the fāʿil being, as preceded, either the pronoun of «القارعة» — the verb being made masculine only because it means "the punishment", or because the tāʾ is for intensiveness and what is meant is «قارِع» — or the pronoun of the Messenger, brought in the third person. They also read «مِنْ ديارهم», and it is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (المر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (١))
His saying, Exalted is He: (المر): its ruling has been mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara.
(تِلْكَ): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ» its khabar (predicate); or it may be the khabar of (المر), with «آيَاتُ» a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition).
(وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is in the position of the nominative (as a mubtadaʾ), and «الْحَقُّ» is its khabar.
It may also be that the khabar is «مِنْ رَبِّكَ», and «الْحَقُّ» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or it is a khabar after a khabar, or the two together are a single khabar. If «الْحَقِّ» had been read in the genitive, it would have been permissible, as an adjective (ṣifa) of «رَبِّكَ». The second view: that «وَالَّذِي» is an adjective of «الْكِتَابِ», the wāw having been brought into the adjective as it was brought in with «التَّائِبِينَ» and «الطَّيِّبِينَ».
And (الْحَقُّ), in the nominative, is on this view the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ يُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّكُمْ تُوقِنُونَ (٢))
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its implied form being "free of pillars".
And al-ʿamad, with fatḥa, is the plural of ʿimād or ʿamūd ("pillar"), like أَدِيمٌ and أَدَمٌ, أَفِيقٌ and أَفَقٌ, إِهَابٌ and أَهَبٌ; and there is no fifth to them.
It is also read with two ḍammas (عُمُدٍ), and it is like كِتَابٌ and كُتُبٌ, رَسُولٌ and رُسُلٌ.
(تَرَوْنَهَا): the object pronoun refers back to the pillars; so «تَرَوْنَهَا» is in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa).
It may also refer back to the heavens; it is then a ḥāl from them.
(يُدَبِّرُ) and (يُفَصِّلُ): both are read with yāʾ and with nūn; their meaning is clear, and they are both resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
It may also be that the first is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «سَخَّرَ», and the second a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يُدَبِّرُ».

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنْهَارًا وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٣))
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ): there are three views on it:
The first: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the second «جَعَلَ», the implied form being "and He made in it two of a pair from all the fruits". The second: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اثْنَيْنِ», being originally an adjective (ṣifa) of it. The third: that it is attached to the first «جَعَلَ», and the second «جَعَلَ» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ): it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun of the name of Allah in whichever of the verbs before it this is valid for, namely: رَفَعَ, سَخَّرَ, يُدَبِّرُ, يُفَصِّلُ, مَدَّ and جَعَلَ.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجَاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ يُسْقَى بِمَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَى بَعْضٍ فِي الْأُكُلِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ): the majority read it with the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ (subject) or as the agent (fāʿil) of the adverbial phrase. Al-Ḥasan read «قِطَعًا مُتَجَاوِرَاتٍ», on the implied form "and He made in the earth…".
And (وَجَنَّاتٌ) is likewise, according to the difference (of readings). None of them read «وَزَرْعًا» in the accusative; but some people read it in the nominative, conjoined to «قِطَعٌ», and likewise what follows it; and others read it in the genitive, conjoined to «أَعْنَابٍ». Some people declared this reading weak, because crops are not part of gardens.
Others said: there may be crops in a garden, but between the palms and the vines. It is also said: the implied form is "and plants of crops", so it was conjoined according to the meaning.
And al-ṣinwān is the plural of ṣinw, like قِنْوٌ and قِنْوَانٌ; its plural of paucity is أَصْنَاءٌ. There are two dialectal forms of it: kasra on the ṣād and ḍamma on it, and it has been read with both.
(تُسْقَى): the majority read it with tāʾ, the feminine being for the preceding plural. It is also read with yāʾ (يُسْقَى), i.e. "that is watered".
(نُفَضِّلُ): it is read with nūn and with yāʾ, naming the agent (active); and with yāʾ and fatḥa on the ḍād (يُفَضَّلُ), with «بَعْضُهَا» in the nominative; and that is clear.
(فِي الْأُكُلِ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of «نُفَضِّلُ»; or it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بَعْضَهَا», i.e. "We prefer some of them as something eaten", or "with eating in it".

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ أَئِذَا كُنَّا تُرَابًا أَئِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (٥))
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ): «قَوْلُهُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «عَجَبٌ» is a fronted khabar (predicate).
It is also said: «الْعَجَبُ» here means "something astonishing"; on this view «قَوْلُهُمْ» may be nominative by it (as its agent).
(أَئِذَا كُنَّا): the whole statement is in the position of the accusative by «قَوْلُهُمْ». What governs «إِذَا» is a verb that the speech points to, its implied form being "when we are dust, shall we be resurrected?"; and His saying (لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ) points to it. It may not be accusative by «كُنَّا», because «إِذَا» is in a genitive construct with it; nor by «جَدِيدٍ», because what comes after «إِنَّ» does not govern what comes before it.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلَاتُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ»; or it may be an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السَّيِّئَةِ».
And (الْمَثُلَاتُ) is with fatḥa on the mīm and ḍamma on the thāʾ; its singular is likewise (مَثُلَةٌ).
It is read with sukūn on the tāʾ (الْمَثْلَاتُ); there are two explanations of it. The first: that it is lightened from the plural with ḍamma, fleeing the heaviness of the ḍamma together with the succession of vowels. The second: that the singular was lightened and then the plural was formed on that.
[Translator's note: "the tāʾ" is as written in the source; the letter concerned is the thāʾ.]
It is also read with two ḍammas (الْمُثُلَاتُ), and with ḍamma on the first and sukūn on the second (الْمُثْلَاتُ); ḍamma on the mīm is a dialectal form of it. As for ḍamma on the thāʾ, it may be a dialectal form in the singular, or it may be vowel harmony (itbāʿ) in the plural; and as for sukūn on it, it is according to the two views.
(عَلَى ظُلْمِهِمْ): a ḥāl from «النَّاسِ», and what governs it is «مَغْفِرَةٍ».
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلَاتُ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَى ظُلْمِهِمْ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (٧)).
[Translator's note: the source repeats the text of verse 6 here under the number (٧); the comment that follows concerns verse 7: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ.]
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ): there are three views on it. The first: that it is a resumptive clause (jumla mustaʾnafa), i.e. "and for every people there is a guiding prophet". The second: that the mubtadaʾ is omitted, its implied form being "and He is, for every people, a guide". The third: its implied form is "you are only a warner, and a guide for every people"; in this there is a separation between the conjunction and the maʿṭūf (conjoined), and they have cited a fair amount of it.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثَى وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدَارٍ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا تَحْمِلُ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it means «الَّذِي» ("that which"), and its position is accusative by «يَعْلَمُ».
The second: it is interrogative; it is then accusative by «تَحْمِلُ», and the clause is in the position of the accusative.
And likewise: «وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ».
(وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدَارٍ): «عِنْدَهُ» may be in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of «شَيْءٍ», or in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «كُلُّ»; what governs it on both views is omitted; and the khabar (predicate) of «كُلُّ» is «بِمِقْدَارٍ».
It may also be an adjective of «مِقْدَارٍ», or an adverb (ẓarf) of what the preposition (in «بِمِقْدَارٍ») is attached to.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "He is".
It may also be a mubtadaʾ, with «الْكَبِيرُ» its khabar.
The better practice is to pause on «الْمُتَعَالِ» without yāʾ, because it is the end of a verse; were it not for that, the better practice would be to keep it.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوءًا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَالٍ (١١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ): its singular is «مُعَقِّبَةٌ», the hāʾ in it being for intensiveness, like «نَسَّابَةٌ» ("a great genealogist"), i.e. "an angel who follows in succession".
It is also said: «مُعَقِّبَةٌ» is an adjective of a group, and then it was put in the plural on that basis.
(مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ): it may be an adjective (ṣifa) of «مُعَقِّبَاتٌ»; or an adverb (ẓarf); or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun that is in it; on this view the speech is complete at it.
It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَحْفَظُونَهُ», i.e. "followers who guard him from before him and from behind him".
And «يَحْفَظُونَهُ» may be an adjective of «مُعَقِّبَاتٌ», or a ḥāl from what the adverbial phrase is attached to.
(مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ): i.e. from the jinn and mankind; so «مِنْ» has its usual meaning. It is also said: «مِنْ» means the bāʾ, i.e. "by the command of Allah". It is also said: it means «عَنْ».
(وَإِذَا أَرَادَ): what governs «إِذَا» is what the answer points to, i.e. "it is not repelled", or "it befalls".
(مِنْ وَالٍ): it is read with imāla (inclining the vowel towards i) because of the kasra; and there is no impediment here.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحَابَ الثِّقَالَ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
And (السَّحَابَ الثِّقَالَ) has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّوَاعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِهَا مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ الْمِحَالِ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ): it is said: it is an angel; on this view it has been named with the maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said: thunder is its voice; the implied form on this view is "the possessor of the thunder" or "the thunderer".
And (بِحَمْدِهِ) has been mentioned in al-Baqara in the story of Ādam, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.
And (الْمِحَالِ) is of the pattern fiʿāl from al-maḥl, which is strength; one says مَحَلَ بِهِ when he overpowered him. There is another dialectal form of it: with fatḥa on the mīm.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الْحَقِّ وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ إِلَّا كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى الْمَاءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ وَمَا دُعَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ): there are two opinions on it. The first: it is an allusion to the idols, i.e. "and the idols, which call the polytheists to worship them, «لَا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُمْ بِشَيْءٍ»"; He gave them the plural of rational beings according to their belief about them. The second: that they are the polytheists, the implied form being "and the polytheists who call upon the idols besides Allah — they (the idols) do not respond to them", i.e. do not answer them; that is, the idols do not answer them with anything.
(إِلَّا كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ): the implied form is "except a response like the response to one who stretches out his palms". The maṣdar (verbal noun) in this implied form is in a genitive construct with its object, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَسْأَمُ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ دُعَاءِ الْخَيْرِ). The agent of this maṣdar is implied (muḍmar), and it is the pronoun of the water, i.e. "they do not answer them except as the water answers one who stretches out his palms to it"; and the answering here is an allusion to compliance.
As for His saying, Exalted is He: (لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ), the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «بَاسِطِ», and the agent is the pronoun of the water, i.e. "so that the water may reach his mouth".
And (مَا هُوَ): i.e. the water. It may not be the pronoun of the one stretching out, with the agent of «بَالِغ» implied, because when an active participle is predicated of someone other than the one to whom it belongs, the agent must be made overt; on this view it would have been necessary to say "وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ الْمَاءَ". But if you make the hāʾ in «بَالِغِهِ» the pronoun of the water, then «هُوَ» may be the pronoun of the one stretching out.
As for the kāf in «كَبَاسِطِ»: if you make it a particle, there is in it (in what it attaches to) a pronoun referring back to the omitted thing qualified; and if you make it a noun, there is no pronoun in it.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَظِلَالُهُمْ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ (١٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (ظِلَالُهُمْ) is conjoined to «مَنْ».
And (بِالْغُدُوِّ) is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَسْجُدُ».

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قُلْ مَنْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَى وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي):
it is read with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and its parallels have preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا فَاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَدًا رَابِيًا وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغَاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَاعٍ زَبَدٌ مِثْلُهُ كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ وَالْبَاطِلَ فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَاءً وَأَمَّا مَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوْدِيَةٌ): it is the plural of وَادٍ ("valley"); the plural of fāʿil on the pattern afʿila is irregular (shādhdh), and we have not heard it in any word other than this one. Its explanation is that fāʿil has come with the meaning of faʿīl; and just as faʿīl has come with (a plural) afʿila, as in جَرِيبٌ and أَجْرِبَةٌ, so has fāʿil.
(بِقَدَرِهَا): an adjective (ṣifa) of «أَوْدِيَةٌ».
(وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ): with yāʾ and with tāʾ.
(عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُوقِدُونَ».
And (ابْتِغَاءَ) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).
(أَوْ مَتَاعٍ): conjoined to «حِلْيَةٍ»; «زَبَدٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مِثْلُهُ» is an adjective of it, and the khabar (predicate) is «مِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ».
The meaning is: "and among the minerals of the earth, such as copper, there is that which has a scum — namely its dross — like it", i.e. like the foam that is on the water.
And (جُفَاءً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); its hamza is converted from a wāw. It is also said: it is original.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنَى وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُ لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لَافْتَدَوْا بِهِ أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْحِسَابِ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ (١٨)).
(لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا): resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and it is the khabar (predicate) of «الْحُسْنَى».

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَنْقُضُونَ الْمِيثَاقَ (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ): it may be accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» ("I mean").

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا وَمَنْ صَلَحَ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ بَابٍ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ): it is a badal (substitute) from «عُقْبَى»; it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «يَدْخُلُونَهَا» the khabar (predicate).
And (وَمَنْ صَلَحَ) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the agent pronoun; this was allowed even though it was not emphasised, because the object pronoun has become a separator like the emphasis (tawkīd).
It may also be accusative with the meaning of «مَعَ» ("with").

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَلَامٌ): i.e. "they say: peace".
(بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ): the bāʾ may not be attached to «سَلَامٌ», because of the separation by the khabar (predicate) that this would involve; it is attached only to «عَلَيْكُمْ», or to what that is attached to.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَاعٌ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ): the implied form is "in comparison with the Hereafter".
It may not be an adverb (ẓarf), either of «الْحَيَاةُ» or of «الدُّنْيَا», because they do not occur in the Hereafter; rather it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the implied form is "and the near life, being set beside the Hereafter, is not…".

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ): it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "tranquillity by it", i.e. tranquillity comes about for them through the remembrance of Allah.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْقُلُوبُ», i.e. "they are at rest, with the remembrance of Allah in them".

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ طُوبَى لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); and (طُوبَى لَهُمْ) is a second mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), in the position of the khabar of the first.
It may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who believed"; then «طُوبَى لَهُمْ» is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), and what governs it is «آمَنُوا» and «عَمِلُوا».
It may also be that «الَّذِينَ» is a badal (substitute) from (مَنْ أَنَابَ), or (accusative) by an implied «أَعْنِي» ("I mean").
It may also be that «طُوبَى» is in the position of the accusative, on the implied form "He made (جَعَلَ)…".
Its wāw is a replacement for a yāʾ, because it is from al-ṭīb ("goodness"); it was replaced by a wāw because of the ḍamma before it.
And (حُسْنُ مَآبٍ): the majority read it with ḍamma on the nūn and the genitive construct; it is conjoined to «طُوبَى» if you make it a mubtadaʾ.
It was also read with fatḥa on the nūn and the genitive construct (وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ); it is conjoined to «طُوبَى» on the view that it is accusative.
It is read irregularly with fatḥa on the nūn and the nominative of «مَآبٌ» (وَحُسْنَ مَآبٌ); «حَسُنَ» on this view is a verb, the ḍamma of whose sīn was transferred to the ḥāʾ; and this is permissible in faʿula when it is for praise or blame.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَلِكَ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ فِي أُمَّةٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهَا أُمَمٌ لِتَتْلُوَ عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِالرَّحْمَنِ قُلْ هُوَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ مَتَابِ (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ): the implied form is "the matter is as We have informed you".

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآنًا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتَى بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعًا أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ لَوْ يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ لَهَدَى النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَلَا يَزَالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا تُصِيبُهُمْ بِمَا صَنَعُوا قَارِعَةٌ أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبًا مِنْ دَارِهِمْ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ وَعْدُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآنًا): the answer of «لَوْ» is omitted, i.e. "it would have been this Qurʾān".
Al-Farrāʾ said: its answer is placed before it, i.e. "and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful, even if there were a Qurʾān…", by way of hyperbole.
(أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتَى): the reason for dropping the tāʾ from this verb while keeping it in the two verbs before it is that «الْمَوْتَى» includes the real masculine, and gives it predominance (taghlīb); so dropping the tāʾ was better; while «الْجِبَالُ» and «الْأَرْضُ» are not like that.
(أَنْ لَوْ يَشَاءُ): in the position of the accusative by «يَيْأَسْ», because its meaning is "has it not become clear (to them) and do they not know?".
(أَوْ تَحُلُّ قَرِيبًا): the agent (fāʿil) of «تَحُلُّ» is the pronoun of «الْقَارِعَةُ». It is also said: it is for the second person, i.e. "or you, O Muḥammad, alight near them with the punishment"; then the position of the clause is accusative, conjoined to «تُصِيبُ».

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَائِمٌ عَلَى كُلِ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ بِظَاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بَلْ زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مَكْرُهُمْ وَصُدُّوا عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ): it is conjoined to «كَسَبَتْ», i.e. "and for their setting up partners". It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(وَصُدُّوا): it is read with fatḥa on the ṣād (وَصَدُّوا), i.e. "and they turned others away"; with ḍamma on it, i.e. "and Satan, or their partners, turned them away"; and with kasra on it (وَصِدُّوا), its original being صُدِدُوا with ḍamma on the first letter; the kasra of the dāl was transferred to the ṣād.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ أُكُلُهَا دَائِمٌ وَظِلُّهَا تِلْكَ عُقْبَى الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَعُقْبَى الْكَافِرِينَ النَّارُ (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "and among what is recited to you is the description of the Garden". On this view (تَجْرِي) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) in «وُعِدَ», i.e. "they were promised it, the flowing of its rivers being foreordained".
Al-Farrāʾ said: the khabar is «تَجْرِي». According to the Basrans this is an error, because rivers do not flow beneath the description; that is only an attribute of the muḍāf ilayhi. His (al-Farrāʾ's) ground is that «الْمَثَلُ» here means "the description", so it is like your saying "Zayd's description is that he is tall".
It may also be that «تَجْرِي» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(أُكُلُهَا دَائِمٌ): it is like (تَجْرِي) on the two views.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا وَاللَّهُ يَحْكُمُ لَا مُعَقِّبَ لِحُكْمِهِ وَهُوَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَنْقُصُهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun, or from «الْأَرْضَ».

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعًا يَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ لِمَنْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ): it is read in the singular (الْكَافِرُ), it being a generic noun (jins), and in the plural, according to the original.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَسْتَ مُرْسَلًا قُلْ كَفَى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ (٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ): it is read with fatḥa on the mīm; it means «الَّذِي» ("the one who"), and concerning its position there are two views. The first: it is nominative, following the position of the name of Allah, i.e. "Allah suffices, and the one who has… suffices". The second: it is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the wording of the name of Allah the Exalted. On this view «عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ» is nominative by the adverbial phrase, because it relies on (something before it) by being a ṣila (relative clause).
It may also be a khabar (predicate), the mubtadaʾ (subject) being «عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ».
It is also read «وَمِنْ عِنْدِهِ», with kasra on the mīm, as a particle (preposition); on this view «عِلْمُ الْكِتَابِ» is a mubtadaʾ, or the agent (fāʿil) of the adverbial phrase.
It is also read «عُلِمَ الْكِتَابُ», as a verb whose agent is not named (passive), and it is what governs «مِنْ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Raʿd
Medinan
﷽
﴿المر﴾: we have explained in Sūrat al-Baqara what has been said about this and its like. It is related that its meaning is: ”أنا اللَّهُ أرى“ ("I am Allah; I see"), and it is related: ”أنا اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ وأرى“ ("I am Allah; I know and I see"), and it is related that ”الـمـر“ are letters indicating the name of the Lord, majestic is His majesty.
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that what was revealed before the Qur'an is "the verses of the Book". ﴿والَّذِي أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ الحَقُّ﴾, i.e. and the Qur'an sent down to you is the truth. It is permissible that the position of ”اَلَّذِي“ be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is permissible that it be nominative by conjunction with ”آياتُ“, in which case ”اَلْحَقُّ“ is nominative on an implied ”هُوَ“.
And it is permissible that the position of ”اَلَّذِي“ be genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to ”اَلْكِتابِ“, the meaning being: ”تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ وآياتُ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إلَيْكَ“ ("those are the verses of the Book and the verses of that which was sent down to you"); and ”اَلَّذِي أُنْزِلُ“ [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source] may be a naʿt (adjective) of ”اَلْكِتابِ“ even though the wāw has come, with ”اَلْحَقُّ“ nominative by implication [of a pronoun]. And it is permissible that ”اَلْحَقُّ“ be an adjective of ”اَلَّذِي“, the meaning being: ”تِلْكَ آياتُ الكِتابِ والَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إلَيْكَ مِن رَبِّكَ الحَقُّ“ [Translator's note: i.e. with الحقِّ in the genitive as adjective of the genitive الذي]; but I know of no one who read it that way.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها﴾: when He mentioned that they do not believe, He made known the proof that necessitates affirming the Creator, Mighty and Majestic is He, and said: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ﴾. In this there is such power and such indication that nothing is clearer than it: that the sky encompasses the earth, standing clear of it, without pillars. The meaning is "without pillars, and you see it thus".
And it is permissible that ”تَرَوْنَها“ be a naʿt (adjective) of the pillars, the meaning being: "without visible pillars"; on this view, what props it up is the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ والقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لأجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾: everything that is subdued and directed, possessing nothing for itself to free it from the subjugation — that is the meaning of al-sukhra (subjection). So the sun and the moon are subjected, running their courses along which they were subjected to run.
﴿يُدَبِّرُ الأمْرَ﴾: He makes it firm. ﴿يُفَصِّلُ الآياتِ لَعَلَّكم بِلِقاءِ رَبِّكم تُوقِنُونَ﴾, i.e. He makes clear the signs that point to His power to resurrect you, so that you may be certain; for they used to deny the resurrection, so they were informed that He who created the heavens, and brought man into being when he had been nothing, is able to bring him back.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الأرْضَ﴾: after making clear the signs of the sky, He directed them to the signs of the earth, and said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الأرْضَ﴾. It is related in the exegesis that it was round and then was stretched out; its meaning is "He spread out the earth", and placed in it rawāsī, i.e. firm mountains. One says: ”قَدْ رَسا الشَّيْءُ، يَرْسُو، رُسُوًّا، فَهو راسٍ“ when something is firm. ﴿وَأنْهارًا ومِن كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ جَعَلَ فِيها زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾: He placed in it two kinds; and ”اَلزَّوْجُ“ is the single one that has no partner [Translator's note: so in the source]. ﴿يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ﴾, and it is also read: ”يَغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهارَ“. Then He made known that in these things mentioned there is proof and clear signs, and said: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾

zajjaj:4-4.t:
Then He added to their proof, and said: ﴿وَفِي الأرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ﴾. It is related in the exegesis that they adjoin one another, some of them cultivated and some not cultivated; and likewise in the exegesis its meaning is: ”قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ“ ("neighbouring tracts"). ﴿وَجَنّاتٌ مِن أعْنابٍ﴾: the best is the nominative ”جَنّاتٌ“, the meaning being: "and in the earth are neighbouring tracts, and between them gardens".
The accusative ”جَنّاتٍ“ is also permissible, and it is read ”وَجَنّاتٍ مِن أعْنابٍ“, the meaning being: "He placed in it firm mountains, and placed in it gardens of grapes". And it is permissible that ”وَجَنّاتٍ“ be genitive (khafḍ), co-ordinated (nasaq) with ”كُلِّ“, the meaning being: "and of every fruit He placed in it two pairs, and of gardens of grapes". ﴿وَزَرْعٌ﴾: as for ”وَزَرْعٌ“, both the nominative and the genitive are permissible in it, and likewise ﴿صِنْوانٌ وغَيْرُ صِنْوانٍ﴾. ”اَلصِّنْوانُ“ is the plural of ”صِنْوٌ“ and ”صُنْوٌ“; and the meaning of ”اَلصِّنْوانُ“ is that the root is one, and from it grow two palm trees, three, or more.
In the plural of ”صِنْوٌ“, ”أصْناءٌ“ is also permissible, like ”عِدْلٌ“ and ”أعْدالٌ“, and likewise ”صُنْوٌ“; and when they are many, it is ”اَلصُّنِيُّ“ and ”اَلصِّنِيُّ“. ﴿يُسْقى بِماءٍ واحِدٍ﴾: ”تُسْقى“, with tāʾ, is also permissible. ﴿بِماءٍ واحِدٍ ونُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها عَلى بَعْضٍ في الأُكُلِ﴾: ”اَلْأُكُلُ“ is the fruit that is eaten.
And ”وَيُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها عَلى بَعْضٍ“ is also permissible, because mention of Allah has preceded, so the meaning is "Allah prefers"; and likewise when one says ”وَنُفَضِّلُ“ with nūn, because the report about Allah is in the plural form, as He said: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي ونُمِيتُ﴾ [Qāf: 43]. The Arabs were addressed in this way because they use the plural form for those whom they honour.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾: this is an address to the Prophet, upon him be peace. ﴿أإذا كُنّا تُرابًا أإنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, i.e. this is a place for wonder, because they denied the resurrection, while He had shown them, from the greatness of the creation of the heavens and the earth, what indicates that the resurrection is easier for [divine] power than what they had already perceived. As for the analysis of ”أئِذا كُنّا تُرابًا أئِنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“: the position of ”إذا“ is accusative. Whoever reads ”أئِذا كُنّا تُرابًا“ in the form of a question, and then reads ”أئِنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“, ”إذا“ is accusative by the sense of "we will be resurrected, and our creation will be renewed"; the meaning is: "when we are dust, shall we be resurrected?" — and ”أئِنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ؟“ indicates what they intended.
And whoever reads ”أئِذا كُنّا تُرابًا إنّا لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ“ brings the interrogative alif onto the whole statement, and ”إذا“ is accusative by ”كُنّا“; but the statement is then in the sense of condition and requital (al-sharṭ wa-l-jazāʾ). It is not permissible for ”جَدِيدٍ“ to govern ”إذا“, because what comes after ”إذا“ does not govern what precedes it [Translator's note: presumably meant: what follows إنّ does not govern what precedes it; translated as written]; there is no disagreement among the grammarians that what comes after ”إنْ“ and ”إذا“ does not govern what precedes them.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that whoever asks about this by way of denial after the clarification and the proof is a disbeliever, and said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وأُولَئِكَ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ﴾. It has come in the exegesis that ”اَلْأغْلالَ“ ("the shackles") are the deeds, on their necks on the Day of Resurrection.
And the proof of that in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿إذِ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ والسَّلاسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 71] ﴿فِي الحَمِيمِ﴾ [Ghāfir: 72]. It has also been said that ”أُولَئِكَ الأغْلالُ في أعْناقِهِمْ“ means the shackles which are the deeds, and these too lead to the shackles being on their necks on the Day of Resurrection; for your saying to a man about an evil deed, ”هَذا غُلٌّ في عُنُقِكَ“ ("this is a shackle on your neck"), means that it clings to you and that you will be requited for it with punishment on the Day of Resurrection.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الحَسَنَةِ﴾, i.e. they seek the punishment by their saying: ﴿فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]. ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ المَثُلاتُ﴾: ”اَلْمُثُلاتُ“ is with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the mīm. Whoever reads ”اَلْمُثُلاتُ“, it is the plural of ”مُثْلَةٌ“; and whoever reads ”اَلْمَثُلاتُ“, it is the plural of ”مَثُلَةٌ“. In ”اَلْمَثُلاتُ“ three forms are permissible: one may say ”وَقَدْ خَلَتْ اَلْمُثْلاتُ“ with sukūn on the thāʾ; fatḥa on the thāʾ is permissible: ”اَلْمُثَلاتُ“; and whoever reads ”اَلْمُثُلاتُ“ puts ḍamma on both the thāʾ and the mīm — it is quiescent in the singular and has ḍamma in the plural, and this ḍamma is a compensation for the dropping of the feminine tāʾ; and whoever gives fatḥa does so because fatḥa is the lightest of the vowels. The transmitters related:
؎وَلَمّا رَأوْنا بادِيًا رُكُباتُنا عَلى مَوْطِنٍ لا نَخْلِطُ الجِدَّ بِالهَزْلِ
(When they saw us, our knees showing, in a place where we do not mix earnest with jest.)
And whoever reads ”اَلْمُثْلاتُ“ with sukūn on the thāʾ does so because in everything with ḍamma or kasra, such as ”رُسُلٌ“, ”عَضُدٌ“ and ”فَخِذٌ“, making it quiescent is permissible because of the heaviness of the ḍamma and kasra. The meaning is that they are hastening the punishment, while there has already preceded punishment that was an exemplary chastisement (muthla), and in which there was a deterrent lesson for them, had they taken heed.

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾: its meaning is: "why has there not been sent down to him?" They only sought signs other than those the Prophet ﷺ brought, such as the splitting of the moon, and the Qur'an, of which they were challenged to bring a sūra like it, and things of this kind; they sought signs like those of ʿĪsā and Mūsā. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that every people has a guide, and said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إنَّما أنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ ولِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هادٍ﴾, i.e. a prophet and a caller to Allah who calls them with the signs he is given, not with what they want and dictate.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿وَما تَغِيضُ الأرْحامُ وما تَزْدادُ﴾: the meaning of ”غاضَ“ in the language is "decreased". In the exegesis: what pregnancy falls short of nine months, and what exceeds the nine. And it has been said: what falls short of completion so that it dies, and what increases until the pregnancy is complete.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
And His saying: ﴿سَواءٌ مِنكم مَن أسَرَّ القَوْلَ ومَن جَهَرَ بِهِ﴾: the position of ”مَن“ is nominative by ”سَواءٌ“, and likewise the second ”مَن“; both are nominative by ”سَواءٌ“, because ”سَواءٌ“ requires two. You say: ”سَواءٌ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“ in the sense of ”ذَوا سَواءٍ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“ ("Zayd and ʿAmr are possessors of equality"), because ”سَواءٌ“ is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so what follows it cannot be nominative except by ellipsis. You say: ”عَدْلٌ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“, and the meaning is ”ذَوا عَدْلٍ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“, because verbal nouns are not active participles; it is nouns that put their attributes in the nominative, and when verbal nouns do so, it is by ellipsis, as al-Khansāʾ said:
؎تَرْتَعُ ما غَفَلَتْ حَتّى إذا ادَّكَرَتْ فَإنَّما هي إقْبالٌ وإدْبارُ
(She grazes as long as she forgets, until when she remembers, she is all coming and going.)
The meaning is: she is one of coming and one of going; and likewise ”زَيْدٌ إقْبالٌ وإدْبارٌ“. This — I mean ”سَواءٌ“ — is among what is used very frequently, so it has been treated like active participles. It is also permissible for it to be nominative as standing in the place of ”مُسْتَوٍ“ ("equal").
However, Sībawayh considers that ugly and does not allow ”مُسْتَوٍ زَيْدٌ وعَمْرٌو“, because in his view active participles, when indefinite, are not used as mubtadaʾ (subject), owing to their being weaker than the verb; so they are not used to begin a sentence, and he treats them like the verb. The meaning of the verse is to inform them that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, knows what is hidden from them and what is witnessed. So He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن هو مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ﴾, i.e. whoever is concealed by night — and the night conceals more than the day — ﴿وَسارِبٌ بِالنَّهارِ﴾, i.e. whoever is out in the open by day on his way (sarab). One says: ”خَلِّ لَهُ سَرَبَهُ“, i.e. his way.
So the meaning is: "the one out in the open in the roads, the one hiding in the darkness, the one who speaks aloud and the one who conceals in himself — Allah's knowledge of them all is equal". Quṭrub mentioned another interpretation: he mentioned that ”مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ“ may mean "appearing by night" — this is permissible in the language — and with this ”وَسارِبٌ بِالنَّهارِ“ would mean "concealed"; one says ”اِنْسَرَبَ الوَحْشِيُّ“ when the wild animal enters its lair. The first is clear, and it is more eloquent in describing knowledge of the unseen.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ومِن خَلْفِهِ﴾, i.e. a human being has angels who succeed one another, some coming after others. ﴿يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾: the meaning is their guarding him is by Allah's command, i.e. by what Allah the Exalted has commanded them, not that they are able to repel Allah's command, as you would say: "they guard him from Allah's command" [Translator's note: the source reads ”يَحْفَظُونَهُ عَنْ أمْرِ اللَّهِ“; the sense of «كما تقول» here is unclear and is translated as written].
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما لَهم مِن دُونِهِ مِن والٍ﴾, i.e. no one besides Allah takes charge of their affairs.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ البَرْقَ خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا﴾: fear for the traveller, because in rain there is fear for the traveller, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إنْ كانَ بِكم أذًى مِن مَطَرٍ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 102]; and hope for the settled person, because he benefits from the rain. And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that ”خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا“ means fear for whoever fears the harm of rain, since not every land benefits from rain, such as Egypt and the like, and hope for whoever hopes to benefit from it.
﴿وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحابَ الثِّقالَ﴾, i.e. those that have become heavy with water.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
﴿وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that it is an angel who drives the clouds. It is also possible that the sound of thunder is its glorification, because the sound of thunder is among the mightiest of things, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has said: ﴿وَإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 44]; thunder was singled out for mention because of the greatness of its sound — and Allah knows best. ﴿وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّواعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِها مَن يَشاءُ وهم يُجادِلُونَ في اللَّهِ﴾: it is possible that the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), so the meaning would be: "and He strikes with them whom He wills while he is disputing about Allah". That is because it came in the exegesis «that a man of the Jāhiliyya called ”أرْبَدُ“ (Arbad) asked the Prophet ﷺ, saying: Tell me about our Lord — is He of copper or of iron? So Allah sent a thunderbolt down upon him and it killed him».
On this basis the wāw may be the wāw of ḥāl. It is also possible that, when Allah had completed the descriptions of what points to His oneness and His power to resurrect, He said after that: ﴿وَهم يُجادِلُونَ في اللَّهِ وهو شَدِيدُ المِحالِ﴾, i.e. severe in power and in punishment. One says in the language: ”ماحَلْتُهُ مِحالًا“ when you contend in strength with him until it becomes clear to him which of you is stronger; and ”اَلْمَحْلُ“ in the language is strength. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الحَقِّ والَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهم بِشَيْءٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that ”دَعْوَةُ الحَقِّ“ ("the call of truth") is "the testimony that there is no god but Allah". And it is possible — and Allah knows best — that ”دَعْوَةُ الحَقِّ“ means that whoever calls on Allah affirming His oneness has his supplication answered.
﴿والَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهم بِشَيْءٍ﴾: then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made clear how the idols respond, since they called on idols besides Allah, and said: ﴿إلا كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إلى الماءِ﴾ — except as the one who stretches out his palms towards water is answered: he calls the water to his mouth, and the water does not respond. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that their calling on the idols is like the thirsty man's calling the water to reach his mouth, ﴿وَما هو بِبالِغِهِ﴾. Some said: ﴿إلا كَباسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إلى الماءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فاهُ﴾ is like a man at the rim of a well calling the water from the bottom of the well to reach his mouth. The two explanations are one.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ طَوْعًا وكَرْهًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that the believer prostrates willingly and the disbeliever prostrates unwillingly.
